title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄序
聖天子秉籙御
天握樞臨極維茲四十有三年適
甲子更新之候實文明昌熾
之期也歲當大比士於鄉
上命左諭德〔臣鏜〕往主應天試事
秋七月丙午
===
陛辭就道乃八月乙亥達府治
丙子遂入鎖院百執事罔不
祗飭同考則郎中〔臣國珍臣軒〕
署郎中〔臣應峯臣鏡臣啓原〕署員
外郎〔臣三益〕主事〔臣焯〕教授
宗慶教諭〔臣紀臣弘道臣守約〕舊凡
兩京分校之役率領諸學官以
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄序

聖天子秉籙御天，握樞臨極，維茲四十有三年，適甲子更新之候，實文明昌熾之期也。歲當大比士於鄉，上命左諭德〔臣鏜〕往主應天試事。秋七月丙午，陛辭就道，乃八月乙亥達府治。丙子，遂入鎖院，百執事罔不祗飭。同考則郎中〔臣國珍臣軒〕、署郎中〔臣應峯臣鏡臣啓原〕、署員外郎〔臣三益〕、主事〔臣焯〕、教授宗慶、教諭〔臣紀臣弘道臣守約〕。舊凡兩京分校之役，率領諸學官以
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

The sagely Son of Heaven holds the mandate and rules by Heaven, grasps the pivot of government, and occupies the supreme throne. This forty-third year of his reign coincides with the renewal of the sixty-year cycle in a jiazi year: truly a time when literary culture flourishes brilliantly. As this was the year for the great triennial examination of scholars in the provinces, His Majesty commanded the Left Admonisher, your servant Tang, to go and preside over the Yingtian examination. On the bingwu day of the seventh month, in autumn, I took leave of His Majesty and set out, reaching the prefectural seat on the yihai day of the eighth month. On the bingzi day, we entered the examination compound and were sequestered there. Every official attending to the work was reverent and diligent.

The Associate Examiners were Bureau Directors, your servants Guozhen and Xuan; Acting Bureau Directors, your servants Yingfeng, Jing, and Qiyuan; Acting Vice Director, your servant Sanyi; Secretary, your servant Zhuo; Prefectural School Instructor Zongqing; and County School Instructors, your servants Ji, Hongdao, and Shouyue.

Previously, the work of assisting in the grading of examinations at the two capitals generally involved assembling the various educational officials, taking this as …

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
爲常項因臣下建議乃參置
省署之臣我
皇上加志賢科特
俞所請而櫽簡詳延法意益精密
矣維時提調則府尹臣自强府
丞臣嘉賓監試則御史臣潤臣
官伏念臣鏜經術淺薄行能
===
無異仰荷
皇上作養旋授史秩兩以職事分
校禮闈往叨
寵命署篆留院今春特
賜召還至是校士復蒙
任使之榮
渥恩殊遇無以爲報乃惟竭其心
punctuated:
爲常項。因臣下建議，乃參置省署之臣。我皇上加志賢科，特俞所請，而櫽簡詳延，法意益精密矣。維時，提調則府尹臣自强、府丞臣嘉賓，監試則御史臣潤、臣官。
伏念臣鏜，經術淺薄，行能無異，仰荷皇上作養，旋授史秩，兩以職事分校禮闈。往叨寵命，署篆留院；今春特賜召還。至是校士，復蒙任使之榮，渥恩殊遇，無以爲報，乃惟竭其心
translation_en:
…as the regular arrangement. Following a proposal by your servants, officials from the ministries were also appointed to serve alongside them. Our Emperor, giving particular attention to the examinations for selecting worthy men, specially approved the request. With screening and careful recruitment [?], the procedures and their intent became still more exacting. At this time, the Proctors were Prefect Ziqiang and Prefectural Vice Prefect Jiabin; the officials overseeing the examination were Censors Run and Guan.
I, your servant Tang, humbly reflect that my learning in the Classics is shallow, and my conduct and abilities unexceptional. Favored by the Emperor’s nurture, I was soon appointed to a historiographical post and twice served, as part of my official duties, as an examiner in the Metropolitan Examination. Previously, I was privileged to receive an imperial command to take temporary charge of the seal of the Hanlin Academy at the auxiliary capital. This spring, I was specially recalled. Now, in examining candidates, I have again received the honor of an imperial assignment. Having no means to repay such abundant grace and exceptional favor, I can only devote my whole heart…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
力得士焉以備他日之用庶
幾仰酬
鴻造於萬一於是矢心誓衆合提
學御史臣耿〔定向〕〔暨諸曹六館〕
所取士三千三百七十五人
三試之遵
制額登儁者一百三十有五人
===
弁録其文之優者以
獻臣鏜濫竽文柄當序諸首簡
惟
國家養士於學校而羅儁異於
科目士生今時苟有志於用
世雖皋夔稷契之賢舍此無
以自見然科目以文程士也
punctuated:
力，得士焉，以備他日之用，庶幾仰酬鴻造於萬一。於是矢心誓衆，合提學御史臣耿〔定向〕〔暨諸曹六館〕所取士三千三百七十五人，三試之。遵制額，登儁者一百三十有五人，弁録其文之優者以獻。臣鏜濫竽文柄，當序諸首簡。
惟國家養士於學校，而羅儁異於科目。士生今時，苟有志於用世，雖皋夔稷契之賢，舍此無以自見。然科目以文程士也。
translation_en:
…strength to select worthy men for service in days to come, hoping thereby to repay even a ten-thousandth part of Your Majesty’s great beneficence. Thus I pledged myself and administered an oath to all concerned. We assembled the 3,375 candidates selected by your servant Geng〔Dingxiang〕, the Censor Supervising Education, 〔together with the various bureaus and the Six Colleges [?]〕, and examined them in three sessions. Following the quota prescribed by imperial regulation, we advanced 135 outstanding men and compiled the best of their writings for presentation to Your Majesty. Your servant Tang, unworthily entrusted with authority over literary selection, is obliged to write a preface for the opening pages.
I reflect that the state nurtures scholars in its schools and gathers exceptional talent through the examinations. For a scholar born in the present age who aspires to serve the world, even one as worthy as Gao, Kui, Ji, or Xie has no means of making himself known apart from this route. Yet the examinations assess scholars through their writing.

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
諸士竭三日之力而欲盡攄
所蘊主司持一人之見而欲
槩其平生固亦難矣夫文根
於心而成於言者也取士以
文固欲因其言而究其心也
故有仁義之德者其言渾厚
典則也有中和之德者其言
===
雄深奧衍也有剛毅之德者
其言明白剴切也閎於中而
肆於外猶夫金藏於淵而川
媚玉產於石而山潤也反是
則神理不超之謂凡矣肉好
不匀之謂舛矣音律不諧之
謂乖矣是皆詭於道而匿其
punctuated: 諸士竭三日之力而欲盡攄所蘊，主司持一人之見而欲槩其平生，固亦難矣。夫文根於心而成於言者也，取士以文，固欲因其言而究其心也。故有仁義之德者，其言渾厚典則也；有中和之德者，其言雄深奧衍也；有剛毅之德者，其言明白剴切也。閎於中而肆於外，猶夫金藏於淵而川媚，玉產於石而山潤也。反是，則神理不超之謂凡矣，肉好不匀之謂舛矣，音律不諧之謂乖矣。是皆詭於道而匿其
translation_en: The candidates expend all their strength over three days, wishing to express fully all that they possess within; the chief examiner, relying on one person's judgment, wishes to assess their entire lives. This is indeed difficult. Writing is rooted in the heart and takes shape in words. Selecting men through writing is thus intended to probe their hearts through their words. Hence, those endowed with benevolence and righteousness write with richness, gravity, classical dignity, and due form; those endowed with equilibrium and harmony write with power, depth, profundity, and amplitude; those endowed with firmness and resolve write with clarity, directness, precision, and force. What is ample within spreads freely outward, just as gold concealed in the depths lends charm to a river, and jade formed within rock lends lustre to a mountain. Conversely, writing whose spirit and underlying principles fail to rise above the ordinary is called commonplace; writing whose solid and open portions are out of proportion—as in a jade disc—is called malformed; writing whose sounds and rhythms lack harmony is called discordant. All these depart from the Way and conceal their …

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
眞也諺曰玉巵無當雖寶非
用侈言無驗雖麗非經主司
執此以求之而實可稽已雖
然臣猶有懼也夫求金於沙
斂而揚之求玉於石剖而別
之然金玉至寶也其得之也
常難而沙與石則比比是也
===
臣恐金與沙而並收玉與石
而兼取也然此猶可言也若
棄其金而惟沙礫之是收棄
其玉而惟碔砆之是取人將
謂何臣之罪抑有甚焉臣竊
有大懼也於是祗率同事者
次第翻閱窮日夜罔懈已乃
punctuated: 眞也。諺曰：「玉巵無當，雖寶非用；侈言無驗，雖麗非經。」主司執此以求之，而實可稽已。雖然，臣猶有懼也。夫求金於沙，斂而揚之；求玉於石，剖而別之。然金玉至寶也，其得之也常難，而沙與石則比比是也。臣恐金與沙而並收，玉與石而兼取也。然此猶可言也。若棄其金而惟沙礫之是收，棄其玉而惟碔砆之是取，人將謂何？臣之罪抑有甚焉。臣竊有大懼也。於是祗率同事者，次第翻閱，窮日夜罔懈，已乃
translation_en: …their genuineness. A proverb says: “A jade goblet without a bottom, though precious, is of no use; extravagant words without substantiation, though beautiful, are no authoritative standard.” If those presiding over the examination apply this principle in their search, the substance can indeed be verified. Even so, your servant still has misgivings. To seek gold in sand, one gathers and winnows it; to seek jade in stone, one splits and separates it. Gold and jade are supremely precious, and finding them is always difficult, whereas sand and stone are everywhere. Your servant fears that gold and sand may be accepted together, and jade and stone taken alike. Yet even this would be something one could explain. But if we discarded the gold and gathered only sand and gravel, discarded the jade and took only stones resembling jade, what would people say? Your servant’s culpability would be greater still. Privately, your servant was deeply afraid. Accordingly, I respectfully led my colleagues in reading through the papers one by one, working tirelessly throughout the days and nights, and only then…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
得其文取盈其數而以額遺
者尚衆乃相顧喜曰始之懼
也庶可少釋乎旣而思之棆
卷嘆曰得無沙礫之混其眞
碔砆之疑於似者乎復取而
詳校之至再至三第見諸士
之文咸能咀嚼英華充飫道
===
德其典厚者不失之於凡瑣
其深奧者不失之於舛雜其
明切者不失之於乖忤若至
寶之陳於前使人心駭目眩
應接不暇文之美者粲然具
是矣於惟休哉臣因是以驗
人才之生恒孕毓於靈粹而
punctuated: 得其文，取盈其數，而以額遺者尚衆，乃相顧喜曰：「始之懼也，庶可少釋乎？」旣而思之，棆卷嘆曰：「得無沙礫之混其眞、碔砆之疑於似者乎？」復取而詳校之，至再至三。第見諸士之文，咸能咀嚼英華，充飫道德。其典厚者，不失之於凡瑣；其深奧者，不失之於舛雜；其明切者，不失之於乖忤。若至寶之陳於前，使人心駭目眩，應接不暇。文之美者，粲然具是矣。於惟休哉！臣因是以驗人才之生，恒孕毓於靈粹，而
translation_en: …we obtained their essays and selected enough to fill the quota, yet many remained excluded because of that limit. We then looked at one another with delight and said, “May our initial fears now be somewhat relieved?” On further reflection, however, I handled the examination scripts [?] and sighed: “Could sand and gravel have become mixed with the genuine treasures, or stones resembling jade have misled us by their likeness?” We took them up again and scrutinized them in detail, a second and a third time. We found that the candidates’ essays all savored the finest literary essence and were richly imbued with the Way and virtue. Those that were classically grounded and substantial did not lapse into banality or triviality; those that were profound did not lapse into error or confusion; those that were clear and pointed did not lapse into perversity or discord. It was as though supreme treasures had been arrayed before us, astonishing the heart and dazzling the eyes, too numerous to take in. All the beauties of literary composition were brilliantly present here. Ah, how splendid! From this your servant has thus seen that the birth of talented people is always nurtured by the numinous and pure essence of their surroundings, and…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
其成也則
道化之所漸濡
南畿爲我
聖祖定鼎之區山川磅礴風雨時
會才美之出宜非他比矧當
時
明良之盛相與賛謨𢫬治賡歌揖
===
讓於斯其遺風餘烈耿耿猶
在也諸士生長其地弁四方
所至游息其間有不聞風而
興起者乎我
皇上稟神聖之資總
君師之任
惇敘彜倫
punctuated:
其成也，則道化之所漸濡。
南畿爲我聖祖定鼎之區，山川磅礴，風雨時會，才美之出，宜非他比。矧當時明良之盛，相與賛謨𢫬治，賡歌揖讓於斯，其遺風餘烈耿耿猶在也。諸士生長其地，弁四方所至游息其間，有不聞風而興起者乎？
我皇上稟神聖之資，總君師之任，惇敘彜倫，
translation_en:
…their maturation, however, comes through gradual immersion in the transforming influence of the Way.
The Southern Metropolitan Region was where our Sagely Progenitor established his capital. Its mountains and rivers are majestic, and wind and rain converge in season; the outstanding talent it produces should surely be beyond comparison with other places. Moreover, in those days an enlightened sovereign and worthy ministers flourished together, assisting in deliberations and furthering good government [?], exchanging songs and observing ceremonial deference here. Their enduring influence and the legacy of their achievements remain vividly present. Among the scholars born and raised in this region, together with those arriving from all quarters [?] who study and dwell here, could any fail to be stirred to emulation upon hearing of that legacy?
Our Emperor, endowed with divine sagacity, bears the combined responsibilities of sovereign and teacher, fostering and ordering the constant human relationships…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
敷析箴訓所以
培植豐芑之仁
振育菁莪之化者益隆弗替士
之翔洽
淳風涵泳
膏澤而奮然有作者固宜斌斌
其盛如此也且
===
國初科目之行未有定制在昔
洪武甲子重議條格至於今
遵守不廢文明之運所由啓
矣今歲甲子我
皇上復加裁定乃正文體汰冗濫
革弊習嚴防範慎擇百執事
諸所厝畫秩然精當足以垂
punctuated: 敷析箴訓，所以培植豐芑之仁、振育菁莪之化者，益隆弗替。士之翔洽淳風、涵泳膏澤而奮然有作者，固宜斌斌其盛如此也。且國初科目之行，未有定制。在昔洪武甲子，重議條格，至於今遵守不廢，文明之運所由啓矣。今歲甲子，我皇上復加裁定，乃正文體，汰冗濫，革弊習，嚴防範，慎擇百執事，諸所厝畫，秩然精當，足以垂
translation_en:
…expounds admonitions and instructions. His benevolence in cultivating talent, like flourishing millet, and his transforming influence in fostering scholars, like luxuriant southernwood, grow ever greater without decline. Scholars move freely amid these wholesome customs and immerse themselves in this nourishing beneficence, rising with determination to accomplish something. It is surely fitting that their flourishing should display such abundant refinement.

Moreover, when the examination system was first implemented at the founding of the dynasty, its regulations were not yet fixed. In the jiazi year of the Hongwu reign (1384), its rules were reconsidered; these have been observed without interruption down to the present, thereby inaugurating an era of cultural brilliance. This year, again a jiazi year (1564), our Emperor has further revised and settled the regulations: correcting the style of examination writing, eliminating prolixity and indiscriminate excess, reforming corrupt practices, tightening safeguards, and carefully selecting all officials charged with these duties. All these arrangements are orderly, precise, and appropriate, sufficient to be handed down…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
諸夂遠則文運更新之會誠
與氣運相爲感通是以
德意所嚮莫不爭自淬礪期以無
負
明時而英賢輩出彪炳璀璨眞
足以敷賁典彝渙揚
國華者今諸士之卷具在可披
===
覽而得也然則
皇上夂道化成之效
壽考作人之功信有明徵而
太平之應不偶然矣諸士旣皐於
有司將展對
大廷敷布有位使能樹列勳庸
表著風節舉今日之所言者
punctuated:
諸夂遠，則文運更新之會，誠與氣運相爲感通。是以德意所嚮，莫不爭自淬礪，期以無負明時，而英賢輩出，彪炳璀璨，眞足以敷賁典彝、渙揚國華者。今諸士之卷具在，可披覽而得也。
然則皇上夂道化成之效，壽考作人之功，信有明徵，而太平之應不偶然矣。諸士旣皐於有司，將展對大廷，敷布有位，使能樹列勳庸，表著風節，舉今日之所言者……
translation_en:
…for ages to come [?], then this occasion of renewal in literary fortunes truly resonates with the larger course of cosmic fortune. Thus, wherever the imperial virtuous intent is directed, all compete to temper and sharpen themselves, hoping not to fail this enlightened age. Outstanding and worthy men emerge in succession, brilliant and resplendent, truly capable of adorning the established institutions and splendidly proclaiming the glory of the realm. The candidates’ papers are now all here; one may examine them and see this for oneself.
Thus there is indeed clear evidence of the transformative effect of His Majesty’s enduring Way [?], and of his achievement in nurturing men of talent over a long reign. The signs of great peace are no mere coincidence. These candidates, having been selected [?] by the responsible officials, will present their answers at the imperial court and be appointed to official posts. May they establish meritorious achievements, display integrity and resolve, and take all that they have said today…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而次第酬之則臣等庶幾體
國薦賢足以副
陛下側席之懷若徒以其言徼利
祿於一時而視所學如弁髦
使人指之曰此沙礫碔砆之
儔也是主司之耻也則臣之
懼也終無以釋矣然
===
聖天子威靈之所遐矚
德敎之所宣㫤臣固知其無是
也而猶惓惓不能釋者誠愼
之至也是爲序
左春坊左諭德兼翰林院侍
讀汪鏜謹序
punctuated:
而次第酬之，則臣等庶幾體國薦賢，足以副陛下側席之懷。若徒以其言徼利祿於一時，而視所學如弁髦，使人指之曰：「此沙礫碔砆之儔也，是主司之耻也。」則臣之懼也，終無以釋矣。然聖天子威靈之所遐矚，德敎之所宣㫤，臣固知其無是也，而猶惓惓不能釋者，誠愼之至也。是爲序。
左春坊左諭德兼翰林院侍讀汪鏜謹序。
translation_en:
…and fulfill these promises one by one, then we, your servants, may hope to have served the state by recommending worthy men, sufficiently to answer Your Majesty’s eager desire for talent. If, however, they merely use their words to seek profit and emolument for the moment, treating what they have learned as discarded caps and shorn hair, so that people point to them and say, “These are mere sand, gravel, and stones masquerading as jade—a disgrace to the chief examiners,” then your servant’s apprehension can never be dispelled. Yet wherever the sagely Son of Heaven’s awe-inspiring power reaches afar, and his moral instruction is disseminated [?], your servant knows assuredly that no such thing will occur. That I nevertheless remain anxiously concerned and unable to set this apprehension aside is truly the utmost expression of caution. This serves as the preface.
Preface respectfully composed by Wang Tang, Left Adviser to the Heir Apparent in the Left Secretariat, concurrently Reader-in-Waiting in the Hanlin Academy.

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖肆拾叁年應天府鄉試
提調官

translation_en:
Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination, forty-third year of Jiajing (1564).

Proctors:
Liu Ji, Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture, courtesy name Tiqian, was from Fugou County, Henan. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the jiachen year.
Luo Jiabin, Grand Master of Central Compliance and Prefectural Vice Prefect of Yingtian, courtesy name Xingxian, was from Yibin County, Sichuan. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year.

Examiner:
Wang Tang, Left Admonisher of the Left Spring Bureau and concurrently Reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy, courtesy name Zhenzong, was from Yin County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the dingwei year.

Associate Examiners:
Cai Guozhen, Director of the Bureau of Appointments in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, courtesy name Rupin, was from Fengxin County, Jiangxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the bingchen year.
Nan Xuan, Grand Master for Deliberation and Director of the Bureau of Evaluations in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, courtesy name Shuhou, was from Weinan County, Shaanxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year.
Liu Yingfeng, Gentleman for Fostering Virtue and Secretary acting as Director of the Bureau of Banquets in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites, courtesy name Shaoheng, was from Chaling Subprefecture, Huguang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the bingchen year.
Niu Jing, Gentleman for Upright Service and Secretary acting as Director of the Bureau of the Arsenal in the Nanjing Ministry of War, courtesy name Gongzhao, was from Xian County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the bingchen year.
Shen Qiyuan, Gentleman for Fostering Virtue and Secretary acting as Director of the Bureau of State Farms in the Nanjing Ministry of Works, courtesy name Daoqing, was from Xiushui County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiwei year.
Jiang Sanyi, Gentleman for Upright Service and Secretary acting as Vice Director of the Huguang Bureau in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, courtesy name Ziqian, was from Chengdu Front Guard, Sichuan. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiwei year.
Wu Zhuo, Gentleman for Upright Service and Secretary of the Zhejiang Bureau in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, courtesy name Chunbo, was from Hezhou, Guangxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the renxu year.
Chen Zongqing, Professor of the Confucian School of Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, courtesy name Chongji, was from Jinxi County, Jiangxi. He became a tribute student (gongshi) in the gengzi year.
Chen Ji, Instructor of the Confucian School of Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, courtesy name Shizhen, was from Putian County, Fujian. He became a tribute student in the yimao year.
Zhou Hongdi, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xi County, Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, courtesy name Yuanhui, was from Macheng County, Huguang. He became a tribute student in the yimao year.
Zhang Shouyue, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xindu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, courtesy name Xizeng, was from Yongfu County, Guangxi. He became a tribute student in the wuwu year.

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
監試官
文林郎南京山東道監察御史林潤〔若雨福建莆田縣人丙辰進士〕
承事郎南京浙江道監察御史史官〔秉衡山西翼城縣人丙辰進士〕
收掌試卷官
應天府治中李渭〔湜之貴州思南府官籍陝西咸寧縣人甲午貢士〕
印卷官
應天府通判李樅〔子偶廣東海陽縣人丙辰進士〕
應天府推官張鏊〔維北福建懷安縣人壬子貢士〕
受卷官
===
應天府上元縣知縣段有成〔可達雲南昆明縣人丁酉貢士〕
南京府軍後衛經歷司經歷范岢〔延儀福建甌寧縣人監生〕
南京應天衛經歷司經歷黃魁〔應元山東武定州人監生〕
彌封官
應天府照磨所檢校李東〔子作河南洛陽縣人監生〕
安慶府桐城縣知縣陳于陛〔允升順天府遵化縣人壬戌進士〕
應天府溧水縣知縣陳文燭〔玉叔湖廣沔陽州人壬戌進士〕
謄錄官
應天府江浦縣知縣蕭惟馨〔德卿廣西桂林中衛人乙卯貢士〕
punctuated:
監試官
文林郎南京山東道監察御史林潤〔若雨，福建莆田縣人，丙辰進士〕。
承事郎南京浙江道監察御史史官〔秉衡，山西翼城縣人，丙辰進士〕。

收掌試卷官
應天府治中李渭〔湜之，貴州思南府官籍，陝西咸寧縣人，甲午貢士〕。

應天府通判李樅〔子偶，廣東海陽縣人，丙辰進士〕。
應天府推官張鏊〔維北，福建懷安縣人，壬子貢士〕。

南京應天衛經歷司經歷黃魁〔應元，山東武定州人，監生〕。

彌封官
應天府照磨所檢校李東〔子作，河南洛陽縣人，監生〕。
安慶府桐城縣知縣陳于陛〔允升，順天府遵化縣人，壬戌進士〕。
應天府溧水縣知縣陳文燭〔玉叔，湖廣沔陽州人，壬戌進士〕。

謄錄官
應天府江浦縣知縣蕭惟馨〔德卿，廣西桂林中衛人，乙卯貢士〕。
translation_en:
Examination Inspectors
Lin Run, Gentleman of Literary Service and Investigating Censor of the Shandong Circuit at Nanjing, had the courtesy name Ruoyu. He was from Putian County, Fujian, and became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the bingchen year.
Shi Guan, Gentleman for Rendering Service and Investigating Censor of the Zhejiang Circuit at Nanjing, had the courtesy name Bingheng. He was from Yicheng County, Shanxi, and became a metropolitan graduate in the bingchen year.

Official Responsible for the Custody of Examination Papers
Li Wei, Administrative Assistant of Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Shizhi. His official household registration was in Sinan Prefecture, Guizhou, and he was originally from Xianning County, Shaanxi. He was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the jiawu year.

Officials Responsible for Stamping Examination Papers
Li Cong, Assistant Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zi'ou. He was from Haiyang County, Guangdong, and became a metropolitan graduate in the bingchen year.
Zhang Ao, Judge of Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Weibei. He was from Huai'an County, Fujian, and was a tribute scholar of the renzi year.

Officials Responsible for Receiving Examination Papers
Duan Youcheng, Magistrate of Shangyuan County in Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Keda. He was from Kunming County, Yunnan, and was a tribute scholar of the dingyou year.
Fan Ke, Registrar in the Registry of the Rear Imperial Guard at Nanjing, had the courtesy name Yanyi. He was from Ouning County, Fujian, and was a student of the Imperial University.
Huang Kui, Registrar in the Registry of the Yingtian Guard at Nanjing, had the courtesy name Yingyuan. He was from Wuding Subprefecture, Shandong, and was a student of the Imperial University.

Officials Responsible for Sealing Candidates’ Identifying Information
Li Dong, Inspector in the Records Office of Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zizuo. He was from Luoyang County, Henan, and was a student of the Imperial University.
Chen Yubi, Magistrate of Tongcheng County in Anqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yunsheng. He was from Zunhua County, Shuntian Prefecture, and became a metropolitan graduate in the renxu year.
Chen Wenzhu, Magistrate of Lishui County in Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yushu. He was from Mianyang Subprefecture, Huguang, and became a metropolitan graduate in the renxu year.

Officials Responsible for Transcribing Examination Papers
Xiao Weixin, Magistrate of Jiangpu County in Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Deqing. He was from the Guilin Central Guard, Guangxi, and was a tribute scholar of the yimao year.

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
太平府當塗縣知縣侯思古〔士睿浙江臨海縣人壬戌進士〕
對讀官
應天府溧陽縣知縣趙應元〔子貞浙江仁和縣人壬戌進士〕
池州府青陽縣知縣田登年〔子登四川忠州人己未進士〕
巡綽官
昭勇將軍安慶衛指揮使石中玉〔子完山東武定州人〕
明威將軍新安衛指揮僉事李勇〔尚義山東賓州人〕
搜檢官
武德將軍南京留守後衛正千戶劉霆〔迅卿順天府香河縣人〕
===
武德將軍南京留守右衛正千戶汪文舉〔惟士徽州府婺源縣人〕
昭信校尉南京留守左衛百戶范玉〔廷美安慶府太湖縣人〕
昭信校尉南京留守前衛百戶王應槐〔國卿河南獲嘉縣人〕
供給官
應天府經歷司經歷許中〔允執四川行部司越巂衛人選貢〕
應天府經歷司知事馮樂〔大和浙江烏程縣人監生〕
應天府照磨所照磨何忠〔汝貞直隸南陽縣人監生〕
應天府江寧縣知縣吳福基〔紹□□□□衛籍直隸□□□□貢士〕
應天府江寧縣縣丞李懋〔敬卿河南□□縣人監生〕
punctuated:
太平府當塗縣知縣侯思古〔士睿，浙江臨海縣人，壬戌進士〕。

對讀官：
應天府溧陽縣知縣趙應元〔子貞，浙江仁和縣人，壬戌進士〕。池州府青陽縣知縣田登年〔子登，四川忠州人，己未進士〕。

巡綽官：
昭勇將軍安慶衛指揮使石中玉〔子完，山東武定州人〕。明威將軍新安衛指揮僉事李勇〔尚義，山東賓州人〕。

搜檢官：
武德將軍南京留守後衛正千戶劉霆〔迅卿，順天府香河縣人〕。武德將軍南京留守右衛正千戶汪文舉〔惟士，徽州府婺源縣人〕。昭信校尉南京留守左衛百戶范玉〔廷美，安慶府太湖縣人〕。昭信校尉南京留守前衛百戶王應槐〔國卿，河南獲嘉縣人〕。

供給官：
應天府經歷司經歷許中〔允執，四川行部司越巂衛人，選貢〕。應天府經歷司知事馮樂〔大和，浙江烏程縣人，監生〕。應天府照磨所照磨何忠〔汝貞，直隸南陽縣人，監生〕。應天府江寧縣知縣吳福基〔紹□□□□衛籍，直隸□□□□貢士〕。應天府江寧縣縣丞李懋〔敬卿，河南□□縣人，監生〕。
translation_en:
Hou Sigu, Magistrate of Dangtu County, Taiping Prefecture, had the courtesy name Shirui and was from Linhai County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the renxu year (1562).

Proofreading Officials:
Zhao Yingyuan, Magistrate of Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zizhen and was from Renhe County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the renxu year (1562).
Tian Dengnian, Magistrate of Qingyang County, Chizhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zideng and was from Zhongzhou, Sichuan. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jiwei year (1559).

Patrol Officials:
Shi Zhongyu, General of Illustrious Courage and Commander of the Anqing Guard, had the courtesy name Ziwan and was from Wuding Subprefecture, Shandong.
Li Yong, General of Manifest Might and Assistant Commander of the Xin’an Guard, had the courtesy name Shangyi and was from Binzhou, Shandong [?].

Search and Inspection Officials:
Liu Ting, General of Martial Virtue and Battalion Commander of the Nanjing Rear Guard of the Regency, had the courtesy name Xunqing and was from Xianghe County, Shuntian Prefecture.
Wang Wenju, General of Martial Virtue and Battalion Commander of the Nanjing Right Guard of the Regency, had the courtesy name Weishi and was from Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture.
Fan Yu, Commandant of Manifest Fidelity and Company Commander of the Nanjing Left Guard of the Regency, had the courtesy name Tingmei and was from Taihu County, Anqing Prefecture.
Wang Yinghuai, Commandant of Manifest Fidelity and Company Commander of the Nanjing Front Guard of the Regency, had the courtesy name Guoqing and was from Huojia County, Henan.

Provisioning Officials:
Xu Zhong, Registrar in the Registry of Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yunzhi and was from Yuexi Guard under the Sichuan regional office [?]. He was a selected tribute student.
Feng Le, Clerk in the Registry of Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Dahe and was from Wucheng County, Zhejiang. He was a student of the Imperial Academy.
He Zhong, Record Keeper in the Records Office of Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Ruzhen and was from Nanyang County, Zhili [?]. He was a student of the Imperial Academy.
Wu Fuji, Magistrate of Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture, had a courtesy name beginning with Shao [remainder illegible]. He was registered with a guard whose name is illegible; the annotation also mentions Zhili, followed by illegible characters, and identifies him as a tribute scholar [?].
Li Mao, Vice Magistrate of Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Jingqing and was from a county in Henan whose two-character name is illegible. He was a student of the Imperial Academy.

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子曰參乎吾道一以貫之曾子曰唯
肫肫其仁淵淵其淵浩浩其天
我非堯舜之道不敢以陳於王前
易
大哉乾乎剛健中正純粹精也六爻發揮
旁通情也時乗六龍以御天也雲行雨
施天下平也
===
利有攸往中正有慶
範圍天地之化而不過曲成萬物而不遺
窮神知化德之盛也
書
惟動丕應徯志以昭受上帝天其申命用
休
山川鬼神亦莫不寧暨鳥獸魚鼈咸若
四五紀一曰歲二曰月三曰日四曰星辰
五曰厯數
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

子曰：「參乎！吾道一以貫之。」曾子曰：「唯。」

肫肫其仁，淵淵其淵，浩浩其天。

我非堯舜之道，不敢以陳於王前。

易

大哉乾乎！剛健中正，純粹精也。六爻發揮，旁通情也。時乗六龍，以御天也。雲行雨施，天下平也。

利有攸往，中正有慶。

範圍天地之化而不過，曲成萬物而不遺。

窮神知化，德之盛也。

書

惟動丕應，徯志以昭受上帝，天其申命用休。

山川鬼神亦莫不寧，暨鳥獸魚鼈咸若。

四、五紀：一曰歲，二曰月，三曰日，四曰星辰，五曰厯數。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said, “Shen! My Way is threaded together by one principle.” Master Zeng replied, “Yes.”

How earnest his benevolence; how deep his profundity; how vast his heavenliness!

Unless it accords with the Way of Yao and Shun, I dare not set it forth before the king.

Book of Changes

Great indeed is Qian! Firm and vigorous, central and correct, it is pure, unmixed, and refined. Its six lines unfold their significance and comprehend the circumstances on every side. At the proper times, it rides the six dragons to govern Heaven. Clouds move and rain falls, and all under Heaven is at peace.

It is beneficial to have somewhere to go: centrality and correctness bring blessings.

It encompasses the transformations of Heaven and Earth without exceeding them, and brings the myriad things to completion in all their particulars, leaving none out.

To fathom the numinous and understand transformation is the fullness of virtue.

Book of Documents

Your every action meets with a great response; they await your intention. Thus you may illustriously receive the mandate of the Lord on High, and Heaven will renew its mandate with favor.

The spirits of mountains and rivers were likewise all at peace, and birds, beasts, fish, and turtles were all in their proper order.

Fourth, the five regulators of time: the first is the year; the second, the month; the third, the day; the fourth, the stars and celestial stations; and the fifth, calendrical calculations.

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
乃用三有宅克卽宅曰三有俊克卽俊嚴
惟丕式
詩
交韔二弓竹閉緄縢
鶴鳴于九皐聲聞于野魚潛在淵或在于
渚樂彼之園爰有樹檀其下維蘀他山
之石可以爲錯
君子萬年介爾景福
莫敢不來享莫敢不來王
===
春秋
夏公及宋公遇于清〔隱公四年〕夏齊侯衛
侯胥命于蒲〔桓公三年〕
冬公次于滑〔莊公三年〕春王正月公會齊
侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯侵蔡
蔡潰遂伐楚次于陘〔僖公四年〕
秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕晉侯伐秦〔文公四年〕
晉師白狄伐秦〔宣公八年〕秦人白狄伐
晉〔成公九年〕
punctuated:
乃用三有宅，克卽宅；曰三有俊，克卽俊。嚴惟丕式。

詩
交韔二弓，竹閉緄縢。
鶴鳴于九皐，聲聞于野。魚潛在淵，或在于渚。樂彼之園，爰有樹檀，其下維蘀。他山之石，可以爲錯。
君子萬年，介爾景福。
莫敢不來享，莫敢不來王。

春秋
夏，公及宋公遇于清。〔隱公四年〕夏，齊侯、衛侯胥命于蒲。〔桓公三年〕
冬，公次于滑。〔莊公三年〕春，王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡。蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。〔僖公四年〕
秦人伐晉。〔文公三年〕晉侯伐秦。〔文公四年〕
晉師、白狄伐秦。〔宣公八年〕秦人、白狄伐晉。〔成公九年〕
translation_en:
Thus, in employing men for the three offices, he could find those fit to occupy them; in seeking outstanding men for the three offices, he could find such outstanding men. He held them in reverence and made them his great example.

Book of Odes
The two bows are placed together in their cases, with bamboo bow-protectors and bindings of cord.
The crane cries in the deepest marshes; its voice is heard in the open country. Fish hide in the depths, or else remain by the islets. Delightful is that garden, where sandalwood trees grow, with fallen leaves beneath them. Stones from another mountain can serve as whetstones.
May the lord live ten thousand years; may great blessings attend you.
None dares fail to come to present offerings; none dares fail to come to acknowledge the king.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In summer, the duke and the Duke of Song met at Qing. 〔Fourth year of Duke Yin.〕 In summer, the Marquis of Qi and the Marquis of Wei exchanged pledges at Pu. 〔Third year of Duke Huan.〕
In winter, the duke encamped at Hua. 〔Third year of Duke Zhuang.〕 In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in invading Cai. Cai collapsed; they then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕
Men of Qin attacked Jin. 〔Third year of Duke Wen.〕 The Marquis of Jin attacked Qin. 〔Fourth year of Duke Wen.〕
The army of Jin and the Baidi attacked Qin. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xuan.〕 Men of Qin and the Baidi attacked Jin. 〔Ninth year of Duke Cheng.〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
大蒐于昌間〔昭公二十有二年〕
禮記
凡在天下九州之民者無不咸獻其力以
共皇天上帝社稷寢廟山林名川之祀
善問者如攻堅木先其易者後其節目及
其久也相說以解
君子之聽音非聽其鏗鏘而已也彼亦有
所合之也
貴其不已如日月東西相從而不已也是
天道也不閉其久是天道也無為而物
成是天道也已成而明是天道也
===
第貳場
論
聖人在天子之位
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令禮官勸學詔〔元朔五年〕
擬唐以張說兼集賢院學士誥〔開元十六
年〕
punctuated:
大蒐于昌間。〔昭公二十有二年〕

禮記
凡在天下九州之民者，無不咸獻其力，以共皇天上帝、社稷、寢廟、山林、名川之祀。
善問者如攻堅木，先其易者，後其節目；及其久也，相說以解。
君子之聽音，非聽其鏗鏘而已也，彼亦有所合之也。
貴其不已，如日月東西相從而不已也，是天道也；不閉其久，是天道也；無為而物成，是天道也；已成而明，是天道也。

第貳場
論
聖人在天子之位。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令禮官勸學詔。〔元朔五年〕
擬唐以張說兼集賢院學士誥。〔開元十六年〕
translation_en:
A great hunt was held at Changjian. 〔Twenty-second year of Duke Zhao.〕

Book of Rites
All the people of the Nine Provinces under Heaven contribute their labor to provide for sacrifices to August Heaven, the Lord on High, the altars of soil and grain, the ancestral sanctuaries and temples, the mountains and forests, and the famous rivers.
One skilled in questioning proceeds as though working hard wood: first tackling the easy parts, then the knots. In time, questioner and respondent find mutual satisfaction as the difficulties are resolved.
When the gentleman listens to music, he does not merely listen to its ringing sounds; he also finds in it something with which he accords.
What is valued is its ceaselessness, like the sun and moon following one another east and west without end: this is the Way of Heaven. Its enduring course is not obstructed [?]: this is the Way of Heaven. Things are brought to completion without action: this is the Way of Heaven. Once completed, they become manifest: this is the Way of Heaven.

Second Session
Discourse
“The sage occupying the position of Son of Heaven.”

Edicts, Letters of Appointment, and Memorials 〔One topic from among these [?].〕
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor ordering the ritual officials to encourage learning. 〔Fifth year of Yuanshuo.〕
Compose a Tang letter of appointment naming Zhang Shuo concurrently an Academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies. 〔Sixteenth year of Kaiyuan.〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
擬海南諸國各遣使
獻麒麟凡四羣臣
賀表〔宣德八年〕
判語〔五條〕
官員襲蔭
功臣田土
鄉飲酒禮
優恤軍屬
修理倉庫
===
第叁塲
策〔五道〕
問自古帝王保艱大之業隆懿爍之治者
必有上下交儆之益焉其明良相遇一
德一心若時幾之勑祗敬之規無逸之
警見於詩書所稱者不一而足也可得
而論述之歟我
太祖高皇帝
成祖文皇帝咸以首出之資應圖啓運我
punctuated:
擬海南諸國各遣使獻麒麟凡四，羣臣賀表〔宣德八年〕。

判語〔五條〕：官員襲蔭；功臣田土；鄉飲酒禮；優恤軍屬；修理倉庫。

第叁塲
策〔五道〕
問：自古帝王保艱大之業、隆懿爍之治者，必有上下交儆之益焉。其明良相遇，一德一心，若時幾之勑、祗敬之規、無逸之警，見於詩書所稱者，不一而足也。可得而論述之歟？我太祖高皇帝、成祖文皇帝，咸以首出之資，應圖啓運。我

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
皇上以聖神之德建極紹天
峻德巍功弘覽踔識眞有以超越三五而非
臣下所能仰跂其萬一者雖欲輸忠納
誨以效一得之愚其道無繇也然
聖不自聖而
宸章固中外之臣所諷誦而傳習者可得而揚
兢業保治之心敷揚於
問答彪炳於
厲之歟然究觀其指於古昔明良孚契
===
之美德業交修之助其亦有所異同歟
漢晁錯言五帝神聖其臣莫及可謂善
窺聖人之蘊者夫曰神聖矣而尚有俟
於交儆者豈別有説歟至宋儒程氏之
意謂唐虞交儆而夏商之後未盡然者
何歟諸士子漸濡
聖化必思所以引揚
德業以鳴我
國家之盛者幸詳著於篇
punctuated: 皇上以聖神之德建極紹天，峻德巍功，弘覽踔識，眞有以超越三五，而非臣下所能仰跂其萬一者。雖欲輸忠納誨，以效一得之愚，其道無繇也。然聖不自聖，而宸章固中外之臣所諷誦而傳習者，可得而揚兢業保治之心，敷揚於問答，彪炳於厲之歟？然究觀其指，於古昔明良孚契之美、德業交修之助，其亦有所異同歟？漢晁錯言五帝神聖，其臣莫及，可謂善窺聖人之蘊者。夫曰神聖矣，而尚有俟於交儆者，豈別有説歟？至宋儒程氏之意，謂唐虞交儆，而夏商之後未盡然者，何歟？諸士子漸濡聖化，必思所以引揚德業，以鳴我國家之盛者，幸詳著於篇。
translation_en:
…His Majesty, through his sagely and divine virtue, establishes the supreme standard and carries forward Heaven’s mandate. His lofty virtue, towering achievements, comprehensive vision, and surpassing discernment truly enable him to transcend the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors; his servants cannot hope to attain even a ten-thousandth part of his greatness. Even if they wished to offer their loyalty and submit admonitions, contributing some small insight from their own humble understanding, they would have no means of doing so. Yet the sage does not regard himself as a sage, and the imperial writings are indeed recited, transmitted, and studied by officials both at court and outside it. Can his vigilant concern to preserve good government be proclaimed, expounded through questions and answers, and brilliantly displayed in exhortation [? The transcription here appears disordered]? Upon examining their purport closely, how do they resemble or differ from the admirable mutual trust between enlightened rulers and worthy ministers of antiquity, and the assistance these gave one another in cultivating virtue and achievement?

Chao Cuo of the Han said that the Five Emperors were divine and sagely, beyond the reach of their ministers. He may be said to have discerned well the inner qualities of sages. Yet if they were divine and sagely, why did they still depend upon mutual admonition? Is there some further explanation? As for the view of Master Cheng, the Song Confucian scholar, why did he hold that rulers and ministers admonished one another in the time of Tang and Yu, but that this was no longer fully the case from Xia and Shang onward? You candidates, steeped in the transforming influence of His Majesty’s sagely rule, must surely be considering how to advance and extol his virtue and achievements, thereby giving voice to the flourishing greatness of our state. Please set forth your views in detail in your essays.

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
問帝王治世隆樸茂之風成愿慤之俗非
教刑迭用致之無繇也然其所以爲教
爲刑俾可世守不變者今能稱說之歟
嬴氏以來文軌頻異代所爲治史冊可
徵而終未帝王若者何豈時漸澆漓古
不可復而致理君子姑一切聽其所自
至歟昔匡衡崔寔有慨於時作爲疏論
以警動當世今其言在也可撮其樞要
爲致理者諷諭歟夫衡之疏班固録焉
===
以其能明政治得失也寔之論范曄録
焉以其指切時要言辯而確也即考究
疏論中則二子造意迥相反矣而皆稱
爲善得歟繫皆有關於教若刑也否歟
國初風醇俗厚媲美帝王其在於今殆不與
類毋亦有如衡寔所慨者歟
聖天子崇德化肅法紀致四十餘年太平而返
醇還厚之意無一歲不形諸
綸旨也乃有司奉行未臻實效何歟有諸士
punctuated: 問：帝王治世，隆樸茂之風，成愿慤之俗，非教刑迭用，致之無繇也。然其所以爲教爲刑，俾可世守不變者，今能稱說之歟？嬴氏以來，文軌頻異，代所爲治，史冊可徵，而終未帝王若者，何？豈時漸澆漓，古不可復，而致理君子姑一切聽其所自至歟？昔匡衡、崔寔有慨於時，作爲疏論，以警動當世。今其言在也，可撮其樞要，爲致理者諷諭歟？夫衡之疏，班固録焉，以其能明政治得失也；寔之論，范曄録焉，以其指切時要，言辯而確也。即考究疏論中，則二子造意迥相反矣，而皆稱爲善，得歟？繫皆有關於教若刑也，否歟？國初風醇俗厚，媲美帝王，其在於今，殆不與類，毋亦有如衡、寔所慨者歟？聖天子崇德化，肅法紀，致四十餘年太平，而返醇還厚之意，無一歲不形諸綸旨也。乃有司奉行未臻實效，何歟？有諸士
translation_en: Question: When the sage emperors and kings governed the world, they fostered an ethos of simplicity and integrity and established customs of sincerity and honesty. Without employing moral instruction and punishment in alternation, there was no way to achieve this. Can you now explain how they instituted instruction and punishment so that these could be maintained unchanged from generation to generation? Since the rule of the Ying house of Qin, systems of writing and carriage gauges have changed repeatedly. The governance of successive dynasties can be verified in the historical records, yet it has never equaled that of the sage emperors and kings. Why is this? Is it that the age has gradually become morally debased and antiquity cannot be restored, so that gentlemen seeking good government must simply leave everything to take its own course? In former times, Kuang Heng and Cui Shi lamented the conditions of their age and composed memorials and discourses to awaken and admonish their contemporaries. Their words survive today. Can you extract their essential points to offer admonition to those seeking good government? Ban Gu recorded Heng’s memorial because it clarified the successes and failures of governance; Fan Ye recorded Shi’s discourse because it addressed the urgent concerns of the time directly, with eloquent and sound arguments. Yet, upon examining the memorial and discourse, we find that the two men’s underlying intentions were diametrically opposed. Is it right to praise both as excellent? Is this because both bear upon instruction and punishment [?], or not? At the founding of our dynasty, the prevailing ethos was pure and customs were sound, rivaling those under the sage emperors and kings. Conditions today scarcely resemble them. Might there not also be grounds for the kinds of lament expressed by Heng and Shi? The sagely Son of Heaven has exalted moral transformation and enforced laws and discipline, bringing more than forty years of peace. Not a year has passed without his intention to restore purity and soundness finding expression in imperial pronouncements. Why, then, has their implementation by the responsible officials failed to produce substantive results? You scholars …

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
目擊其然必勃興致理之志試陳他日
所能爲俾我執爲左券焉可矣
問上古之世載籍未具至周始備焉然當
時傳播未廣士之獲覩全經者或鮮迨
遭秦火之後殘闕殆甚漢興始表章六
經諸儒競起而補葺之於是六籍復全
其功偉矣然皆各守師說乃有五經家
法之號五經師法之名何歟或議其伐
異黨同穿鑿附會不能無失焉然諸儒
===
訓詁之盛簡帙浩繁其視成周之世奚
啻百倍果能羽翼聖經否歟有宋諸儒
考定傳註粹然一出於正可謂有補於
經學然非漢儒訓釋之遺則將安所折
衷耶或謂漢儒網羅放失能存之於博
而宋儒妙契宗旨能反之於約信歟然
朱子亦謂當時解經者有三而深不滿
於蘇陳張子韶輩其視漢儒訓詁之失
又何如也且上古之世六籍未具而士
punctuated:
目擊其然，必勃興致理之志。試陳他日所能爲，俾我執爲左券焉，可矣。

問：上古之世，載籍未具，至周始備焉。然當時傳播未廣，士之獲覩全經者或鮮。迨遭秦火之後，殘闕殆甚。漢興，始表章六經，諸儒競起而補葺之，於是六籍復全，其功偉矣。然皆各守師說，乃有五經家法之號、五經師法之名，何歟？或議其伐異黨同，穿鑿附會，不能無失焉。然諸儒訓詁之盛，簡帙浩繁，其視成周之世，奚啻百倍！果能羽翼聖經否歟？有宋諸儒考定傳註，粹然一出於正，可謂有補於經學。然非漢儒訓釋之遺，則將安所折衷耶？或謂漢儒網羅放失，能存之於博，而宋儒妙契宗旨，能反之於約，信歟？然朱子亦謂當時解經者有三，而深不滿於蘇、陳、張子韶輩，其視漢儒訓詁之失，又何如也？且上古之世，六籍未具，而士
translation_en:
…having witnessed this state of affairs, you must surely be stirred to aspire to bring about good government. Set forth what you will be able to accomplish in the future, so that I may hold it as a binding pledge; that will suffice.

Question: In high antiquity, written records were not yet complete; only under the Zhou did they become fully available. Yet their circulation at that time was limited, and perhaps few scholars had the opportunity to see the classics in their entirety. After the Qin book-burning, the losses and lacunae were exceedingly severe. With the rise of the Han, the Six Classics began to receive recognition and promotion. Confucian scholars competed to restore and repair them, and thus the six canonical works were once again complete. Their achievement was great indeed. Yet each adhered to the teachings of his own master, giving rise to the designations “school traditions of the Five Classics” and “master traditions of the Five Classics.” Why was this? Some criticize them for attacking those who differed and siding with those who agreed, forcing interpretations and making strained connections; they could not have been without faults. Yet their exegetical scholarship flourished, filling vast numbers of volumes—surely more than a hundred times those of the Zhou in its maturity! Did this truly help elucidate the sages’ classics?

The Confucian scholars of the Song examined and established the commentaries and annotations, their work proceeding purely and wholly from correct principles. They may indeed be said to have contributed to classical scholarship. Yet without the explanations bequeathed by Han scholars, on what basis could they have weighed competing interpretations? Some say that Han scholars gathered what had been scattered and lost, preserving it through breadth of learning, whereas Song scholars subtly grasped the essential purport and brought it back to its essentials. Is this true? Yet Master Zhu also said that interpreters of the classics in his day fell into three groups, and he was deeply dissatisfied with such men as Su, Chen, and Zhang Zishao. How do their shortcomings compare with the exegetical failings of Han scholars? Furthermore, in high antiquity, when the six canonical works were not yet complete, scholars…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
皆篤於自修何今之時簡帙大備而士
之所學寖不及古豈所謂徒求之於博
而不能反之於約歟我
國家尊崇儒術甄育多士
皇上闡揚經傳陶鑄羣材諸士生當其盛其於
通經學古之道博聞反約之功有槪於
中久矣其悉言之以覩所藴
問古帝王而降禦戎無上策矣乃論議之
臣憤時自效若晁錯陸贄范仲淹言皆
===
班然丈册也果鑿鑿協時宜裨戰守耶
今天下敉寧跡古帝王時何讓第郊圻千里內
胡卒觭虜東薊遼西宣大無歲撤烽燧
不警也而論議之臣競出其畫諳
闕下獻豈盡協時宜裨戰守如晁陸范三子耶
夫談守者是守矣然不計而守卽守不
堅守胡爲耶談戰者是戰矣然不教而
戰卽戰不克戰胡爲耶懲守之失者曰
分境秉垣外多棄野不如梟旅而應戎
punctuated:
皆篤於自修，何今之時簡帙大備，而士之所學寖不及古？豈所謂徒求之於博，而不能反之於約歟？我國家尊崇儒術，甄育多士，皇上闡揚經傳，陶鑄羣材。諸士生當其盛，其於通經學古之道、博聞反約之功，有槪於中久矣。其悉言之，以覩所藴。
問：古帝王而降，禦戎無上策矣。乃論議之臣憤時自效，若晁錯、陸贄、范仲淹，言皆班然丈册也，果鑿鑿協時宜、裨戰守耶？今天下敉寧，跡古帝王時何讓？第郊圻千里內，胡卒觭虜，東薊遼，西宣大，無歲撤烽燧不警也。而論議之臣競出其畫，諳闕下獻，豈盡協時宜、裨戰守，如晁、陸、范三子耶？夫談守者是守矣，然不計而守，卽守不堅，守胡爲耶？談戰者是戰矣，然不教而戰，卽戰不克，戰胡爲耶？懲守之失者曰：分境秉垣，外多棄野，不如梟旅而應戎
translation_en:
…all devoted themselves earnestly to self-cultivation. Why is it that today, when books are so abundantly available, scholars’ learning increasingly falls short of that of antiquity? Is this what is meant by merely pursuing breadth without being able to return to essentials? Our dynasty honors Confucian learning and selects and nurtures its many scholars. His Majesty elucidates the classics and their commentaries and molds men of many talents. You scholars have been born into this flourishing age. Surely you have long reflected upon the way of mastering the classics and studying antiquity, and upon the work of acquiring broad knowledge and returning to essentials. Set forth your views fully, so that we may see what you have within you.
Question: Since the sovereigns of antiquity, there has been no supreme strategy for resisting the Rong. Yet ministers who offered counsel, troubled by the circumstances of their times, sought to prove their usefulness. The words of such men as Chao Cuo, Lu Zhi, and Fan Zhongyan are all conspicuously recorded in writings [?]. Did they truly and precisely suit the needs of their times and aid warfare and defense? Today all under Heaven is tranquil: in its achievements, how does it fall short of the age of the ancient sovereigns? Yet within the thousand-li region surrounding the capital, there are Hu soldiers and raiders [?]; from Ji and Liao in the east to Xuan and Da in the west, there is no year when the beacon fires can be discontinued and no alarms sound. Ministers offering counsel compete to produce their plans and present them at the palace gates [?]. Do all these plans suit present needs and aid warfare and defense, as did those of Chao, Lu, and Fan? Those who advocate defense regard defense as correct. Yet defending without planning means that the defenses will not hold firm: what purpose does such defense serve? Those who advocate battle regard battle as correct. Yet fighting without training means that battle will not bring victory: what purpose does such fighting serve? Those who take warning from the failures of defense say: ‘Dividing the territory and holding the ramparts leaves much open country outside abandoned. Better to deploy valiant troops [?] to meet the Rong…’

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
有惴心也守顧已耶懲戰之失者曰摧
鋒挫銳內鮮良材不如據險而須戎無
騁足也戢顧已耶守非一事執要者堅
戰非一途握機者克機要可豫定耶閫
鉞之臣任在疆場身所經略非料想者
同也而罕著殊勳勢固不獲自盡耶
王上神聖超軼古帝王得邊臣一疏至卽夜分
詔樞筦臣行矣而謂不獲自盡也信耶諸士
經濟石畫無愧晁陸范三子試吐之占
===
後效焉毋但搖筆端飾文辭相眩也
問兵之所重者將將之所握者機故慮周
計遠道出萬全此非識權達變者何以
與此然其要總之曰得天者勝得地者
勝得人者勝三者一闕北矣任宏論次
兵書而有陰陽形勝權謀技巧之說非
是之謂耶乃若孫武始計之篇呂望龍
韜之書固言之詳矣可得而聞其指歟
試舉古事一二評之歲星南見而東晉
punctuated:
有惴心也。守顧已耶？懲戰之失者曰：「摧鋒挫銳，內鮮良材，不如據險而須，戎無騁足也。」戢顧已耶？守非一事，執要者堅；戰非一途，握機者克。機要可豫定耶？閫鉞之臣，任在疆場，身所經略，非料想者同也，而罕著殊勳，勢固不獲自盡耶？王上神聖，超軼古帝王，得邊臣一疏至，卽夜分詔樞筦臣行矣，而謂不獲自盡也，信耶？諸士經濟石畫，無愧晁陸范三子，試吐之，占後效焉，毋但搖筆端、飾文辭相眩也。

問：兵之所重者將，將之所握者機。故慮周計遠，道出萬全，此非識權達變者，何以與此？然其要，總之曰：得天者勝，得地者勝，得人者勝。三者一闕，北矣。任宏論次兵書，而有陰陽、形勝、權謀、技巧之說，非是之謂耶？乃若孫武《始計》之篇、呂望《龍韜》之書，固言之詳矣，可得而聞其指歟？試舉古事一二評之：歲星南見，而東晉
translation_en:
…have cause for apprehension. But would defense then cease? Those who take warning from failures in battle say: “To break the enemy’s vanguard and blunt their elite forces, we have few capable men at home. Better to occupy defensible terrain and await them, so that the enemy has no room to advance.” But would warfare then cease? Defense involves more than one undertaking: those who grasp its essentials hold firm. Battle admits more than one approach: those who seize the opportune moment prevail. Can these opportunities and essentials be determined beforehand? Commanders entrusted with military authority bear responsibility on the frontiers. Their personal experience of managing operations differs from the conjectures of others. Yet they seldom achieve outstanding merit. Do circumstances indeed prevent them from exercising their abilities to the full? Our sovereign, in his divine sagacity, surpasses the emperors and kings of antiquity. Whenever a frontier official’s memorial arrives, he immediately orders the officials directing military affairs to act, even in the middle of the night. Can the claim that commanders cannot exercise their abilities to the full really be true? You scholars possess firm plans for ordering the realm, worthy of the three masters Chao, Lu, and Fan. Set them forth, so that their future efficacy may be judged. Do not merely flourish your brushes and embellish your language to dazzle one another.

Question: What an army depends upon is its commander; what a commander must grasp is the opportune moment. Thus his deliberations must be comprehensive, his plans far-reaching, and his methods entirely secure. How could anyone accomplish this without understanding expedient action and adapting to changing circumstances? Yet the essentials may be summed up thus: those who secure the advantages of Heaven prevail; those who secure the advantages of terrain prevail; those who secure the support of men prevail. If any one of these three is lacking, defeat follows. When Ren Hong classified and arranged military writings, he distinguished yin and yang, dispositions and strategic advantages, expedient planning, and technical skills. Was this not what he meant? As for Sun Wu’s chapter “Initial Calculations” and Lü Wang’s book “Dragon Secret Teaching,” they certainly discuss these matters in detail. May we hear an explanation of their purport? Take one or two events from antiquity and assess them: Jupiter appeared in the south, and the Eastern Jin…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
昌月行掩昴而蠕蠕破歲在庚午不利
西行之師熒惑退舍卒克渭橋之難此
非得天時者勝歟據北山之險而秦兵
解得水草之便而諸羌遁移軍河陽而
敵兵阻襲取固軍而北鄙寧此非得地
形者勝歟仁賢任用而蜀漢興隆智士
效謀而赤壁奏捷忘身徇國者乃再造
唐室推誠待士者卒計擒元濟此非得
人謀者勝歟卽三者筭計見效其章明
===
較著若此可一闗歟至其輕重緩急之
辨則又不可執一論者後世淫巫瞽史
舍人而談天驕將惰卒乃恃險而廢謀
則胥失之矣諸士必有定見也其試言
之毋誘曰末之學也
punctuated: 昌。月行掩昴而蠕蠕破，歲在庚午，不利西行之師；熒惑退舍，卒克渭橋之難。此非得天時者勝歟？據北山之險而秦兵解，得水草之便而諸羌遁，移軍河陽而敵兵阻，襲取固軍而北鄙寧。此非得地形者勝歟？仁賢任用而蜀漢興隆，智士效謀而赤壁奏捷，忘身徇國者乃再造唐室，推誠待士者卒計擒元濟。此非得人謀者勝歟？卽三者筭計見效，其章明較著若此，可一闗歟？至其輕重緩急之辨，則又不可執一論者。後世淫巫瞽史，舍人而談天；驕將惰卒，乃恃險而廢謀，則胥失之矣。諸士必有定見也，其試言之，毋誘曰末之學也。
translation_en:
… flourished. When the moon passed over and occulted the Pleiades, the Rouran were defeated. In the gengwu year, conditions were unfavorable for an army marching west; when Mars retreated from its celestial station, the crisis at Weiqiao was finally overcome. Do these examples not show that those who obtain favorable celestial timing prevail? By occupying the strategic heights of Beishan, an army caused the Qin forces to withdraw; by securing convenient access to water and pasture, it drove the various Qiang groups into flight. Moving the army to Heyang blocked the enemy forces; taking Gujun [?] by surprise pacified the northern frontier. Do these examples not show that those who obtain favorable terrain prevail? Employing humane and worthy men brought prosperity to Shu Han; wise men's contributions to strategy secured victory at Chibi. A man who forgot himself in service to his country restored the Tang ruling house; one who treated his officers with wholehearted sincerity ultimately devised the plan that captured Yuanji. Do these examples not show that those who obtain sound human counsel prevail?

Calculations based on these three considerations have proved effective, with results so clear and manifest: can any one be omitted [?]? Yet distinctions concerning their relative importance and urgency cannot be discussed by rigidly adhering to a single principle. In later ages, wayward shamans and blind astrologers abandoned human affairs to discourse on Heaven; arrogant generals and indolent soldiers relied on difficult terrain and neglected planning. All alike went astray. You gentlemen must surely have settled views on this. Set them forth, and do not misleadingly dismiss this as a minor branch of learning [?].

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰參乎吾道一以貫之曾子曰唯
李國士
同考試官教諭張　批〔講甚明暢而於唯字　尤善發揮〕
同考試官署郎中牛　批〔深得聖賢授受口氣〕
同考試官郎中蔡　批〔不費詞說理趣躍如〕
考試官左諭德汪　批〔語有意見〕
===
聖人之傳道以心而大賢之悟道亦以心也夫
一貫之旨聖人傳心之要法也非大賢深契其
妙安能感悟之速若此哉昔夫子以爲學資貫
於知要道不可以易傳若參也察識之精已博
觀其用而眞積之久將默會其原故特舉而示
之曰天下之道雖散見於事物而實根柢於吾
心吾惟本此心之一致以效天下之動而成性之
中存者有以達諸萬化而不匱由吾心之一理
以應天下之事而淵泉之內蓄者有以通諸萬
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
子曰：「參乎！吾道一以貫之。」曾子曰：「唯。」
李國士
同考試官教諭張　批〔講甚明暢，而於唯字　尤善發揮。〕
同考試官署郎中牛　批〔深得聖賢授受口氣。〕
同考試官郎中蔡　批〔不費詞說，理趣躍如。〕
考試官左諭德汪　批〔語有意見。〕

聖人之傳道以心，而大賢之悟道亦以心也。夫一貫之旨，聖人傳心之要法也。非大賢深契其妙，安能感悟之速若此哉？昔夫子以爲學資貫於知要，道不可以易傳。若參也，察識之精，已博觀其用；而眞積之久，將默會其原。故特舉而示之曰：「天下之道，雖散見於事物，而實根柢於吾心。吾惟本此心之一致，以效天下之動，而成性之中存者，有以達諸萬化而不匱；由吾心之一理，以應天下之事，而淵泉之內蓄者，有以通諸萬
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

The Master said: “Shen! My Way is threaded through by one principle.” Master Zeng said: “Yes.”

Li Guoshi

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The exposition is very clear and fluent, and particularly good at drawing out the meaning of the word ‘Yes.’”
Associate Examiner Niu, Acting Director, comments: “It captures profoundly the tone in which the sage transmits and the worthy receives the teaching.”
Associate Examiner Cai, Director, comments: “Without expending words on explanation, the significance of the principle comes vividly to life.”
Examiner Wang, Left Mentor, comments: “The language shows insight.”

The sage transmits the Way through the mind, and the great worthy likewise apprehends the Way through the mind. The purport of the single unifying principle is the essential method by which the sage transmits his mind. Had the great worthy not deeply grasped its subtlety, how could he have responded with such swift understanding? Formerly, the Master considered that achieving coherence in learning depended on knowing what was essential, and that the Way could not be transmitted lightly. As for Shen, through the precision of his observation and discernment, he had already surveyed its workings widely; through his long accumulation of genuine effort, he was about to comprehend its source silently. Thus the Master singled this out and revealed it to him, saying: “Though the Way of all under Heaven appears dispersed among affairs and things, it is in fact rooted in my mind. I simply take the unity of this mind as my foundation in responding to all movements under Heaven, so that what is preserved within my fully realized nature can extend to the myriad transformations without being exhausted. Following the single principle of my mind, I respond to the affairs of all under Heaven, so that what is stored within, like a deep-flowing spring, can permeate the myriad …

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
變而不窮蓋合萬爲一而綱維衆動之原已豫
吾内則一實萬分而酬酢百爲之妙自利吾外
吾之道如是而已此夫子嘗可之敎固有以投
其所欲聞而曾子造詣之純實有以發其所深
省故不復有所疑而直應之曰唯以爲參也向
嘗隨在省察固疑其不足以立本也今聞夫子
之言果知天下之道管於吾心而泛觀博識者
之爲勞也向嘗卽事持循固疑其不足以守要
也今聞夫子之言果知萬事之原統於吾性而
===
强探力索者之爲遠也蓋由博而歸之約則致
一之功自足由體而達之用則應務之地有餘
非夫子之善敎安知至道之妙一如此哉噫觀
聖門授受之旨而道統之傳有所託矣抑夫子
嘗以是道語子貢矣子貢之疑信相參固不若
曾子之脫然有悟何也蓋曾子之學得之於踐
履篤實而子貢則求之於博聞强識故悟道之
淺深不同如此此可見知行雖合一而輕重本
末又有等焉善學者當自得之
punctuated:
變而不窮。蓋合萬爲一，而綱維衆動之原已豫吾内，則一實萬分，而酬酢百爲之妙自利吾外。吾之道如是而已。」此夫子嘗可之敎，固有以投其所欲聞，而曾子造詣之純，實有以發其所深省。故不復有所疑，而直應之曰：「唯！」以爲參也向嘗隨在省察，固疑其不足以立本也。今聞夫子之言，果知天下之道管於吾心，而泛觀博識者之爲勞也。向嘗卽事持循，固疑其不足以守要也。今聞夫子之言，果知萬事之原統於吾性，而强探力索者之爲遠也。蓋由博而歸之約，則致一之功自足；由體而達之用，則應務之地有餘。非夫子之善敎，安知至道之妙一如此哉？

噫！觀聖門授受之旨，而道統之傳有所託矣。抑夫子嘗以是道語子貢矣，子貢之疑信相參，固不若曾子之脫然有悟，何也？蓋曾子之學，得之於踐履篤實，而子貢則求之於博聞强識，故悟道之淺深不同如此。此可見知行雖合一，而輕重本末又有等焉。善學者當自得之。
translation_en:
…transformations without exhaustion. By gathering the myriad into one, the source that orders all activity is already present within me [?]; thus the one reality is differentiated into myriad particulars, and the wondrous capacity to respond to every undertaking operates smoothly in my outward dealings. My Way is simply this.” This teaching of the Master [?] indeed addressed what Zengzi wished to hear, while the purity of Zengzi’s attainment enabled it to awaken what he had deeply pondered. Thus he had no further doubt and answered directly: “Yes!” His thought was this: I, Shen, formerly examined myself in every circumstance, yet suspected that this was insufficient to establish the foundation. Now, hearing the Master’s words, I truly know that the Way of all under Heaven is gathered within my mind [?], and that wide-ranging observation and extensive learning entail toil. Formerly I maintained my practice in each particular affair, yet suspected that this was insufficient to hold fast to the essentials. Now, hearing the Master’s words, I truly know that the source of all affairs is united in my nature, and that strenuous probing and forceful searching lead far afield. By returning from breadth to simplicity, the effort to attain unity is sufficient of itself; by extending from substance to function, one has ample capacity to respond to affairs. Without the Master’s skill in teaching, how could I have known that the wondrous unity of the highest Way was like this?

Ah! In considering the purport of what was imparted and received within the sage’s school, we see that the transmission of the succession of the Way had found someone to whom it could be entrusted. Yet the Master also once spoke of this Way to Zigong. Why did Zigong mingle doubt with belief, falling short of Zengzi’s unimpeded awakening? Zengzi’s learning was attained through earnest and substantial practice, whereas Zigong sought it through broad learning and a strong memory. Hence their understanding of the Way differed in depth to this degree. This shows that although knowledge and action form a unity, they nevertheless have differing weights and stand in a relation of root and branch. Those skilled in learning should grasp this for themselves.

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
肫肫其仁淵淵其淵浩浩其天
汪文輝
同考試官教授陳　批　措詞精確中庸義如
此者最難得
同考試官署郎中劉　批　至誠天道最難形容
獨此作發得心源透徹且詞語精潔無疵非淺
學可易到者
同考試官郎中南　批　至誠功用之盛發明
殆盡且文詞簡質簡潔可以式矣
===
考試官左諭德汪　批　講意透徹
中庸於至誠之功用而極贊其為至焉蓋功用
者以誠而發者也誠至而功用亦至矣此中庸
所以極致其贊歟且其意若謂理之在人其用
為道其體為性其原為命也至誠無所倚而渾
全之矣而功用一何至耶今夫道也者天下之
大經也而能經綸焉其心之仁殆不得而閑已
吾知惇厚以敘人倫而德意為之融徹懇惻以
和民紀而愛心自爾流通其辨異也非其私為
punctuated:
肫肫其仁，淵淵其淵，浩浩其天。
汪文輝
同考試官教授陳批：措詞精確，《中庸》義如此者最難得。
同考試官署郎中劉批：至誠天道，最難形容，獨此作發得心源透徹，且詞語精潔無疵，非淺學可易到者。
同考試官郎中南批：至誠功用之盛，發明殆盡，且文詞簡質簡潔，可以式矣。
考試官左諭德汪批：講意透徹。
《中庸》於至誠之功用，而極贊其為至焉。蓋功用者，以誠而發者也；誠至，而功用亦至矣。此《中庸》所以極致其贊歟？且其意若謂：理之在人，其用為道，其體為性，其原為命也。至誠無所倚而渾全之矣，而功用一何至耶！今夫道也者，天下之大經也，而能經綸焉，其心之仁殆不得而閑已。吾知惇厚以敘人倫，而德意為之融徹；懇惻以和民紀，而愛心自爾流通。其辨異也，非其私為
translation_en:
“How earnest his benevolence, how deep his profundity, how vast his Heaven.”
Wang Wenhui
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The wording is precise. An exposition of the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean such as this is exceedingly rare.”
Associate Examiner Liu, Acting Director, comments: “Utmost sincerity—the Way of Heaven—is exceedingly difficult to describe. This composition alone elucidates the wellspring of the mind with penetrating clarity. Moreover, its language is refined, concise, and flawless: this is no level that someone of shallow learning could readily attain.”
Associate Examiner Nan, Director, comments: “The abundant efficacy of utmost sincerity is elucidated almost exhaustively. Moreover, the language is concise, unadorned, and lucid; it may serve as a model.”
Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher, comments: “The meaning is expounded with penetrating clarity.”
The Doctrine of the Mean praises the efficacy of utmost sincerity to the highest degree, declaring it supreme. For efficacy is what issues from sincerity; when sincerity reaches its utmost, its efficacy likewise reaches its utmost. Is this why the Doctrine of the Mean carries its praise to such a height? Its meaning seems to be this: principle, as present in human beings, is the Way in its operation, human nature in its substance, and Heaven’s mandate in its source. The person of utmost sincerity comprehends it in its wholeness without relying on anything else. How consummate, then, is his efficacy!
Now the Way is the great ordering framework of all under Heaven. Since he can order and arrange it, the benevolence of his mind can scarcely be bounded. I understand that, through generosity and earnestness, he sets human relationships in order, and his virtuous intentions permeate them throughout; through heartfelt concern, he brings harmony to the ordering bonds among the people, and his loving heart naturally flows freely. When he distinguishes differences, it is not that he arbitrarily makes …

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之分也其統同也非其私爲之合也肫肫乎其
仁焉爾矣至哉其盡道乎性也者天下之大本
也而能立焉其心之淵殆不得而窺已吾知無
欲而靜萬變悉具於深微有主而虛萬化悉涵
於宥密無所感也澄其源而不淆也有所感也
沛其用而不滯也淵淵乎其淵焉爾矣至哉其
盡性乎命也者天地之化育而性道所從以出
者也於此而能知焉其心之天殆不得而限量
已吾知妙陰陽於無始而形器不能拘會動靜
===
於無端而法象不能囿道天道也即推行有漸
者焉性天性也即合一不測者焉浩浩乎其天
焉爾矣至哉其至於命乎夫道盡而心極於和
矣性盡而心極於中矣命至而心極於理之太
原矣聖人天道之極致也如此夫雖然此非有
加於吾心也吾心之初一仁也淵也天也欲以
蔽之則純者漓深者窒而廣大者隘至誠非有
加於吾心也不失其初焉耳學者反諸其初而
不疚於動以復道焉不愧於靜以存性焉不顯
punctuated: 之分也，其統同也，非其私爲之合也。肫肫乎其仁焉爾矣！至哉，其盡道乎！性也者，天下之大本也，而能立焉，其心之淵殆不得而窺已。吾知無欲而靜，萬變悉具於深微；有主而虛，萬化悉涵於宥密。無所感也，澄其源而不淆也；有所感也，沛其用而不滯也。淵淵乎其淵焉爾矣！至哉，其盡性乎！命也者，天地之化育，而性道所從以出者也。於此而能知焉，其心之天殆不得而限量已。吾知妙陰陽於無始，而形器不能拘；會動靜於無端，而法象不能囿。道，天道也，即推行有漸者焉；性，天性也，即合一不測者焉。浩浩乎其天焉爾矣！至哉，其至於命乎！夫道盡而心極於和矣，性盡而心極於中矣，命至而心極於理之太原矣。聖人天道之極致也，如此夫！雖然，此非有加於吾心也。吾心之初，一仁也，淵也，天也。欲以蔽之，則純者漓，深者窒，而廣大者隘。至誠非有加於吾心也，不失其初焉耳。學者反諸其初，而不疚於動以復道焉，不愧於靜以存性焉，不顯
translation_en: …divisions of his own private making; when he brings things together in unity, their union is likewise not of his own private making. Such is the earnest sincerity of his benevolence! How consummately he fulfills the Way! Human nature is the great foundation of all under Heaven, and he can establish it. The depth of his mind can scarcely be fathomed. I know that, free from desire and still, it contains every transformation within its profound subtlety; possessing an inner master yet empty, it embraces every change within its quiet depths. When nothing stirs it, its source remains clear and unmuddied; when something stirs it, its activity flows abundantly and without obstruction. Such is the unfathomable depth of his profundity! How consummately he fulfills human nature! Heaven’s mandate is the transforming and nourishing activity of Heaven and Earth, from which human nature and the Way emerge. He can understand this, and the heavenlike character of his mind can scarcely be bounded or measured. I know that he apprehends the subtle workings of yin and yang beyond any beginning, unconstrained by physical forms; he comprehends the convergence of movement and stillness beyond any starting point, unrestricted by patterns and images. The Way is Heaven’s Way: that which unfolds in an ordered progression. Human nature is Heaven-endowed nature: that which unites as one beyond all fathoming. Such is his vast, heavenlike expanse! How consummately he reaches Heaven’s mandate! When the Way is fulfilled, the mind attains the utmost harmony; when human nature is fulfilled, the mind attains the utmost equilibrium; when Heaven’s mandate is reached, the mind attains the ultimate source of principle. Such is the sage’s consummate realization of Heaven’s Way! Yet this adds nothing to our mind. In its original state, our mind is wholly benevolent, profound, and heavenlike. When desires obscure it, what was pure becomes diluted, what was deep becomes obstructed, and what was vast becomes confined. Perfect sincerity adds nothing to our mind: it merely preserves its original state. Learners return to that original state, remaining free of remorse in activity so as to recover the Way, and free of shame in stillness so as to preserve their nature; in what is unmanifest…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而乎於天載以復命焉則所謂其仁其淵其天
者咸在我矣
我非堯舜之道不敢以陳於王前
沈位
同考試官教諭陳　批〔說孟子敬君之意詞旨懇切〕
〔然溢於言表〕
同考試官署郎中沈　批〔發孟子語意剴切明〕
〔到意必自重之士〕
考試官左諭德汪　批〔明暢〕
===
大賢以法古之治期其君敬其君者也蓋治法
堯舜治之至也大賢以是而望其君其異乎世
俗之事君者矣昔孟子曉景丑氏之意若曰言
聖者必以堯舜爲準而言治者必以唐虞爲極
故後王舍是無以爲法人臣舍是無以告君者
矣何則大哉堯也治隆於千古而蕩乎民莫能
名君哉舜也功盛於百王而巍乎世莫能及我
則以堯舜之聖爲可必至而所以敷陳於左右
者必稽其用中之迹以唐虞之治爲可必復而
punctuated:
而乎於天載，以復命焉，則所謂其仁、其淵、其天者咸在我矣。

我非堯舜之道，不敢以陳於王前。
沈位
同考試官教諭陳，批〔說孟子敬君之意，詞旨懇切〕〔然溢於言表。〕
同考試官署郎中沈，批〔發孟子語意，剴切明〕〔到，意必自重之士。〕
考試官左諭德汪，批〔明暢。〕

大賢以法古之治期其君，敬其君者也。蓋治法堯舜，治之至也。大賢以是而望其君，其異乎世俗之事君者矣。昔孟子曉景丑氏之意，若曰：「言聖者必以堯舜爲準，而言治者必以唐虞爲極。故後王舍是，無以爲法；人臣舍是，無以告君者矣。何則？大哉堯也！治隆於千古，而蕩乎民莫能名。君哉舜也！功盛於百王，而巍乎世莫能及。我則以堯舜之聖爲可必至，而所以敷陳於左右者，必稽其用中之迹；以唐虞之治爲可必復，而
translation_en:
…and accords [?] with the workings of Heaven, thereby recovering one's Heaven-conferred mandate; then what are called its benevolence, its depth, and its Heaven-like vastness are all within me.

“Unless it is the Way of Yao and Shun, I dare not set it forth before the king.”
Shen Wei
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔The account of Mencius's intention to respect his ruler is earnest in wording and purport〕〔and conveys more than the words themselves express [?].〕
Associate Examiner Shen, Acting Director, comments: 〔It develops the meaning of Mencius's words incisively and clearly〕〔and thoroughly; I judge that the writer must be a man who respects himself.〕
Examiner Wang, Left Exhorter of Virtue, comments: 〔Clear and fluent.〕

The great worthy expects his ruler to govern on the model of antiquity: this is to respect his ruler. For government that takes Yao and Shun as its models is government at its highest. In holding this expectation for his ruler, the great worthy differs indeed from those who serve rulers in the ordinary worldly manner. Formerly, when Mencius explained his meaning to Jing Chou, it was as though he said: “Those who speak of sages must take Yao and Shun as their standard, and those who speak of government must take Tang and Yu as its highest exemplars. Thus, if later kings abandon these, they have no model to follow; if ministers abandon these, they have nothing with which to instruct their rulers. Why is this? Great indeed was Yao! His government surpassed that of all ages, so boundless that the people could find no name for it. Truly a ruler was Shun! His achievements surpassed those of the hundred kings, so lofty that none in the world could equal them. I regard the sagehood of Yao and Shun as assuredly attainable; thus, whatever I set forth in the king's presence must draw upon the precedents of their putting the Mean into practice. I regard the government of Tang and Yu as assuredly recoverable, and …

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
所以納誨於朝夕者必本其協和之化固嘗告
以養民之道矣而所以分田制畝以遂其生者
非堯舜育民之仁乎外此寧默焉而不敢盡其
言也固嘗啓以教民之道矣而所以立學明倫
以復其性者非堯舜正民之義乎外此寧訥焉
而不敢畢其說也是將舉明王於二帝之隆而
不牽於流俗之見躋斯世於雍熙之盛而不狥
於駁雜之言我之所以事君者如是而已彼狃
於近功而昧格心之要旨規於小利而忘經國
===
之遠猷者則安敢以是售吾之說而瀆君之聽
哉是蓋以堯舜期其君而不以世俗待其君敬
君之大何以加此彼齊人之事君徒以貌而不
以心者亦獨何哉大抵孟子之言所以發明性
善之旨初無二說蓋堯舜之性本與人同而仁
義之道皆其所固有也他日遏惠王之言利對
滕君之論性率由此道固其平日所自許者故
歷聘諸侯而卒未嘗變也噫若孟子者可謂有
功於堯舜矣
punctuated:
所以納誨於朝夕者，必本其協和之化。固嘗告以養民之道矣，而所以分田制畝以遂其生者，非堯舜育民之仁乎？外此，寧默焉而不敢盡其言也。固嘗啓以教民之道矣，而所以立學明倫以復其性者，非堯舜正民之義乎？外此，寧訥焉而不敢畢其說也。是將舉明王於二帝之隆，而不牽於流俗之見；躋斯世於雍熙之盛，而不狥於駁雜之言。我之所以事君者，如是而已。彼狃於近功而昧格心之要旨，規於小利而忘經國之遠猷者，則安敢以是售吾之說而瀆君之聽哉？是蓋以堯舜期其君，而不以世俗待其君，敬君之大，何以加此？彼齊人之事君，徒以貌而不以心者，亦獨何哉？
大抵孟子之言，所以發明性善之旨，初無二說。蓋堯舜之性，本與人同，而仁義之道，皆其所固有也。他日遏惠王之言利，對滕君之論性，率由此道，固其平日所自許者，故歷聘諸侯而卒未嘗變也。噫！若孟子者，可謂有功於堯舜矣。
translation_en:
…and the admonitions I offer morning and evening must be grounded in their transforming influence, which brought all into harmony. I have indeed instructed the ruler in the way to nourish the people. Is not the division of fields and regulation of allotments to secure their livelihoods precisely the benevolence with which Yao and Shun nurtured the people? Beyond this, I would rather remain silent than dare give full expression to my words. I have indeed enlightened him on the way to educate the people. Is not the establishment of schools and clarification of human relationships to restore their original nature precisely the righteousness with which Yao and Shun set the people right? Beyond this, I would rather be inarticulate than dare expound my views in full. My purpose is to raise an enlightened king to the eminence of the Two Emperors, without being drawn aside by conventional views, and to bring this age to the fullness of harmony and prosperity, without yielding to confused and impure doctrines. This alone is how I serve my ruler. As for being habituated to immediate achievements while failing to grasp the essential purpose of rectifying the ruler’s heart, or being confined to petty gains while forgetting long-range plans for governing the state—how could I dare use such things to win acceptance for my views and profane my ruler’s hearing? This means expecting one’s ruler to become a Yao or Shun, rather than treating him according to worldly convention. What greater reverence for a ruler could there be? What, then, are we to make of those men of Qi who serve their ruler merely with outward appearances, rather than with their hearts?
In general, Mengzi’s words elucidate the principle that human nature is good; his teaching was never divided on this point. The nature of Yao and Shun was fundamentally the same as that of other people, and the way of benevolence and righteousness was inherent in them all. On other occasions, when he checked King Hui’s talk of profit and answered the ruler of Teng on human nature, he consistently followed this way. This was indeed the commitment he had always professed; thus, throughout his travels to the courts of the feudal lords, he never once changed it. Ah! A man such as Mengzi may truly be said to have rendered service to Yao and Shun.

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
易
利有攸往中正有慶
俞忭南
同考試官教授陳　批　敷衍明白而語有照
應益卦之旨無餘藴矣
同考試官署郎中劉　批　講中正切當深得益
卦之義
同考試官郎中南　批　理致精到體格莊嚴
易義之冣佳者
===
考試官左諭德汪　批　簡潔得體
彖傳釋益民之利而推本於君臣同德焉甚矣
上下交而德業成也益之二五咸有一德則卦
辭攸往之利有由然哉夫子彖傳之意若謂君
子之立政也固以厚下之澤爲先而尤以中正
之德爲本繫益之辭而曰利有攸往者蓋言德
施普於無方而駿惠之所流者初無疆域之殊
膏澤濡於廣運而宏恩之所究者初無彼此之
間至德深入於人心而无疆之說於此乎得之
punctuated:
易

利有攸往，中正有慶。

俞忭南

同考試官教授陳批：敷衍明白，而語有照應，益卦之旨無餘藴矣。

同考試官署郎中劉批：講中正切當，深得益卦之義。

同考試官郎中南批：理致精到，體格莊嚴，易義之冣佳者。

考試官左諭德汪批：簡潔得體。

彖傳釋益民之利，而推本於君臣同德焉。甚矣，上下交而德業成也！益之二五咸有一德，則卦辭攸往之利有由然哉！夫子彖傳之意，若謂君子之立政也，固以厚下之澤爲先，而尤以中正之德爲本。繫益之辭而曰「利有攸往」者，蓋言德施普於無方，而駿惠之所流者，初無疆域之殊；膏澤濡於廣運，而宏恩之所究者，初無彼此之間。至德深入於人心，而无疆之說於此乎得之，
translation_en:
Book of Changes

“It is beneficial to have somewhere to go: centrality and correctness bring blessings.”

Yu Biannan

Associate Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “The exposition is clear, and its expressions echo one another. Nothing of the purport of the hexagram Increase is left unexplored.”

Associate Examiner Liu, Acting Bureau Director, comments: “The discussion of centrality and correctness is precise and apt, grasping deeply the meaning of the hexagram Increase.”

Associate Examiner Nan, Bureau Director, comments: “The reasoning is refined and penetrating, and the composition dignified: one of the finest essays on the meaning of the Changes.”

Examiner Wang, Left Mentor, comments: “Concise, lucid, and appropriate in form.”

The Commentary on the Judgments explains the benefits of enriching the people and traces their source to ruler and ministers sharing the same virtue. How profound it is that interaction between those above and those below brings virtuous accomplishments to fruition! Since the second and fifth lines of Increase share one virtue, surely there is a reason for the benefit of going somewhere described in the hexagram statement! The Master's meaning in the Commentary on the Judgments seems to be that, when the gentleman establishes government, he certainly gives priority to beneficence that enriches those below, but takes the virtue of centrality and correctness as its essential foundation. The words attached to Increase say, “It is beneficial to have somewhere to go.” This means that the bestowal of virtue extends everywhere without restriction, and the flow of great bounty recognizes no distinctions between territories; nourishing beneficence permeates the vast expanse, and the reach of generous grace makes no distinction between here and there. Supreme virtue enters deeply into people's hearts, and thereby boundless joy is attained …

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
蓋有推無不準動無不化者矣聲教旁達於九
圍而大光之道於此乎基之蓋有近則不遺遠
則不禦者矣卦辭之宜於益民如此果何修而
獲此哉蓋益之爲卦也五以中正應二得君道
焉二以中正應五得臣道焉是君臣同德而所
以綏猷出治者莫非大中至正之矩上下一心
而所以勑法和民者悉皆無偏無黨之政則精
神孚契而謀慮相從建中之治由此出焉而仁
恩之布自交慶於四方也情意感通而休美並
===
濟表正之化由此洽焉而福慶之隆自覃敷於
無外也如是而往其利也寧有窮乎蓋有是君
臣故有是政教有是中正之德具於心故有是
中正之治及於民也否則其體不立無以爲出
治之本而欲其益民也難矣抑天道無私聖人
體之以益天下故存之而爲天德達之而爲王
道其致一也使有一毫私曲存乎其間則與天
道不相似而所謂益民者不過驩虞小惠而已
故曰有天德便可語王道此又益民之大旨也
punctuated: 蓋有推無不準、動無不化者矣。聲教旁達於九圍，而大光之道於此乎基之，蓋有近則不遺、遠則不禦者矣。卦辭之宜於益民如此，果何修而獲此哉？蓋益之爲卦也，五以中正應二，得君道焉；二以中正應五，得臣道焉。是君臣同德，而所以綏猷出治者，莫非大中至正之矩；上下一心，而所以勑法和民者，悉皆無偏無黨之政。則精神孚契，而謀慮相從，建中之治由此出焉，而仁恩之布自交慶於四方也；情意感通，而休美並濟，表正之化由此洽焉，而福慶之隆自覃敷於無外也。如是而往，其利也寧有窮乎？蓋有是君臣，故有是政教；有是中正之德具於心，故有是中正之治及於民也。否則，其體不立，無以爲出治之本，而欲其益民也難矣。抑天道無私，聖人體之以益天下，故存之而爲天德，達之而爲王道，其致一也。使有一毫私曲存乎其間，則與天道不相似，而所謂益民者，不過驩虞小惠而已。故曰：「有天德便可語王道。」此又益民之大旨也。
translation_en:
…Indeed, wherever this virtue is extended, it accords with the proper standard; whenever it acts, it brings transformation. The ruler’s moral influence and teaching reach throughout the nine regions, and here the way of great radiance finds its foundation: those nearby are not neglected, and those far away are not turned away. Such is the hexagram statement’s account of what conduces to benefiting the people. Through what cultivation can this actually be attained?

In the hexagram Increase (Yi), the fifth line responds to the second with centrality and correctness, thus fulfilling the way of the ruler; the second responds to the fifth with centrality and correctness, thus fulfilling the way of the minister. Ruler and minister therefore share one virtue, and everything through which they establish their plans and bring forth good government conforms to the standards of perfect centrality and utmost correctness. Those above and below are of one mind, and everything through which they put laws in order and harmonize the people constitutes government free of partiality and faction. Their spirits accord in mutual trust, and their deliberations converge. Government that establishes the mean arises from this, and the spread of benevolence and kindness naturally brings shared rejoicing throughout the four quarters. Their feelings and intentions communicate sympathetically, and their admirable qualities work together. The transforming influence of setting an upright example thus spreads everywhere, and abundant blessings naturally extend to all, leaving none outside. Proceeding in this manner, could the benefits ever be exhausted?

It is because there are such rulers and ministers that there are such government and teaching. It is because this virtue of centrality and correctness is fully present in their hearts that government embodying centrality and correctness reaches the people. Otherwise, its essential foundation is not established, and there is no basis from which to bring forth good government. To seek to benefit the people under such circumstances would indeed be difficult.

Moreover, the Way of Heaven is impartial. The sage embodies it to benefit all under Heaven. Thus, preserved within, it constitutes heavenly virtue; extended outward, it constitutes the kingly way. Their ultimate principle is one. If the slightest trace of selfishness or crookedness remains within, one no longer accords with the Way of Heaven, and what is called benefiting the people amounts merely to pleasing them with petty favors. Hence the saying: “Only with heavenly virtue can one speak of the kingly way.” This, too, is a fundamental principle of benefiting the people.

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
圖治者於此求之始得
範圍天地之化而不過曲成萬物而不遺
汪文輝
同考試官教授陳　批〔說至命之義甚親切必邃養之士〕
同考試官署郎中劉　批〔詞不費而理自足亦易義之精潔者宜錄以式〕
同考試官郎中南　批〔以中和位育發明聖人以易至命之妙殆非淺學可及者〕
===
考試官左諭德汪　批〔發揮詳盡〕
聖人用易而贊化育則與命爲一矣蓋化育者
命所在也聖人以易贊之謂一於命也非歟今
夫命者理性之原也運於天地通於萬物而具
於聖人之心者也聖人心用乎易而窮理盡性
矣容有間於命耶彼天地之化以氣而行氣無
窮其化亦無窮何以盡協於中也聖人即易體
天地之撰者而範圍焉仰觀陰陽之變節宣之
而弗偏俯察剛柔之常裁畫之而弗紊推焉測
punctuated:
圖治者於此求之，始得。

範圍天地之化而不過，曲成萬物而不遺。
汪文輝

同考試官教授陳　批〔說至命之義甚親切，必邃養之士。〕
同考試官署郎中劉　批〔詞不費而理自足，亦易義之精潔者，宜錄以式。〕
同考試官郎中南　批〔以中和位育發明聖人以易至命之妙，殆非淺學可及者。〕
考試官左諭德汪　批〔發揮詳盡。〕

聖人用易而贊化育，則與命爲一矣。蓋化育者，命所在也。聖人以易贊之，謂一於命也，非歟？今夫命者，理性之原也，運於天地，通於萬物，而具於聖人之心者也。聖人心用乎易而窮理盡性矣，容有間於命耶？彼天地之化以氣而行，氣無窮，其化亦無窮，何以盡協於中也？聖人即易體天地之撰者而範圍焉，仰觀陰陽之變，節宣之而弗偏；俯察剛柔之常，裁畫之而弗紊。推焉，測
translation_en:
…Only by seeking here can those who aspire to good government attain it.

“He encompasses the transformations of Heaven and Earth without exceeding their bounds, and brings the myriad things to fulfillment in all their particularities without omitting any.”
By Wang Wenhui.

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔His explanation of the meaning of attaining Heaven’s mandate is exceptionally apt and incisive. He must be a man of profound self-cultivation.〕
Associate Examiner Liu, Acting Bureau Director, comments: 〔The wording is economical, yet the reasoning is complete in itself. This, too, is a refined and lucid exposition of the meaning of the Changes; it should be recorded as a model.〕
Associate Examiner Nan, Bureau Director, comments: 〔Through equilibrium and harmony, Heaven and Earth taking their proper places, and the myriad things being nourished, he elucidates the subtle way in which the sage attains Heaven’s mandate through the Changes. This is surely beyond the reach of shallow learning.〕
Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher, comments: 〔The exposition is thorough and exhaustive.〕

When the sage employs the Changes to assist transformation and nourishment, he becomes one with Heaven’s mandate. For transformation and nourishment are where that mandate resides. When the sage assists them through the Changes, does this not mean that he is at one with the mandate? Now, the mandate is the source of principle and nature. It operates throughout Heaven and Earth, pervades the myriad things, and is fully present in the sage’s mind. When the sage applies his mind through the Changes, exhaustively investigating principle and fully realizing nature, how could any separation from the mandate remain?

The transformations of Heaven and Earth proceed through vital force. Vital force is inexhaustible, and their transformations are likewise inexhaustible. How can they all be brought into accord with equilibrium? The sage draws upon the Changes, which embodies the workings of Heaven and Earth, to encompass them. Looking upward, he observes the changes of yin and yang, regulating and giving expression to them without partiality; looking downward, he examines the constant patterns of the firm and the yielding, defining and ordering them without confusion. He extends them and fathoms …

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
焉其度明也疆焉理焉其紀正也而範圍所施
無或過矣非範圍於吾也範圍於易也聖人不
能外易以爲中天地不能外易以爲位易其聖
人所以參天地者乎萬物之育以氣而順氣弗
齊其育亦弗齊何以盡恊於和也聖人即易類
萬物之情者而曲成焉緣人以治人而教養之
制備因物以付物而保愛之道周樂樂利利得
其所也形形色色遂其生也而曲成所及無或
遺矣非曲成於吾也曲成於易也聖人不能外
===
易以爲和萬物不能外易以爲育易其聖人所
以宰萬物者乎夫參天地則命在天地者自我
而流行也宰萬物則命在萬物者自我而賦予
也聖人以易至命如此易之大也信哉雖然易
易也聖人之心亦易也是故統而天地散而萬
物一理也心所圍也大而範圍小而曲成一事
也心所爲也窮理盡性之極也非窮理盡性外
有所謂至命也人惟自小其心乃謂命不可至
宜乎以卜筮視易也
punctuated: 焉，其度明也；疆焉，理焉，其紀正也。而範圍所施，無或過矣。非範圍於吾也，範圍於易也。聖人不能外易以爲中，天地不能外易以爲位。易其聖人所以參天地者乎！萬物之育，以氣而順；氣弗齊，其育亦弗齊，何以盡恊於和也？聖人即易類萬物之情者而曲成焉。緣人以治人，而教養之制備；因物以付物，而保愛之道周。樂樂利利，得其所也；形形色色，遂其生也。而曲成所及，無或遺矣。非曲成於吾也，曲成於易也。聖人不能外易以爲和，萬物不能外易以爲育。易其聖人所以宰萬物者乎！夫參天地，則命在天地者，自我而流行也；宰萬物，則命在萬物者，自我而賦予也。聖人以易至命如此，易之大也，信哉！雖然，易，易也；聖人之心，亦易也。是故統而天地，散而萬物，一理也，心所圍也；大而範圍，小而曲成，一事也，心所爲也。窮理盡性之極也，非窮理盡性外有所謂至命也。人惟自小其心，乃謂命不可至，宜乎以卜筮視易也。
translation_en:
… its measures are made clear; by setting boundaries and ordering them, its guiding framework is set right. Thus, wherever this encompassing and regulation extend, nothing exceeds its proper bounds. This encompassing and regulation rest not on my own self, but on the Changes. The sage cannot attain centrality apart from the Changes, nor can Heaven and Earth take their proper places apart from it. Is not the Changes the means by which the sage forms a triad with Heaven and Earth?

The growth of the myriad things follows the course of vital energy. Since vital energy is unequal, their growth is likewise unequal. How can it all accord with harmony? The sage draws upon the Changes, which classifies the actual dispositions of the myriad things, and brings each to fulfillment according to its particular circumstances. Governing people in accordance with their humanity, he makes complete the institutions for educating and nourishing them; assigning things their due in accordance with their nature, he makes comprehensive the way of protecting and cherishing them. Taking delight in what delights them and benefiting from what benefits them, they obtain their proper places; each with its own form and color, they fulfill their lives. Thus, wherever this particularized fulfillment extends, nothing is omitted. This fulfillment rests not on my own self, but on the Changes. The sage cannot achieve harmony apart from the Changes, nor can the myriad things grow apart from it. Is not the Changes the means by which the sage governs the myriad things?

In forming a triad with Heaven and Earth, the heavenly mandate present in Heaven and Earth flows forth through me; in governing the myriad things, the mandate present in the myriad things is imparted through me. Such is the sage’s attainment of the heavenly mandate through the Changes. Great indeed is the Changes! Nevertheless, the Changes is change, and the sage’s mind is also change. Thus, taken together as Heaven and Earth or dispersed as the myriad things, all is one principle, encompassed by the mind. Encompassing and regulating on the grand scale, and bringing each thing to fulfillment on the small scale, are one undertaking, performed by the mind. This is the culmination of fathoming principle and fully realizing nature; there is no separate attainment of the heavenly mandate beyond fathoming principle and fully realizing nature. Only because people belittle their own minds do they say that the heavenly mandate cannot be attained. No wonder they regard the Changes merely as a book of divination!

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
書
山川鬼神亦莫不寧暨鳥獸魚鼈咸若
沈位

考試官左諭德汪　批〔典雅之作〕
大臣敘聖世之休徵望時王以懋德也甚矣惟
===
德動天也德懋而天休應矣此有夏之盛而伊
尹爲太甲望歟意曰治化以得天而隆治道以
法古而善觀夏后之得天而商知所法矣且天
地之氣無大不包山川得之融結鬼神得之變
通而人得之以參贊者也惟德不足以格天則
乖氣相乘胥失其位矣夏德之懋也不惟時罔
有災已爾吾知明與山川同其動靜而至精所
達安流峙之常幽與鬼神合其吉凶而至誠所
孚協屈伸之正剛柔不易其道恒也陰陽不測
punctuated:
書

山川鬼神亦莫不寧，暨鳥獸魚鼈咸若。

沈位

同考試官教諭陳　批〔以豊腴之詞抒寫盛世功化之美，非積學之士不能。〕
同考試官署郎中沈　批〔措詞雅醇，而意復融暢，盛世太平氣象宛然可覩，經義之最佳者。〕
考試官左諭德汪　批〔典雅之作。〕

大臣敘聖世之休徵，望時王以懋德也。甚矣，惟德動天也！德懋而天休應矣。此有夏之盛，而伊尹爲太甲望歟？意曰：治化以得天而隆，治道以法古而善。觀夏后之得天，而商知所法矣。且天地之氣，無大不包，山川得之融結，鬼神得之變通，而人得之以參贊者也。惟德不足以格天，則乖氣相乘，胥失其位矣。夏德之懋也，不惟時罔有災已爾。吾知明與山川同其動靜，而至精所達，安流峙之常；幽與鬼神合其吉凶，而至誠所孚，協屈伸之正。剛柔不易，其道恒也；陰陽不測
translation_en:
Book of Documents

“The mountains, rivers, and spirits were likewise all at peace, and the birds, beasts, fish, and turtles all fared well.”

Shen Wei

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “He uses rich and ample language to convey the beauty of the achievements and transforming influence of a flourishing age. Only a scholar of accumulated learning could accomplish this.”
Associate Examiner Shen, Acting Director, comments: “The diction is elegant and pure, and the meaning flows freely and coherently. The atmosphere of peace in a flourishing age is vividly apparent. This is among the finest essays interpreting the Classics.”
Examiner Wang, Left Mentor, comments: “A work of classical elegance.”

A great minister recounts the auspicious signs of a sage’s age, hoping that the reigning king will exert himself in virtue. How profound it is that virtue alone moves Heaven! When virtue flourishes, Heaven responds with blessings. Was this not the flourishing condition of the Xia that Yi Yin hoped Tai Jia would attain? His meaning was this: transformative government flourishes by winning Heaven’s favor, and the way of governing becomes good by emulating antiquity. By observing how the sovereigns of Xia won Heaven’s favor, Shang would know what to emulate.

Now, the vital energy of Heaven and Earth encompasses everything, however great. Mountains and rivers receive it to coalesce and take form; spirits receive it to transform and circulate; human beings receive it to participate in and assist the workings of Heaven and Earth.
