The Book of Changes says: “Heaven and Earth interact, and the myriad things communicate; those above and below interact, and their purposes are united.” The interaction of vital energies and the free communication of things constitute the harmony of Heaven and Earth; the interaction of hearts and unity of purpose constitute harmony in human affairs. Thus, to understand the Way of Heaven and Earth is to understand the Way of ruler and minister. From antiquity, those who have spoken of flourishing government have cited Tang and Yu—the ages of Yao and Shun—and the Three Dynasties. Among the words of mutual admonition in those times were these: “If I err, correct me; do not merely assent to my face.” And: “Attend reverently to Heaven’s…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之命維時維幾曰各守爾典以承天休其
所以勉飭乎臣者何至哉曰儆戒無虞罔
失法度曰夙夜罔或不勤曰王敬作所不
可不敬德其所以規警乎君者何切哉君
有以信乎其下臣有以說乎其上形迹相
忘油然如家人父子精神貫徹驩然如手
足腹心由是禮備樂和而萬事皆得其宜
道洽政治而萬物各止其所至德達於神
明宏業敷於海宇和氣薰蒸而休徵協應
===
至順洋溢而災沴潛消治效之隆粹乎無
以復加也裔是而降此道浸微其間英君
賢佐雖知勉於治業之修而志睽情離終
阻於勢分之隔槩以賡歌勸相之風則藐
乎其不相及也彼賈生在漢嘗策治安以
進於帝矣魏徵在唐嘗疏十漸以戒其主
矣司馬光在宋嘗規五事以勸其君矣然
宣室之召未幾而竟阸於梁藩之行弦韋
之喻雖切而未釋於停婚之謗入相之任
punctuated:
之命，維時維幾。」曰：「各守爾典，以承天休。」其所以勉飭乎臣者何至哉！曰：「儆戒無虞，罔失法度。」曰：「夙夜罔或不勤。」曰：「王敬作所，不可不敬德。」其所以規警乎君者何切哉！君有以信乎其下，臣有以說乎其上，形迹相忘，油然如家人父子；精神貫徹，驩然如手足腹心。由是禮備樂和，而萬事皆得其宜；道洽政治，而萬物各止其所。至德達於神明，宏業敷於海宇，和氣薰蒸而休徵協應，至順洋溢而災沴潛消。治效之隆，粹乎無以復加也。
裔是而降，此道浸微。其間英君賢佐，雖知勉於治業之修，而志睽情離，終阻於勢分之隔。槩以賡歌勸相之風，則藐乎其不相及也。彼賈生在漢，嘗策治安以進於帝矣；魏徵在唐，嘗疏十漸以戒其主矣；司馬光在宋，嘗規五事以勸其君矣。然宣室之召未幾，而竟阸於梁藩之行；弦韋之喻雖切，而未釋於停婚之謗；入相之任
translation_en:
…Heaven’s mandate, attending to the times and the slightest incipient changes.” They said: “Let each of you keep to your appointed duties, thereby receiving Heaven’s blessings.” How thoroughly they encouraged and admonished their ministers! The ministers said: “Remain vigilant when there is no cause for concern, and do not depart from the laws and standards.” They said: “Morning and night, never be anything but diligent.” They said: “Let the king reverently establish his place; he must not fail to revere virtue.” How earnestly they admonished and warned their rulers! The ruler won the trust of those below him, and the ministers pleased the sovereign above them. They forgot formal distinctions and outward appearances, naturally resembling fathers and sons within a family. Their spirits were joined throughout, harmoniously united like hands and feet, belly and heart. Thus ritual was complete and music harmonious, and all affairs attained their proper order; the Way prevailed and government was well ordered, and all things rested in their proper places. Their consummate virtue reached the spirits, and their great achievements extended throughout the realm. Harmonious influences suffused all things, and auspicious signs appeared in concert. Perfect accord overflowed, while calamities and baleful influences quietly vanished. The excellence of their government’s results was so pure that nothing could further enhance it.
In subsequent ages, this Way gradually declined. Among those who lived in these times, enlightened rulers and worthy assistants understood that they should strive to perfect the work of government. Yet their purposes diverged and their feelings became estranged; ultimately they were obstructed by the separation imposed by differences of power and station. Measured against the practice of exchanging songs and encouraging and assisting one another, they fell far short. Under the Han, Master Jia submitted to the emperor a policy essay on securing good government and peace. Under the Tang, Wei Zheng presented a memorial on ten gradual failings to admonish his sovereign. Under the Song, Sima Guang offered admonitions on five matters to exhort his ruler. Yet scarcely had Jia been summoned to the Xuanshi Hall before he ultimately suffered the setback of being sent to the princely domain of Liang. Although Wei’s analogy of the bowstring and leather thong was pointed, it did not dispel the slander that led to the cancellation of the marriage alliance. As for Sima Guang’s appointment as chief councillor…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
雖隆而卒遂其乞閑之請要之上之遇其
下也非有一體之誠而臣之事其君也非
有一德之感耳漢晁錯曰五帝神聖其臣
莫及夫不以神聖而忘其交儆之助豈非
望道之心不自滿假歟此古帝王致太和
之盛者此也宋儒程氏曰唐虞之世君臣
交儆其後則多臣戒君耳非謂賡歌之風
漸不及古歟此漢唐而下治止於小康者
此也洪惟我
===
太祖高皇帝稟剛明純懿之資體仁義中正之
德
功闢渾淪治恢熙皡至矣盛矣而其
保邦圖治之心兢惕不已其與諸臣交相儆
戒者可得而言也如
醉學士歌則恩義流通而心膂之寄何重也
君臣同遊之言則勢分脫略而勸勉之意一何
深也與許好問論祈天永命之道則以上
下交修爲格天之本與傅瓛論水旱災異
punctuated:
雖隆，而卒遂其乞閑之請。要之，上之遇其下也，非有一體之誠；而臣之事其君也，非有一德之感耳。漢晁錯曰：「五帝神聖，其臣莫及。」夫不以神聖而忘其交儆之助，豈非望道之心不自滿假歟？此古帝王致太和之盛者，此也。宋儒程氏曰：「唐虞之世，君臣交儆，其後則多臣戒君耳。」非謂賡歌之風漸不及古歟？此漢唐而下治止於小康者，此也。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，稟剛明純懿之資，體仁義中正之德，功闢渾淪，治恢熙皡，至矣，盛矣！而其保邦圖治之心，兢惕不已。其與諸臣交相儆戒者，可得而言也。如《醉學士歌》，則恩義流通，而心膂之寄何重也！君臣同遊之言，則勢分脫略，而勸勉之意一何深也！與許好問論祈天永命之道，則以上下交修爲格天之本；與傅瓛論水旱災異
translation_en:
…though the honor of his appointment as chief councilor was great, in the end his request to retire was granted. In sum, the rulers’ treatment of their subordinates lacked the sincerity of belonging to a single body, while the ministers’ service to their rulers lacked the mutual responsiveness born of shared virtue. Chao Cuo of the Han said: “The Five Emperors were divinely wise and sagely; none of their ministers could equal them.” Yet their divine wisdom and sageliness did not make them forget the aid afforded by mutual admonition. Was this not because, in aspiring to the Way, their hearts were never complacent? This was how the ancient emperors and kings brought about the flourishing of supreme harmony. The Song Confucian Master Cheng said: “In the age of Tang and Yu, ruler and ministers admonished one another; afterward, it was mostly ministers admonishing their ruler.” Does this not mean that the practice of exchanging songs of counsel gradually fell short of antiquity? This was why, from the Han and Tang onward, government attained only a lesser peace.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao possessed an innate firmness, discernment, purity, and excellence, and embodied benevolence, righteousness, centrality, and rectitude. His achievements opened order out of primordial chaos, and his government spread luminous prosperity. How consummate, how magnificent! Yet his concern to safeguard the realm and secure good government remained ceaselessly vigilant. The ways in which he and his ministers admonished one another can be recounted. In the Song of the Drunken Academician, favor and dutiful devotion flowed between them: how weighty the trust placed in a minister as his own heart and limbs! In his words about ruler and ministers traveling together, distinctions of rank were set aside: how profound his intention to encourage and exhort! In discussing with Xu Haowen the way to pray to Heaven for an enduring mandate, he took the mutual cultivation of ruler and ministers as the foundation for moving Heaven. In discussing with Fu Huan floods, droughts, calamities, and anomalies…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之警則以君臣一體爲回天之道與徐達
言紀綱法度而欲交任其責與劉基論堯
舜憂虞而思益致其警其更相淬礪一德
一心雖唐虞君臣之盛何以加此
成祖文皇帝神智出於天授至德冠乎百王
武功肴定函夏謐寧至矣盛矣而其
持盈守成之念慄慄不忘其與諸臣交相儆
戒者可得而知也今觀
訓言所載則明創業守成之難而矻矻於君
===
臣交儆以成天下之治
聖學心法所著則言經歷艱難之迹而惓惓於
勤學敬天以示正心之要
諭大臣以晡時奏納而勉以勤勵之言
命楊士奇編輯奏議而訓以盡忠之說他如
諭朱能以刑賞之要則以徇私爲戒
諭武臣以君臣相與之道則以蓄疑爲戒其
更相警飭上孚下契雖三代君臣之盛何
以異此
punctuated:
之警，則以君臣一體爲回天之道；與徐達言紀綱法度，而欲交任其責；與劉基論堯舜憂虞，而思益致其警。其更相淬礪，一德一心，雖唐虞君臣之盛，何以加此？

成祖文皇帝神智出於天授，至德冠乎百王，武功肴定，函夏謐寧，至矣盛矣！而其持盈守成之念，慄慄不忘。其與諸臣交相儆戒者，可得而知也。今觀《訓言》所載，則明創業守成之難，而矻矻於君臣交儆，以成天下之治；《聖學心法》所著，則言經歷艱難之迹，而惓惓於勤學敬天，以示正心之要。諭大臣以晡時奏納，而勉以勤勵之言；命楊士奇編輯奏議，而訓以盡忠之說。他如諭朱能以刑賞之要，則以徇私爲戒；諭武臣以君臣相與之道，則以蓄疑爲戒。其更相警飭，上孚下契，雖三代君臣之盛，何以異此？
translation_en:
…as warnings, he held that ruler and ministers acting as one was the way to turn Heaven’s course. In speaking with Xu Da about governing principles, laws, and institutions, he wished them to share responsibility for these; in discussing with Liu Ji the cares and apprehensions of Yao and Shun, he sought to heighten his vigilance still further. They honed and tempered one another, united in virtue and purpose. Even the flourishing relations between rulers and ministers in the ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun—how could they surpass this?

Emperor Wen, Chengzu, received his divine wisdom from Heaven, and his consummate virtue surpassed that of all kings. His military achievements secured order [?], and all the Chinese realm was tranquil. How consummate, how flourishing! Yet he never forgot, in his trembling vigilance, the need to preserve prosperity and safeguard what had been achieved. We can discern how he and his ministers admonished and cautioned one another. Looking now at what is recorded in Admonitory Words (Xunyan), we see that he explained the difficulty of founding an enterprise and preserving its achievements, and labored tirelessly to have ruler and ministers admonish one another so as to bring orderly government to the realm. What is set forth in The Essential Method of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa) recounts the hardships he had experienced and earnestly urges diligent study and reverence for Heaven, thereby showing the essentials of rectifying the mind. He instructed the high ministers to present their memorials in the late afternoon, encouraging them with words of diligence and exertion. He ordered Yang Shiqi to compile memorials and admonished him to fulfill his loyalty to the utmost. In other instances, when instructing Zhu Neng on the essentials of punishments and rewards, he warned against favoritism; when instructing military officials on the proper relations between ruler and ministers, he warned against harboring suspicion. They cautioned and admonished one another: sincerity above met with accord below. Even the flourishing relations between rulers and ministers of the Three Dynasties—how did they differ from this?

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承率循無間迨我
皇上神功聖德益有以覲揚而光大之雖
道崇業廣物阜民康治化之極無以復加然
德已盛而心愈虛治已至而功益密
君唱臣和而從容於燕咏之間濟美交歡而感
孚於奏對之頃芳猷偉蹟固難畢數姑舉
其大者言之如著
欽天記以示勑天之戒
答賀雪吟以啓臣鄰之勸見於
===
敬一之箴則有省躬察咎儆戒無虞行顧其
言終如其始之訓見於五箴之註則有觀
邪正諮故實謹號令戒妄動之防無非所
以儆戒臣工也無非所以勉修德業也如
平臺之咏則有君臣一德庶政惟和地天交
泰民物平康之句如衍義之講則有匪徒
知之實欲行之尚賴竭誠協恭輔導朕躬
之諭其
賜輔臣除夕之詩則有華夙衍德興新德交修
punctuated: 列聖相承，率循無間。迨我皇上，神功聖德，益有以覲揚而光大之。雖道崇業廣，物阜民康，治化之極無以復加，然德已盛而心愈虛，治已至而功益密。君唱臣和，而從容於燕咏之間；濟美交歡，而感孚於奏對之頃。芳猷偉蹟，固難畢數，姑舉其大者言之。如著《欽天記》，以示勑天之戒；《答賀雪吟》，以啓臣鄰之勸。見於《敬一》之箴，則有省躬察咎、儆戒無虞、行顧其言、終如其始之訓；見於五箴之註，則有觀邪正、諮故實、謹號令、戒妄動之防。無非所以儆戒臣工也，無非所以勉修德業也。如平臺之咏，則有「君臣一德，庶政惟和，地天交泰，民物平康」之句；如《衍義》之講，則有「匪徒知之，實欲行之，尚賴竭誠協恭，輔導朕躬」之諭。其賜輔臣除夕之詩，則有「華夙衍德，興新德，交修
translation_en:
The successive sage emperors inherited this tradition and followed it without interruption. When it came to our present Emperor, his divine achievements and sagely virtue further exalted and enlarged it. Although his Way is lofty and his accomplishments extensive, goods abundant and the people at ease, and the perfection of his government and transforming influence admits of no further improvement, the fuller his virtue becomes, the humbler his heart; the more consummate his government, the more painstaking his efforts. The ruler leads and his ministers respond, at ease amid leisurely poetic exchanges; they carry forward past excellence and share their joy, attaining mutual trust in the course of memorials and responses at audience. Their admirable counsels and great deeds are indeed too numerous to recount fully; let us mention only the foremost examples.

Thus he composed the Record of Revering Heaven (Qintian ji) to convey an admonition to heed Heaven, and the Poem in Reply to Congratulations on Snow to encourage his close ministers. In the Admonition on Reverent Single-mindedness (Jingyi), there are instructions to examine oneself and scrutinize one’s faults, remain vigilant when no danger is apparent, ensure that conduct accords with words, and finish as one began. In the annotations to the Five Admonitions, there are safeguards: distinguish the crooked from the upright, consult precedents, issue commands circumspectly, and guard against rash action. All these serve to admonish his officials; all serve to encourage the cultivation of virtue and achievement.

Thus the poem on the Platform contains the lines: “Ruler and ministers are of one virtue; the many affairs of government are harmonious; Earth and Heaven interact in grand concord; the people and all things enjoy peace and well-being.” At the lectures on the Extended Meaning (Yanyi), he instructed: “I wish not merely to understand it, but truly to put it into practice. I still rely upon you to exert your utmost sincerity and unite in reverent service, assisting and guiding my person.” His New Year’s Eve poem bestowed upon his grand secretaries contains the words: “Hua su [?], extend virtue, renew virtue, and cultivate it together …

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
不怠斯實朕望之語若此者無非所以儆
戒臣工也無非所以勉修德業也不特此
也稽勤衆任而
綸音屢下於臣鄰裁決萬幾而
札諭日頒於宰輔嘉猷入告則有造膝之陳
召對從容則有燕閒之賜
虛心清問邪謀不得而間之
温顏聽納羣議不得而沮之諸臣之條疏罔
不敷答四方之類奏罔不躬省且歲時之
===
燕賚有加出入之慰勞特至
仁恩優洽情意感通善無微而不錄言無小
而或忘
德懋於交修而功勤於儆戒雖虞廷賡載之
歌周室卷阿之咏無以逾此是不有以媲
德
二聖而邁迹古帝王也哉夫有
謙冲祗畏之念故其德純曜而益彰有
兢惕勤厲之心故其治悠久而不替一時中
punctuated:
不怠，斯實朕望」之語。若此者，無非所以儆戒臣工也，無非所以勉修德業也。不特此也，稽勤衆任，而綸音屢下於臣鄰；裁決萬幾，而札諭日頒於宰輔。嘉猷入告，則有造膝之陳；召對從容，則有燕閒之賜。虛心清問，邪謀不得而間之；温顏聽納，羣議不得而沮之。諸臣之條疏，罔不敷答；四方之類奏，罔不躬省。且歲時之燕賚有加，出入之慰勞特至。仁恩優洽，情意感通，善無微而不錄，言無小而或忘。德懋於交修，而功勤於儆戒。雖虞廷賡載之歌、周室卷阿之咏，無以逾此。是不有以媲德二聖，而邁迹古帝王也哉？

夫有謙冲祗畏之念，故其德純曜而益彰；有兢惕勤厲之心，故其治悠久而不替。一時中
translation_en:
…“without flagging: this is truly what I hope for.” Such words all serve to admonish his officials and encourage them to cultivate virtue and achievement. Nor is this all. He examines diligence in the various offices, repeatedly issuing imperial pronouncements to his attendant ministers; he decides the myriad affairs of state, daily sending written instructions to his chief ministers. When sound counsels are presented, he allows them to be explained at close audience; when he summons ministers for unhurried consultation, he grants them audience in his hours of leisure. He asks discerning questions with an open mind, so that pernicious schemes cannot intrude; he listens and accepts counsel with a kindly countenance, so that opposing opinions cannot thwart it. There is no itemized memorial from his ministers to which he does not fully respond, no collected report from the four quarters that he does not personally examine. Moreover, his seasonal banquets and gifts grow more generous, and his expressions of solicitude for those arriving and departing are especially attentive. His benevolent favor is abundant and pervasive; feelings and intentions pass freely between ruler and ministers. No good deed is too slight to be recorded, no utterance too minor to be remembered. Virtue flourishes through mutual cultivation, and achievement is diligently pursued through admonition. Even the responsive songs at Shun’s court and the Zhou court’s ode Winding Mound (Juan a) cannot surpass this. Does this not enable him to equal the virtue of the two sage rulers and surpass the accomplishments of the emperors and kings of antiquity?

Because he cherishes humility, reverence, and awe, his virtue shines with pure radiance and becomes ever more manifest; because his heart is vigilant, diligent, and resolute, his governance endures without decline. At that time, within …

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
外之臣仰窺
虛抑之懷佩服
交修之訓咸知祓濯心志聚會精神奔走率
職無敢曠越慎於夙夜以明恊恭和衷之
義謹於幾微以盡惠疇亮采之責然而
至德難名
神功莫及思欲敷賁謀猷恢張治術而
聖德淵微之妙
聖學緝熈之純與夫
===
洪厖峻偉之業
昌明熈皥之化固有非諸臣所能仰贊其萬
一者也猗歟盛矣抑愚復有聞焉如日中
天唐虞之治極矣而不忘時幾之勑平成
允殖夏商之治至矣而尤嚴祗敬之規景
命郅隆周室之治盛矣而益勤無逸之警
蓋古之帝王兢兢業業恒以保天下之治
爲難而艱危其思慮貞固其施爲而爲之
臣者張而相之翼而成之酌可否以濟之
punctuated:
外之臣仰窺虛抑之懷，佩服交修之訓，咸知祓濯心志，聚會精神，奔走率職，無敢曠越，慎於夙夜，以明恊恭和衷之義；謹於幾微，以盡惠疇亮采之責。然而至德難名，神功莫及，思欲敷賁謀猷，恢張治術，而聖德淵微之妙、聖學緝熈之純，與夫洪厖峻偉之業、昌明熈皥之化，固有非諸臣所能仰贊其萬一者也。猗歟，盛矣！

抑愚復有聞焉：如日中天，唐虞之治極矣，而不忘時幾之勑；平成允殖，夏商之治至矣，而尤嚴祗敬之規；景命郅隆，周室之治盛矣，而益勤無逸之警。蓋古之帝王兢兢業業，恒以保天下之治爲難，而艱危其思慮，貞固其施爲。而爲之臣者，張而相之，翼而成之，酌可否以濟之，
translation_en:
…officials outside the court reverently discern Your Majesty’s humble and self-effacing intentions and respectfully embrace your instruction to cultivate virtue through mutual assistance. All know to cleanse their hearts and minds, gather their energies, and hasten to fulfill their offices, daring neither to neglect their duties nor to exceed their authority. They remain vigilant morning and night, manifesting the principles of concord in reverence and unity of purpose; they attend carefully to the slightest beginnings of affairs, fulfilling their responsibility to act harmoniously with their colleagues and discharge their duties faithfully. Yet your supreme virtue is difficult to name, and your wondrous achievements are beyond compare. Though your ministers wish to embellish your counsels and extend your methods of government, the profound subtlety of your sagely virtue, the purity of your ever-brightening sagely learning, your vast and lofty achievements, and your brilliant, radiant transforming influence are such that your ministers cannot assist in even one ten-thousandth part of them. Ah, how magnificent!

Yet I, in my ignorance, have also heard this: like the sun at the zenith, the government of Tang and Yu reached its highest point, yet their rulers did not forget the admonition to attend to the incipient workings of affairs. With the world brought into order and growth securely established, the government of Xia and Shang attained perfection, yet their rulers observed the rule of reverence with particular strictness. With Heaven’s great mandate at its most exalted, the government of the house of Zhou flourished, yet its rulers attended still more diligently to the warning against ease. For the emperors and kings of antiquity were ever cautious and conscientious. They always regarded preserving order throughout the realm as difficult, contemplated its hardships and dangers, and remained steadfast in their actions. Those who served as their ministers extended and assisted their work, supported and brought it to completion, and weighed what was acceptable and what was not in order to aid them…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
啓乃心以沃之則庶幾明良相慶上下同
德始於憂勤終於逸樂施之廟堂而澤溥
九垓行之一時而福流萬世也愚生跧伏
草茅粗濡
聖化久矣區區芹縣之忱無由自達敢以古帝
王德業之盛爲
明時獻焉
第二問
陳子忠
===
同考試官教諭張　批　〔教刑異用而隨時救弊則一是篇條析明白區畫精當施之厝理裕〕
同考試官署郎中牛　批　〔政教雖迭相爲用而亦不無本末輕重之殊執此以酌今定古非通如矣〕
〔達治體者不能也〕
同考試官郎中蔡　批　〔條答明悉議論純正且本末輕重卓有定見非留意時務者不能〕
考試官左諭德汪　批　〔說博大明作之意甚切當〕
punctuated:
啓乃心以沃之，則庶幾明良相慶，上下同德，始於憂勤，終於逸樂，施之廟堂而澤溥九垓，行之一時而福流萬世也。愚生跧伏草茅，粗濡聖化久矣。區區芹縣之忱，無由自達，敢以古帝王德業之盛，爲明時獻焉。

第二問
陳子忠

同考試官教諭張，批：〔教刑異用，而隨時救弊則一。是篇條析明白，區畫精當，施之厝理裕〕
同考試官署郎中牛，批：〔政教雖迭相爲用，而亦不無本末輕重之殊。執此以酌今定古，非通如矣〕〔達治體者不能也。〕
同考試官郎中蔡，批：〔條答明悉，議論純正，且本末輕重卓有定見，非留意時務者不能〕
考試官左諭德汪，批：〔說博大明作之意，甚切當。〕
translation_en:
…and open their hearts to nourish him with counsel, then perhaps an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers may rejoice in one another, and those above and below share a common virtue. Beginning with anxious diligence and ending with ease and enjoyment, their work at court will spread its blessings throughout the nine regions; practiced in one age, it will bring good fortune to myriad generations. I, an unworthy scholar living in obscurity among the common people, have long received some measure of the influence of the sage emperor’s transforming rule. With no means of conveying my humble sincerity in offering celery [?], I venture to present this account of the flourishing virtue and achievements of ancient emperors and kings to this enlightened age.

Second Question
Chen Zizhong

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔“Moral instruction and punishments serve different purposes, but they are alike in remedying abuses as circumstances require. This essay analyzes its points clearly and makes precise and appropriate distinctions. Applied to the ordering of affairs, it would amply… [?]”〕

Associate Examiner Niu, Acting Bureau Director, comments: 〔“Government and moral instruction may serve each other in turn, yet there remain distinctions between root and branch, and between greater and lesser importance. To use these distinctions to weigh present circumstances and judge antiquity—without understanding… [?]”〕〔“one cannot do this without comprehending the essentials of government.”〕

Associate Examiner Cai, Bureau Director, comments: 〔“The answers to the individual points are clear and thorough, and the arguments sound and correct. Moreover, the author has firm and outstanding judgments concerning root and branch, and greater and lesser importance. Anyone who does not attend to current affairs cannot…”〕

Examiner Wang, Left Mentor, comments: 〔“The discussion of the meaning of ‘broad and great’ and ‘clear and rousing’ is most apt.”〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
通達治體者
聖王之治天下爲之教以防民僞於將然
也而非徒文也爲之刑以禁民僞於已然
也而非徒令也蓋民習之敝待教而端而
教也者所以飭民之行也實也非以其文
焉而已民僞之滋待刑而禁而刑也者所
以懲民之奸也實也非以其令焉而已以
教之實飭諸始既潛沮其不自制之情以
刑之實懲諸終又深懾其不自抑之氣而
===
民遷善而民遠罪而聖王之治成矣世嘗
病聖王之教之過詳也而不知其飭民者
周也是故以陰禮陽禮教以祀禮樂禮
教焉以俗以誓以度以事教焉而未也州
長各屬其州之民而讀法黨正各屬其黨
之民而讀法族師閭師各屬其族閭之民
而讀法教備矣而倡之自上焉師氏詔王
以三德三行教國子也保氏詔王以六儀
六藝教國子也倡之也不徒文也而後天
punctuated:
通達治體者。
聖王之治天下，爲之教以防民僞於將然也，而非徒文也；爲之刑以禁民僞於已然也，而非徒令也。蓋民習之敝，待教而端，而教也者，所以飭民之行也，實也，非以其文焉而已；民僞之滋，待刑而禁，而刑也者，所以懲民之奸也，實也，非以其令焉而已。以教之實飭諸始，既潛沮其不自制之情；以刑之實懲諸終，又深懾其不自抑之氣，而民遷善，而民遠罪，而聖王之治成矣。世嘗病聖王之教之過詳也，而不知其飭民者周也。是故以陰禮、陽禮教，以祀禮、樂禮教焉，以俗、以誓、以度、以事教焉。而未也，州長各屬其州之民而讀法，黨正各屬其黨之民而讀法，族師、閭師各屬其族閭之民而讀法。教備矣，而倡之自上焉。師氏詔王，以三德、三行教國子也；保氏詔王，以六儀、六藝教國子也。倡之也，不徒文也，而後天
translation_en:
…one who comprehends the principles of governance.
When the sage kings governed the realm, they established instruction to forestall deceit among the people before it arose; this was no mere outward form. They established punishments to restrain deceit once it had arisen; these were no mere commands. Corrupt popular habits require instruction to be corrected. Instruction serves to regulate the people's conduct: it has substance and does not consist merely in outward forms. The proliferation of deceit among the people requires punishments to restrain it. Punishment serves to chastise the people's wrongdoing: it has substance and does not consist merely in commands. By applying substantive instruction to regulate conduct at the outset, the kings quietly checked impulses that the people could not control themselves. By applying substantive punishment to chastise wrongdoing afterward, they also profoundly overawed the unruly spirit that the people could not restrain themselves. Thus the people turned toward goodness and kept far from crime, and the sage kings' governance was accomplished.
People have often criticized the sage kings' instruction as excessively elaborate, failing to understand how comprehensively it regulated the people. Thus they taught through yin rites and yang rites, through sacrificial rites and musical rites, and through customs, solemn injunctions, standards, and duties. Nor was this all. Each District Chief assembled the people of his district and read the laws to them; each Neighborhood Head assembled the people of his neighborhood and read the laws to them; each Clan Master and Neighborhood Master assembled the people of his respective clan or neighborhood and read the laws to them. Instruction was thus complete, yet leadership in it came from above. The Preceptor instructed the king and taught the sons of the state through the three virtues and three forms of conduct. The Guardian instructed the king and taught the sons of the state through the six forms of deportment and six arts. This leadership was no mere outward form. Only then did all under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
下相率而趨吾教又嘗病聖王之刑之過
詳也而不知其懲民者周也是故悖於孝
弟睦婣任卹者刑焉析言破律亂名改作
者刑焉行僞而堅言僞而辨學非而愽順
非而澤者刑焉而未也鄉士掌其鄉之民
數而糾戒遂士掌其遂之民數而糾戒縣
士方士掌其縣方之民而糾戒刑備矣而
愼之自上焉諸侯之獄訟以邦典定之也
卿大夫之獄訟以邦法斷之也愼之也不
===
徒令也而後天下相戒而避吾刑惟相率
而趨吾教也而吾之刑可省也是成其民
無自殘之命而遂吾不殘民命之心者教
爲之也惟相戒而避吾刑也而吾之教可
達也是成其民無自鑿之性而遂吾不鑿
民性之心者刑爲之也民不殘命相與樂
生而已矣民不鑿性相與式化而已矣夫
是謂樸茂之風是謂愿慤之俗自夫禮教
廢而民無則游吉所以諭趙鞅也而至於
punctuated:
下相率而趨吾教。又嘗病聖王之刑之過詳也，而不知其懲民者周也。是故悖於孝弟睦婣任卹者刑焉，析言破律、亂名改作者刑焉，行僞而堅、言僞而辨、學非而愽、順非而澤者刑焉。而未也，鄉士掌其鄉之民數而糾戒，遂士掌其遂之民數而糾戒，縣士、方士掌其縣方之民而糾戒。刑備矣，而愼之自上焉。諸侯之獄訟，以邦典定之也；卿大夫之獄訟，以邦法斷之也。愼之也，不徒令也，而後天下相戒而避吾刑。
惟相率而趨吾教也，而吾之刑可省也。是成其民無自殘之命，而遂吾不殘民命之心者，教爲之也。惟相戒而避吾刑也，而吾之教可達也。是成其民無自鑿之性，而遂吾不鑿民性之心者，刑爲之也。民不殘命，相與樂生而已矣；民不鑿性，相與式化而已矣。夫是謂樸茂之風，是謂愿慤之俗。自夫禮教廢而民無則，游吉所以諭趙鞅也，而至於
translation_en:
…all under heaven lead one another to embrace our teaching. People have also criticized the sage kings’ punishments as excessively detailed, without recognizing how comprehensive their correction of the people was. Thus, those who violated filial devotion, fraternal respect, harmony among kin, amity among relations by marriage, trustworthiness, and compassion were punished. Those who split hairs over words to subvert the statutes, confused established names, or introduced arbitrary changes were punished. Those who persisted in deceitful conduct, defended false statements eloquently, acquired extensive learning in false doctrines, or embellished their adherence to error were punished. Nor was this all: the judicial officials of the townships kept account of their populations and corrected and admonished them; the judicial officials of the outer districts kept account of their populations and corrected and admonished them; and the judicial officials of the counties and regions likewise oversaw their people and corrected and admonished them. The penal system was complete, yet caution in its application began with those above. Cases involving the feudal lords were settled according to the state’s canonical institutions; cases involving ministers and grand masters were decided according to the state’s laws. Such caution was more than a mere command. Only then did all under heaven admonish one another and avoid incurring our punishments.
Only when people lead one another to embrace our teaching can our punishments be reduced. It is teaching that enables the people to preserve their lives from self-inflicted destruction, thereby fulfilling our desire not to destroy their lives. Only when people admonish one another and avoid incurring our punishments can our teaching reach them fully. It is punishment that enables the people to preserve their inherent nature from self-inflicted damage, thereby fulfilling our desire not to damage that nature. When the people do not destroy their lives, they simply join together in delighting in life; when they do not damage their nature, they simply join together in following the transforming influence of moral instruction. This is what is called an ethos of flourishing simplicity, customs of sincerity and integrity. Since ritual teaching fell into disuse, the people have had no standard to follow: this was what You Ji explained to Zhao Yang. And when matters reached the point of…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
焚經典除謚法併教之文而捐焉者漱又
不可勝言矣自夫刑制議而民無忌叔向
所以非鄭僑也而至於寵法吏誅忠言併
刑之令而謬焉者漱又不可勝言矣甚哉
嬴秦之置天下也亟矣不以民之理理民
而惟民是尤焉不以古昔之道道民而惟
古人是陋焉而教與刑胥失之也漢西京
之治肇自高帝而成於文景識者稱其有
惇大之體數傳而至元光漸失其舊矣匡
===
衡以為屢赦之後姦邪不止非陳之以德
義示之以好惡刑未易簡也故欲曠然大
變其俗而為疏以獻焉今究所指狗勢利
也而廉恥忘提攜害也而仁讓棄耽聲色
也而邪僻日恣競侈靡也而僭踰日勝誠
抉其弊合德教以哉於是為鄭伯好勇
之證為秦穆貴信之證為陳國尚巫晉國
尚儉之證正見德教之行倡之在上不徒
文焉而已此衡之疏所以能明政治見錄
punctuated:
焚經典、除謚法，併教之文而捐焉者，漱又不可勝言矣。自夫刑制議而民無忌，叔向所以非鄭僑也，而至於寵法吏、誅忠言，併刑之令而謬焉者，漱又不可勝言矣。甚哉！嬴秦之置天下也，亟矣！不以民之理理民，而惟民是尤焉；不以古昔之道道民，而惟古人是陋焉，而教與刑胥失之也。

漢西京之治，肇自高帝而成於文景，識者稱其有惇大之體。數傳而至元光，漸失其舊矣。匡衡以為，屢赦之後，姦邪不止，非陳之以德義、示之以好惡，刑未易簡也。故欲曠然大變其俗，而為疏以獻焉。今究所指，狗勢利也，而廉恥忘；提攜害也，而仁讓棄；耽聲色也，而邪僻日恣；競侈靡也，而僭踰日勝。誠抉其弊，合德教以哉。於是為鄭伯好勇之證，為秦穆貴信之證，為陳國尚巫、晉國尚儉之證。正見德教之行，倡之在上，不徒文焉而已。此衡之疏所以能明政治，見錄
translation_en:
…burning the canonical books and abolishing the rules for posthumous titles, even discarding the written forms of moral instruction: such instances, too, are beyond enumeration [?]. Once penal institutions became a matter of public debate, the people ceased to have scruples—this was why Shuxiang criticized Zheng Qiao. Matters then reached the point of favoring legal functionaries and executing those who spoke loyally, even perverting the ordinances governing punishment; such instances, too, are beyond enumeration [?]. How extreme was the predicament in which the Ying house of Qin placed the realm! How urgent it had become! They did not govern the people according to the principles inherent in the people, but merely blamed them. They did not guide the people by the Way of antiquity, but merely disparaged the ancients. Thus they went astray in both moral instruction and punishment.

The good government of the Western Han began with Emperor Gao and reached fulfillment under Emperors Wen and Jing. Discerning observers praised its generous and magnanimous character. After several reigns, by the Yuanguang era, it was gradually losing its former character. Kuang Heng held that, when repeated amnesties had failed to put an end to wickedness, punishments could not readily be reduced unless the people were instructed in virtue and righteousness and shown what to favor and what to reject. Wishing therefore to transform their customs profoundly and comprehensively, he composed and submitted a memorial. Examining now the abuses he identified: people pursued power and profit [?], forgetting integrity and shame; they abetted harm [?], abandoning benevolence and deference; they indulged in music and sensual pleasures, becoming daily more unrestrained in wickedness; and they competed in extravagance, increasingly transgressing the limits of their stations. He truly exposed these abuses and brought moral instruction to bear [?]. He accordingly adduced the examples of the Earl of Zheng’s fondness for courage, Duke Mu of Qin’s esteem for trustworthiness, the state of Chen’s regard for shamans, and the state of Jin’s regard for frugality. These show precisely that moral instruction takes effect when those above lead the way, and is not merely a matter of written forms. This is why Heng’s memorial could illuminate the principles of government and was included …

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
於班固也惜當時不從而惇大之治日以
替焉東京之治致自光武而成於明章識
者稱其有明作之功數傳而至元嘉漸異
其初矣崔寔以爲夂弱之餘縱弛不一非
御之以賞罰檢之以法制教未易孚也故
欲奮然扶植其傾而爲論以諷焉今究所
指語法令也而垢翫叢語上下也而怠懈
積語習俗也而凋敝日增語人庶也而巧
僞日益誠抹其弊舍刑罰曷以哉於是爲
===
結繩舞干之喻爲延曆續骨之喻爲藥石
養生粱肉治疾之喻誠見刑罰之舉愼之
在上不徒令焉而已此寔之論所以能達
時變見錄於范曄也惜當時不悟而明作
之治日以衰焉夫西京之日替也非獨失
教也抑其刑失也刑失教所繇不行也而
衡專以教言彼其時教急於刑爾王吉時
政之疏先衡而言者非是歟東京之日衰
也非獨失刑也抑其教失也教失刑所繇
punctuated:
於班固也。惜當時不從，而惇大之治日以替焉。東京之治，致自光武，而成於明章，識者稱其有明作之功。數傳而至元嘉，漸異其初矣。崔寔以爲夂弱之餘，縱弛不一，非御之以賞罰、檢之以法制，教未易孚也。故欲奮然扶植其傾，而爲論以諷焉。今究所指，語法令也，而垢翫叢；語上下也，而怠懈積；語習俗也，而凋敝日增；語人庶也，而巧僞日益。誠抹其弊，舍刑罰曷以哉？於是爲結繩舞干之喻，爲延曆續骨之喻，爲藥石養生、粱肉治疾之喻。誠見刑罰之舉，愼之在上，不徒令焉而已。此寔之論所以能達時變，見錄於范曄也。惜當時不悟，而明作之治日以衰焉。
夫西京之日替也，非獨失教也，抑其刑失也。刑失，教所繇不行也。而衡專以教言，彼其時教急於刑爾。王吉時政之疏，先衡而言者，非是歟？東京之日衰也，非獨失刑也，抑其教失也。教失，刑所繇
translation_en:
…by Ban Gu. Regrettably, those of the time did not follow his advice, and government grounded in generosity and magnanimity declined daily. The government of the Eastern Han originated with Guangwu and reached its fulfillment under Emperors Ming and Zhang. Discerning observers praised its achievement in the enlightened application of punishments. After several reigns, however, by the Yuanjia era it had gradually departed from its beginnings. Cui Shi believed that, after prolonged weakness [?], laxity had become widespread: unless people were governed through rewards and punishments and restrained through laws and institutions, moral instruction could hardly win their trust. Thus, determined to shore up the tottering order, he composed a discourse to offer admonition.
Examining the matters he addressed, we find that, when he spoke of laws and ordinances, abuses and disregard had multiplied; of superiors and subordinates, indolence and negligence had accumulated; of customary practices, deterioration increased daily; and of the common people, cunning and deceit grew daily. If these abuses were truly to be eliminated [?], what means were available apart from punishments? Hence his analogies of knotted cords and dancing with shields, of extending the years and knitting bones [?], and of using medicines and mineral remedies to nourish life while using fine grain and meat to treat illness. These indeed show that the application of punishments depends upon those above exercising care; it is not merely a matter of issuing orders. This is why Cui Shi’s discourse could comprehend changing circumstances and was included in Fan Ye’s history. Regrettably, those of the time failed to understand, and government through the enlightened application of punishments declined daily.
Now, the daily decline of the Western Han resulted not only from failures in moral instruction, but also from failures in punishment. Failures in punishment were what prevented moral instruction from taking effect. Yet Kuang Heng spoke exclusively of moral instruction because, at that time, it was more urgent than punishment. Was this not also the point of Wang Ji’s memorial on contemporary government, written before Heng’s? The daily decline of the Eastern Han resulted not only from failures in punishment, but also from failures in moral instruction. Failures in moral instruction were the reason that punishments…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
不中也而寔專以刑言彼其時刑急於教
爾王符述赦之篇先寔而言者非是歟是
故民心不容一日而肆則教典不容一日
而隳民習不容一日而邪則刑典不容一
日而墜教所不加刑所必加矣刑所不及
教所必及矣終其身出入於教刑之內而
不能兩釋以爲生者民也惟知所出入焉
即謂之良民終其任重輕於教刑之間而
不能兩釋以爲治者吏也惟知所重輕焉
即謂之良吏會以世既太平也而可置此
不講耶我
===
聖祖開創之始加意教刑
製通訓以率善良
編大誥以繩頑僻天下回心嚮道垂二百年
其在於今漸至玩愒西漢之敝風雖無也
而識微者耿衡之思東漢之頹俗雖無也
而炳幾者抱寔之慮則夫教刑二典誠不
得不重加申飭矣
punctuated:
不中也，而寔專以刑言，彼其時刑急於教爾。王符《述赦》之篇，先寔而言者，非是歟？是故民心不容一日而肆，則教典不容一日而隳；民習不容一日而邪，則刑典不容一日而墜。教所不加，刑所必加矣；刑所不及，教所必及矣。終其身出入於教刑之內，而不能兩釋以爲生者，民也；惟知所出入焉，即謂之良民。終其任重輕於教刑之間，而不能兩釋以爲治者，吏也；惟知所重輕焉，即謂之良吏。會以世既太平也，而可置此不講耶？
我聖祖開創之始，加意教刑，製通訓以率善良，編大誥以繩頑僻，天下回心嚮道，垂二百年。其在於今，漸至玩愒。西漢之敝風雖無也，而識微者耿衡之思；東漢之頹俗雖無也，而炳幾者抱寔之慮。則夫教刑二典，誠不得不重加申飭矣。
translation_en:
…fails to hit the proper mark. Yet Shi spoke exclusively of punishment because, in his time, punishment was more urgently needed than moral instruction. Was this not also what Wang Fu said before Shi in his essay “On Pardons” (Shu she)? Thus, since the people’s hearts must not be allowed to run unchecked for even a day, the institutions of moral instruction must not be allowed to fall into ruin for even a day. Since the people’s habits must not be allowed to become deviant for even a day, the institutions of punishment must not be allowed to lapse for even a day. Where moral instruction does not exert its influence, punishment must be applied; where punishment does not reach, moral instruction must reach. Those who throughout their lives move within the bounds of instruction and punishment, and cannot cast both aside in making their living, are the people. If they understand how to conduct themselves within those bounds, they are called good subjects. Those who throughout their tenure weigh the relative importance of instruction and punishment, and cannot cast both aside in governing, are officials. If they understand which should receive greater or lesser weight, they are called good officials. Can it be thought that, because the world is already at peace, these matters may be set aside without discussion [?]?
When our Sagely Progenitor first founded the dynasty, he devoted particular attention to instruction and punishment. He composed the General Instructions (Tongxun) to guide the good and compiled the Grand Pronouncements (Da gao) to restrain the obstinate and wayward. All under Heaven turned their hearts toward the Way, and nearly two hundred years have elapsed. By the present day, however, people have gradually become negligent and idle. Although the corrupt practices of the Western Han are absent, those who discern subtle signs are troubled by the concerns of Heng; although the decadent customs of the Eastern Han are absent, those who perceive the beginnings of change harbor the anxieties of Shi. Thus the two institutions of instruction and punishment truly must be reaffirmed and rigorously enforced.

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
皇上弘敷道化昭布法紀惇大明作之意無歲
不揩於
綸音正宜海内清和教洽而刑措也而容未
盡然得非百爾臣工奉行罔實之故歟愚
請得而繹言之夫教不足以動民非教也
文也一轉移而文皆實矣今惟推衡之意
以實行焉崇廉退之風惇忠厚之行防邪
僻之患革僭踰之習謹禮以示民厚防以
止欲庶幾綱紀振肅法度修明毀譽不行
===
善惡不眩民有可封之俗世有安瀾之美
而惇大之治不再見於今時耶刑不足以
防民非刑也令也一轉移而令皆實矣今
惟推寔之意以實求焉洗其垢翫之弊懲
其怠緩之私反其凋敝之俗止其巧僞之
奸觸禁者刑變易者流庶幾淳風可挽僞
習可端淫僻者化而善良者起科條備而
不犯五刑具而不試而明作之功不復覩
於今世耶夫制禮所以止刑而明刑所以
punctuated:
皇上弘敷道化，昭布法紀，惇大明作之意，無歲不揩於綸音。正宜海内清和，教洽而刑措也，而容未盡然，得非百爾臣工奉行罔實之故歟？愚請得而繹言之。
夫教不足以動民，非教也，文也。一轉移而文皆實矣。今惟推衡之意以實行焉，崇廉退之風，惇忠厚之行，防邪僻之患，革僭踰之習，謹禮以示民，厚防以止欲，庶幾綱紀振肅，法度修明，毀譽不行，善惡不眩，民有可封之俗，世有安瀾之美，而惇大之治不再見於今時耶？
刑不足以防民，非刑也，令也。一轉移而令皆實矣。今惟推寔之意以實求焉，洗其垢翫之弊，懲其怠緩之私，反其凋敝之俗，止其巧僞之奸，觸禁者刑，變易者流，庶幾淳風可挽，僞習可端，淫僻者化而善良者起，科條備而不犯，五刑具而不試，而明作之功不復覩於今世耶？夫制禮所以止刑，而明刑所以
translation_en:
His Majesty widely extends moral transformation and clearly promulgates laws and discipline. Not a year passes without his intention to make instruction generous and comprehensive, and to institute punishments with discernment, being expressed [?] in his imperial pronouncements. All within the seas should accordingly enjoy peace and harmony, with instruction prevailing and punishments laid aside. Yet this may not entirely be so. Could this be because you, the many officials, fail to give substantive effect to these commands? Allow me, in my humble judgment, to elaborate.
Instruction that cannot move the people is not instruction, but mere form. With a change of direction, all such forms can become realities. Now, if we extend Heng’s intention and put it genuinely into practice—promoting integrity and modest withdrawal, encouraging loyal and generous conduct, guarding against the dangers of perversity, reforming habits of overstepping one’s station, carefully observing ritual to set an example for the people, and strengthening restraints to curb desires—we may hope that the governing order will be reinvigorated and made rigorous, and laws and institutions put in good order and clarified. Groundless disparagement and praise will cease to circulate, and good and evil will no longer be confused. The people’s customs will be such that all could merit enfeoffment, and the age will enjoy the beauty of untroubled waters. Would not the rule of generous and comprehensive instruction then appear again in our own time?
Punishment that cannot restrain the people is not punishment, but mere commands. With a change of direction, all such commands can become realities. Now, if we extend Shi’s intention and earnestly seek its realization—cleansing the abuses of ingrained neglect, chastising self-serving indolence and laxity, reversing the decline of customs, and stopping cunning and deceitful wrongdoing, punishing those who violate prohibitions and exiling those who alter established rules—we may hope to restore wholesome customs and rectify deceitful practices. The dissolute and perverse will be transformed, while the good and upright will come forward. Statutes will be fully provided yet never violated; the five punishments will stand ready yet never be put to use. Would not the achievement of instituting punishments with discernment then be seen again in our own age? Ritual is established in order to obviate punishment, while punishments are made clear in order to…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
弼敎二者實相資以有成者也今惟端本
以核實而無俟乎虛文推誠以孚化而不
專於法令則敎洽刑措風移俗易而於復
古之治誠易易也是使衡寔二子復生何
容置喙哉謹對
第三問
沈位
同考試官敎諭陳　批〔窮經一策士子類能言之漫無歸束子獨考覈精詳準裁不謬豈有〕
===
得於傳約之訓者乎
同考試官署郎中沈　批〔漢去古未遠崇尚經術故通經之士家相授受羽翼之功殆不可泯〕
第訓詁繁而實得尠至宋儒始考定折衷一準
諸理耳其說固未盡廢也此作能根極理要灼
見指歸而於漢儒亦存而不線使諸□□可作亦
當心服不獨裁覈之精爾已
考試官左諭德汪　批〔考究儒先之得失而折衷於傳約之旨深有意見〕
punctuated:
弼敎，二者實相資以有成者也。今惟端本以核實，而無俟乎虛文；推誠以孚化，而不專於法令，則敎洽刑措，風移俗易，而於復古之治，誠易易也。是使衡寔二子復生，何容置喙哉？謹對。
第三問
沈位
同考試官敎諭陳，批〔窮經一策，士子類能言之，漫無歸束。子獨考覈精詳，準裁不謬，豈有〕得於傳約之訓者乎？
同考試官署郎中沈，批〔漢去古未遠，崇尚經術，故通經之士家相授受，羽翼之功殆不可泯。〕第訓詁繁而實得尠，至宋儒始考定折衷，一準諸理耳。其說固未盡廢也。此作能根極理要，灼見指歸，而於漢儒亦存而不線，使諸□□可作，亦當心服，不獨裁覈之精爾已。
考試官左諭德汪，批〔考究儒先之得失，而折衷於傳約之旨，深有意見。〕
translation_en:
…to assist moral instruction. The two truly support one another in achieving their purposes. Now, if we rectify the foundations to scrutinize actual practice, without relying on empty formalities, and extend sincerity to inspire trust and transformation, without depending exclusively on laws and ordinances, then moral instruction will spread everywhere, punishments will be set aside, and prevailing ways and customs will change. Restoring the governance of antiquity will then be very easy indeed. Were Heng and Shi to return to life, what room would they have to interject? Respectfully submitted in reply.
Third Question
Shen Wei
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “On the policy question concerning exhaustive study of the Classics, candidates generally have something to say, but their discussions ramble without reaching a conclusion. You alone investigate with precision and thoroughness, and judge by sound standards without error. Might you have gained something from the teaching on ‘transmission and concision’ [?]?”
Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Acting Director: “The Han was not far removed from antiquity and held classical learning in high esteem. Thus, scholars versed in the Classics transmitted and received their learning within their families; their contribution in supporting that learning can hardly be effaced. Yet their glosses were copious and their actual attainments few. Only with the Song Confucians did scholars begin to examine, establish, and adjudicate interpretations, taking principle alone as their standard. The earlier explanations were certainly not discarded altogether. This essay can probe the essentials of principle to their roots and clearly perceive their ultimate import. As for the Han Confucians, it also preserves their learning without ‘threading’ it [?]. If the various □□ could return to life, they too would surely be convinced at heart. This is more than merely precision in judgment and examination.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher: “Examining the achievements and shortcomings of earlier Confucian scholars and adjudicating them according to the purport of ‘transmission and concision’ [?], this essay shows considerable insight.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖賢之道散見於載籍而統會於吾心非
愽無以廣學也非約無以致精也然徒愽
者溺於汗漫而徑約者淪於空虛君子於
是有兼體不累之功有交養互發之妙玩
索於言意之表而默識以通其蘊反覆於
簡帙之繁而冥會以盡其微庶幾聖賢之
道不在經傳而在吾心也夫上古之世六
籍未備其所謂書者不過墳典丘索之類
而已至成周之時而制作始盛若周官外
===
史之所掌小行人之所達皇覽詳而國典
著聖謨具而至道彰易以道化長於變矣
詩以達意長於風矣書以道事長於政矣
春秋以道義長於治人矣禮以節人長於
行矣樂以合情長於和矣道之所在因言
以洩事之所寓因文以顯是文之所載者
愽而意之所該者約也然是時六籍雖著
而傳播未廣故易與春秋具矣以韓宣子
之賢也適魯然後見易象與春秋詩具矣
punctuated:
聖賢之道散見於載籍，而統會於吾心。非愽無以廣學也，非約無以致精也。然徒愽者溺於汗漫，而徑約者淪於空虛。君子於是有兼體不累之功，有交養互發之妙，玩索於言意之表，而默識以通其蘊；反覆於簡帙之繁，而冥會以盡其微。庶幾聖賢之道不在經傳，而在吾心也。
夫上古之世，六籍未備，其所謂書者，不過墳典丘索之類而已。至成周之時，而制作始盛，若周官外史之所掌、小行人之所達，皇覽詳而國典著，聖謨具而至道彰。《易》以道化，長於變矣；《詩》以達意，長於風矣；《書》以道事，長於政矣；《春秋》以道義，長於治人矣；《禮》以節人，長於行矣；《樂》以合情，長於和矣。道之所在，因言以洩；事之所寓，因文以顯。是文之所載者愽，而意之所該者約也。然是時六籍雖著，而傳播未廣。故《易》與《春秋》具矣，以韓宣子之賢也，適魯然後見《易》象與《春秋》；《詩》具矣，
translation_en:
The Way of the sages and worthies appears scattered throughout written records, yet is brought together into a unified whole within our minds. Without breadth, learning cannot be enlarged; without concentration on essentials, precision cannot be attained. Yet those who pursue breadth alone drown in boundless expanses, while those who take a shortcut to essentials sink into emptiness. The gentleman therefore works to embody both without being encumbered by either, attaining the subtle capacity to let each nourish and illuminate the other. He ponders and explores beyond words and their meanings, silently apprehending their hidden import; he returns repeatedly to the profusion of written volumes, inwardly comprehending their finest subtleties. Thus he may come close to having the Way of the sages and worthies reside not in the classics and their commentaries, but within his own mind.
In highest antiquity, the Six Classics were not yet complete. What were called writings amounted only to works such as the Three Tombs, Five Canons, Nine Mounds, and Eight Cords. Only in the time of the fully established Zhou did the creation of institutions and writings begin to flourish. Consider what the Outer Scribe administered and what the Minor Messenger communicated, as described in the Offices of Zhou: imperial records were detailed and the canons of the state made manifest; sagely counsels were complete and the supreme Way shone forth. The Changes expounds transformation and excels in treating change; the Odes conveys intentions and excels in moral influence; the Documents recounts affairs and excels in government; the Spring and Autumn Annals expounds rightness and excels in governing people; the Rites regulates people and excels in conduct; the Music brings feelings into accord and excels in harmony. Wherever the Way resides, words disclose it; whatever affairs are embodied in these works, writing makes them manifest. Thus what their texts contain is broad, while what their meaning encompasses is concentrated in essentials. Yet although the Six Classics had been set down at that time, they had not circulated widely. Thus the Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals were already complete, yet even someone as worthy as Han Xuanzi saw the images of the Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals only after traveling to Lu. The Odes was already complete…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
以吳季札之博雅也聘於上國乃始聞風
雅頌之音書具矣惟楚之左史倚相能讀
三墳五典八索九丘之書禮具矣惟周柱
下史聃以知禮名樂具矣惟魯萇弘以知
樂名士生斯時獲覩全經而以闡辯名家
者亦難矣噫此非以見古人會之於約而
無事於博耶周衰放棄道德奔逐功利五
帝三王之文飄淪散軼漫不省識繼以秦
政不經坑焚肆虐芟滅先王之道屛絶百
===
家之言雖好古君子心誦腹藏壁扃巖鐍
其能濟秦之險以通於漢繹古之緒而垂
之今者曾幾何人是以漢承秦後上視三
代如更晝夜夢覺有識之士所爲憤嘆而
不能已也柰何高帝從事干戈未遑庠序
之事文景不任儒術本好黃老之言其後
挾書之律雖除然因循舊俗未有尚者博
士之名雖設然具官待問未有進者至建
元元狩之間廢黜百家尊崇儒術傍求竄
punctuated:
以吳季札之博雅也，聘於上國，乃始聞風雅頌之音。書具矣，惟楚之左史倚相能讀三墳、五典、八索、九丘之書。禮具矣，惟周柱下史聃以知禮名。樂具矣，惟魯萇弘以知樂名。士生斯時，獲覩全經而以闡辯名家者亦難矣。噫！此非以見古人會之於約而無事於博耶？
周衰，放棄道德，奔逐功利，五帝三王之文飄淪散軼，漫不省識。繼以秦政不經，坑焚肆虐，芟滅先王之道，屛絶百家之言。雖好古君子心誦腹藏，壁扃巖鐍，其能濟秦之險以通於漢，繹古之緒而垂之今者，曾幾何人？是以漢承秦後，上視三代，如更晝夜夢覺，有識之士所爲憤嘆而不能已也。
柰何高帝從事干戈，未遑庠序之事；文景不任儒術，本好黃老之言。其後挾書之律雖除，然因循舊俗，未有尚者；博士之名雖設，然具官待問，未有進者。至建元元狩之間，廢黜百家，尊崇儒術，傍求竄
translation_en:
…even Ji Zha of Wu, with his broad learning and refinement, only began to hear the airs, court hymns, and sacrificial hymns when he visited the central states on a diplomatic mission. The Documents were already complete, yet only Yi Xiang, the Scribe of the Left in Chu, could read the Three Tombs, Five Canons, Eight Cords, and Nine Mounds. The rites were already complete, yet only Dan, the Archivist of Zhou, was renowned for understanding them. Music was already complete, yet only Chang Hong of Lu [?] was renowned for understanding it. For scholars born in that age, it was difficult indeed to see the classics in their entirety and establish a reputation as authorities through exposition and argument. Alas! Does this not show that the ancients grasped their essentials and had no need to pursue breadth?
As Zhou declined, people abandoned the Way and virtue and raced after achievement and profit. The writings of the Five Emperors and Three Kings drifted into oblivion and became scattered and lost, with scarcely anyone attending to or understanding them. Then came Qin’s unprincipled rule: its cruel burying of scholars and burning of books eradicated the Way of the former kings and suppressed the teachings of the Hundred Schools. Although gentlemen devoted to antiquity recited texts inwardly and stored them in memory, or sealed them within walls and locked them away in caves, how many could carry them through Qin’s perils into Han, unravel the threads of antiquity, and transmit them to the present? Thus, when Han succeeded Qin and looked back upon the Three Dynasties, it was as though day had changed to night, or waking to dreaming. This was something that discerning men could never cease lamenting with indignation.
Yet Emperor Gao was occupied with warfare and had no leisure for schools. Emperors Wen and Jing did not employ Confucian learning, being inclined instead toward the teachings of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi. Subsequently, although the law against possessing books was repealed, people continued to follow established customs, and none yet esteemed such learning. Although the title of Erudite was instituted, its holders merely filled their posts and awaited consultation; none yet came forward. It was only in the period between the Jianyuan and Yuanshou reign eras that the Hundred Schools were dismissed, Confucian learning was honored, and a wide search was undertaken for scattered…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
簡博訪殘編剏甲乙之科擢賢良之士而
先王載籍或得之於名山壞宅或傳之於
耆儒夙彥文學彬彬始進詩書往往間出
矣當時言易自淄川田生言書自濟南伏
生言詩則韓太傅申培公轅固生言禮則
高堂生言春秋則董仲舒胡毋生辨析於
疑難增煩於訓詁而典籍之傳博矣然專
門命氏以顯其家學故爲傳訓者皆言氏
而不言名於是有五經家法之號儒者各
===
以指意相爲授受而弟子轉相傳習守而
不變於是有五經師法之名射策決科則
有明經通義之目屏居教授則有編牒著
錄之稱夫學有統宗而不紛於異議尊尚
師說而不淆於衆言漢之儒者誠知篤信
好學矣然守之太拘而不能精思明辨以
究異同之指考中折衷以綜致一之的豈
得爲至當之論哉卒之專己黨同轍殊牖
別是非錯謬準裁靡定而復惑以纖緯術
punctuated: 簡，博訪殘編，剏甲乙之科，擢賢良之士，而先王載籍，或得之於名山壞宅，或傳之於耆儒夙彥，文學彬彬始進，詩書往往間出矣。當時言易，自淄川田生；言書，自濟南伏生；言詩，則韓太傅、申培公、轅固生；言禮，則高堂生；言春秋，則董仲舒、胡毋生。辨析於疑難，增煩於訓詁，而典籍之傳博矣。然專門命氏，以顯其家學，故爲傳訓者皆言氏而不言名，於是有五經家法之號。儒者各以指意相爲授受，而弟子轉相傳習，守而不變，於是有五經師法之名。射策決科，則有明經通義之目；屏居教授，則有編牒著錄之稱。夫學有統宗，而不紛於異議；尊尚師說，而不淆於衆言。漢之儒者誠知篤信好學矣。然守之太拘，而不能精思明辨，以究異同之指，考中折衷，以綜致一之的，豈得爲至當之論哉？卒之專己黨同，轍殊牖別，是非錯謬，準裁靡定，而復惑以纖緯術
translation_en:
…scattered bamboo slips and searched widely for surviving portions of texts, established Class A and Class B examinations, and promoted men of worth and ability. The writings of the former kings were sometimes recovered from famous mountains and ruined dwellings, and sometimes transmitted by venerable scholars and long-established men of learning. Men accomplished in literary learning began to advance, and the Odes and Documents repeatedly came to light. At that time, exposition of the Changes derived from Master Tian of Zichuan; exposition of the Documents, from Master Fu of Jinan. For the Odes there were Grand Tutor Han, Master Shen Pei, and Master Yuan Gu; for the Rites, Master Gaotang; and for the Spring and Autumn Annals, Dong Zhongshu and Hu Wusheng. They analyzed doubtful and difficult passages and elaborated textual glosses, and the transmission of the canonical writings became extensive. Yet specialized schools took their surnames as designations to distinguish their particular traditions of learning. Thus commentaries and glosses were identified by surnames rather than personal names, giving rise to the designation “lineage methods of the Five Classics.” Scholars imparted and received their respective interpretations, and disciples transmitted and studied them in succession, preserving them without alteration. Hence arose the term “teachers’ methods of the Five Classics.” Those who answered policy questions drawn by lot to determine their examination standing were designated as “versed in the classics and conversant with their meanings”; those who taught in retirement were spoken of as having pupils entered in registers.

Their learning had a governing lineage and was not scattered among divergent opinions; they honored their teachers’ explanations and did not confuse them with the multitude of other views. The Han scholars truly understood steadfast faith and love of learning. Yet they adhered to their traditions too rigidly. They could not think deeply and discriminate clearly to investigate the purport of agreements and differences, examine what was correct and weigh competing views, and bring these together toward a unified aim. How could their judgments be considered entirely sound? In the end, they insisted on their own views and sided with those who agreed with them, following different tracks and looking through separate windows. Right and wrong became confused, and no settled standard of judgment remained. They were further led astray by apocryphal writings [?] and the arts of…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
數之學雜以申韓釋老之言妄生穿鑿破
碎大道亦已甚矣安能闡繹道眞探索聖
藴激昻情性之變窮研坎井之奧而使六
經之道復明於世哉雖劉向之博綜羣籍
馬融之剖析疑義尚有餘譏焉他可知已
夫六籍先王所以正天道明人心致至治
之成法也使高明超卓之士一覽可以得
其閫奧奚必過求巧鑿窮搜遠引贅以支
離之說文以艱深之辭耶昔秦延君以十
===
餘萬言明堯典可謂知要乎朱普以三十
餘萬言解尚書可謂致一乎於戲此漢儒
務博而不能歸約之病也雖然綜蒐遺編
網羅放失抱遺經於千載之上而使後之
諸儒得有所考據而聖賢之學不至湮滅
者此又漢儒務博之功也可盡誣哉迨於
有宋眞儒輩出理學大明覃思於義訓之
表妙契於性命之微若周子太極圖之作
而陰陽動靜之理著張子西銘之撰而理
punctuated:
數之學，雜以申韓釋老之言，妄生穿鑿，破碎大道，亦已甚矣！安能闡繹道眞，探索聖藴，激昻情性之變，窮研坎井之奧，而使六經之道復明於世哉？雖劉向之博綜羣籍，馬融之剖析疑義，尚有餘譏焉，他可知已。夫六籍，先王所以正天道、明人心、致至治之成法也。使高明超卓之士一覽可以得其閫奧，奚必過求巧鑿，窮搜遠引，贅以支離之說，文以艱深之辭耶？昔秦延君以十餘萬言明《堯典》，可謂知要乎？朱普以三十餘萬言解《尚書》，可謂致一乎？於戲！此漢儒務博而不能歸約之病也。雖然，綜蒐遺編，網羅放失，抱遺經於千載之上，而使後之諸儒得有所考據，而聖賢之學不至湮滅者，此又漢儒務博之功也，可盡誣哉？

迨於有宋，眞儒輩出，理學大明，覃思於義訓之表，妙契於性命之微。若周子《太極圖》之作，而陰陽動靜之理著；張子《西銘》之撰，而理
translation_en:
…the study of numerical arts, mingling it with the teachings of Shen Buhai and Han Fei, Buddhism and Laozi, recklessly devising strained interpretations and fragmenting the Great Way: this had indeed gone much too far! How could they elucidate the truth of the Way, explore the profundities of the sages, stir the transformations of feelings and nature, fathom the mysteries of pits and wells [?], and thereby make the Way of the Six Classics shine forth again in the world? Even Liu Xiang, with his comprehensive command of many books, and Ma Rong, with his analysis of doubtful meanings, still left grounds for criticism. The others may be judged accordingly. The Six Classics are the established models by which the former kings rectified the Way of Heaven, illuminated human hearts, and brought about perfect government. If men of lofty understanding and outstanding ability can grasp their innermost mysteries at a reading, why must one pursue ingenious, forced interpretations to excess, search exhaustively and adduce remote evidence, encumber them with disjointed explanations, and embellish them with difficult, abstruse language? In former times, Qin Yanjun used more than a hundred thousand words to elucidate the Canon of Yao: can he be said to have understood its essentials? Zhu Pu used more than three hundred thousand words to explain the Book of Documents: can he be said to have attained unity? Alas! This was the failing of Han scholars: they pursued breadth but could not bring it back to essentials. Nevertheless, they comprehensively gathered surviving writings, collected what had been scattered and lost, and preserved the remaining classics from a thousand years before. Thus later scholars had evidence on which to base their inquiries, and the learning of the sages and worthies did not disappear. This, too, was an achievement of the Han scholars’ pursuit of breadth. Can it all be dismissed?

With the advent of the Song, true Confucian scholars emerged in succession, and the learning of principle became brilliantly clear. They reflected deeply beyond textual meanings and glosses, attaining a subtle understanding of the mysteries of human nature and Heaven’s mandate. Thus Master Zhou’s composition of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate made manifest the principles of yin and yang, movement and stillness; Master Zhang’s composition of the Western Inscription made principle…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
一分殊之義彰程子之爲易傳而卦畫爻
象之意悉朱子之註釋經書而聖賢傳授
之旨明蔡沈之作書傳以闡典謨訓誥之
義胡安國之作春秋傳以定褒貶是非之
準根極領要發千古不傳之秘分析毫芒
祛前人不決之惑而使六經之道粲然復
明於世其用功亦勤矣故曰漢儒之學得
其梗槩能務博也宋儒之學得其精華能
反約也斯言也不信然哉雖然間有可疑
===
者朱子蓋嘗別而言之矣夫濂洛關閩闡
明經傳敷析疑義是爲儒者之經蘇軾陳
少南輩攻習鄭靡馳騖詞華是爲文人之
經張子韶輩躭寂悟空談心見性是爲禪
者之經夫儒者之經尚矣若文詞之患溺
人於淺近而禪悟之病蔽人於高明此又
不可不明辨而詳審也蓋漢儒之學務工
考索而不免徒博之患宋儒之學務窮根
本而遂有徑約之弊窮經者又當考其所
punctuated:
一分殊之義彰；程子之爲《易傳》，而卦畫爻象之意悉；朱子之註釋經書，而聖賢傳授之旨明；蔡沈之作《書傳》，以闡典謨訓誥之義；胡安國之作《春秋傳》，以定褒貶是非之準。根極領要，發千古不傳之秘；分析毫芒，祛前人不決之惑，而使六經之道粲然復明於世，其用功亦勤矣。故曰：「漢儒之學得其梗槩，能務博也；宋儒之學得其精華，能反約也。」斯言也，不信然哉？
雖然，間有可疑者，朱子蓋嘗別而言之矣。夫濂洛關閩，闡明經傳，敷析疑義，是爲儒者之經；蘇軾、陳少南輩，攻習鄭靡，馳騖詞華，是爲文人之經；張子韶輩，躭寂悟空，談心見性，是爲禪者之經。夫儒者之經尚矣。若文詞之患，溺人於淺近；而禪悟之病，蔽人於高明。此又不可不明辨而詳審也。蓋漢儒之學務工考索，而不免徒博之患；宋儒之學務窮根本，而遂有徑約之弊。窮經者又當考其所
translation_en:
…the meaning of the unity of principle and the differentiation of its manifestations became clear. Master Cheng’s Commentary on the Changes fully elucidated the meaning of the hexagram configurations and line images; Master Zhu’s annotations to the canonical writings clarified the purport transmitted by the sages and worthies. Cai Shen composed his Commentary on the Documents to explain the meaning of its canons, counsels, instructions, and announcements; Hu Anguo composed his Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals to establish standards for praise and blame, right and wrong. They probed to the roots and grasped the essentials, revealing secrets that had gone untransmitted for a thousand ages. They analyzed the finest distinctions and dispelled doubts that their predecessors had left unresolved, making the Way of the Six Classics shine clearly in the world once more. Their labors were indeed diligent. Thus it is said: “The learning of the Han scholars grasped the broad outlines, for they could devote themselves to breadth; the learning of the Song scholars grasped the essence, for they could return to the essentials.” Is this statement not truly so?
Nevertheless, there are points open to doubt, and Master Zhu once discussed these by distinguishing different approaches. The scholars of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min elucidated the classics and commentaries and expounded doubtful meanings: these were the classics as understood by Confucian scholars. Su Shi, Chen Shaonan, and their like assiduously cultivated the decadent manner of Zheng [?] and pursued ornate expression: these were the classics as understood by literary men. Zhang Zishao and his like immersed themselves in stillness and the realization of emptiness, discoursing on the mind and the discernment of one’s nature: these were the classics as understood by Chan Buddhists. The Confucian scholars’ understanding of the classics deserves esteem. As for the danger of literary embellishment, it immerses people in the superficial; the fault of Chan awakening obscures their understanding with lofty abstractions. These, too, must be clearly distinguished and carefully examined. Han scholarship sought proficiency in investigation, yet could not escape the danger of mere breadth; Song scholarship sought to penetrate to the foundations, yet consequently incurred the fault of taking a shortcut to essentials. Those who thoroughly investigate the classics must also examine their…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
自矣夫君子之學不求之於博無以爲反
約之地不歸之於約無以收博學之功由
是以身體之以心驗之從容默會於幽閒
靜一之中超然自得於書言象意之外使
義理融通足以爲進德之助見聞該洽足
以成致一之功則以之解經可也不爲支
離之病治經可也不爲師心之謬下此而
詞章可也不爲藻繪之談而說家紛紛之
議舉不足以惑之矣雖然三代而上載籍
===
未具而士皆篤於自修三代而下簡帙詳
矣而士之所學寖不及古誠有如明問所
疑者葢古人之學不求之於篇籍而考之
於身心不資之於記誦而反之於行業故
達而在上則昌言嘉謨足爲熙載亮工之
具窮而在下則令德令儀足爲維世淑人
之本是六經未出而經在吾心求之於約
也乃今之人尋行數墨以爲工獵異標奇
以自炫始焉逐跡喪眞徒爲利祿之媒終
punctuated:
自矣。夫君子之學，不求之於博，無以爲反約之地；不歸之於約，無以收博學之功。由是以身體之，以心驗之，從容默會於幽閒靜一之中，超然自得於書言象意之外，使義理融通，足以爲進德之助；見聞該洽，足以成致一之功。則以之解經可也，不爲支離之病；治經可也，不爲師心之謬；下此而詞章可也，不爲藻繪之談。而說家紛紛之議，舉不足以惑之矣。
雖然，三代而上，載籍未具，而士皆篤於自修；三代而下，簡帙詳矣，而士之所學寖不及古，誠有如明問所疑者。葢古人之學，不求之於篇籍，而考之於身心；不資之於記誦，而反之於行業。故達而在上，則昌言嘉謨，足爲熙載亮工之具；窮而在下，則令德令儀，足爲維世淑人之本。是六經未出，而經在吾心，求之於約也。乃今之人，尋行數墨以爲工，獵異標奇以自炫，始焉逐跡喪眞，徒爲利祿之媒，終
translation_en:
…the sources from which it derives. In the gentleman’s learning, without seeking breadth, there is no foundation for returning to essentials; without returning to essentials, there is no way to realize the benefits of broad learning. On this basis, he embodies his learning in practice and tests it in his heart, calmly apprehending it in quiet seclusion and undivided stillness, and freely attaining understanding beyond writings, words, images, and ideas. Thus moral principles become thoroughly integrated, sufficient to aid the advancement of virtue, while comprehensive knowledge becomes sufficient to achieve unity. He may then use this learning to interpret the classics without the fault of fragmentation, or to study the classics without the error of taking his own mind as his sole authority. At a lesser level, he may use it in literary composition without producing merely ornate language. The contentious arguments of the various commentators will all be powerless to confuse him.
Nevertheless, in the Three Dynasties and earlier, written records were not yet complete, yet scholars were all devoted to cultivating themselves. After the Three Dynasties, books became abundant, yet scholars’ learning gradually fell short of that of the ancients. This is indeed as your perceptive question suggests. The ancients, in their learning, did not seek it in books but examined it in their own persons and hearts; they did not rely on memorization and recitation but turned back to their conduct and undertakings. Thus, when successful and occupying high office, their sound words and excellent counsels sufficed as means of bringing affairs to completion and assisting the work of government. When without advancement and remaining below, their admirable virtue and exemplary bearing sufficed as a foundation for sustaining society and improving others. Thus, before the Six Classics had appeared, the classics were already within one’s own heart: learning was sought in its essentials. People today, however, pride themselves on following lines and counting characters, hunting out novelties and flaunting curiosities to show themselves off. At first, they pursue outward traces and lose the truth, making their learning merely a means to profit and official emoluments; in the end…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
焉入耳出口不啻弁髦之棄是六經雖具
徒爲陳迹耳雖博亦何益哉此又古今學
術之辨而亦世道升降之機所由係也
明興首建學校訪求載籍纂修羣書
頒賜中外使聖賢之道既晦而復明斯文之
緒既墜而復振
皇上建中立極惇化厲賢遂
敬一之學紹道統之傳表尚書三要以續
聖訓而帝王之治績益彰建
===
皇史宬以收圖籍而
列聖之謨烈有光邇者防
大典之散軼而弘開史局翻錄副本念
皇澤之久湮而
簡命儒臣考修
興志其所以加意於典章羽翼於經傳闡揚
國華陶鑄人文者至矣盛矣士生斯世一何
幸耶然漸濡既久涵泳益深不有通經學
古之士反約致一之儒上接先賢之統而
punctuated:
焉入耳出口，不啻弁髦之棄。是六經雖具，徒爲陳迹耳，雖博亦何益哉？此又古今學術之辨，而亦世道升降之機所由係也。
明興，首建學校，訪求載籍，纂修羣書，頒賜中外，使聖賢之道既晦而復明，斯文之緒既墜而復振。皇上建中立極，惇化厲賢，遂敬一之學，紹道統之傳，表《尚書三要》以續聖訓，而帝王之治績益彰；建皇史宬以收圖籍，而列聖之謨烈有光。邇者防《大典》之散軼，而弘開史局，翻錄副本；念皇澤之久湮，而簡命儒臣考修《興志》。其所以加意於典章，羽翼於經傳，闡揚國華，陶鑄人文者，至矣，盛矣！士生斯世，一何幸耶！然漸濡既久，涵泳益深，不有通經學古之士、反約致一之儒，上接先賢之統而
translation_en:
…in the end, what enters their ears passes straight out of their mouths; they discard it like the ceremonial cap and forelocks cast aside after coming of age. Thus, although the Six Classics remain complete, they are merely vestiges of the past. What benefit is there even in extensive learning? Here, too, lies the distinction between ancient and modern scholarship, and upon this hinges the rise and decline of the moral order.
When the Ming arose, it first established schools, sought out written works, compiled and edited books, and bestowed them upon the capital and the provinces. Thus the Way of the sages and worthies, once obscured, shone forth again, and the thread of this cultural tradition, once broken, was restored. His Majesty established the mean and set the supreme standard, fostered moral transformation and encouraged the worthy, advanced the learning of reverent unity, and continued the transmission of the Way. He gave prominence to the Three Essentials of the Book of Documents to carry forward the sagely instructions, making the achievements of imperial government still more manifest. He built the Imperial Historical Archive to house maps and writings, bringing lustre to the plans and accomplishments of successive sage emperors. Recently, to prevent the Great Compendium from becoming dispersed and lost, he greatly expanded the historical compilation office and had a duplicate transcribed. Mindful that imperial beneficence had long remained obscured, he selected and commissioned Confucian officials to research and compile the Gazetteer of Xing [?]. His care for statutes and institutions, his support for the Classics and their commentaries, his celebration of the dynasty’s splendour, and his cultivation of cultural accomplishment have been consummate and magnificent! How fortunate are scholars to be born into this age! Yet, after such prolonged exposure and ever deeper immersion, will there not be scholars who comprehend the Classics and study antiquity, Confucians who return to essentials and attain unity, who carry forward the lineage of the earlier worthies and…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
下啓來學之傳者出於其間乎愚生諷誦
陳編徒有志焉而未逮也姑述此爲明問
復
第四問
陳王道
同考試官教授陳　批　指陳戰守機宜歷歷
有證雖生長邊陲者不能道其詳如是識時務
者非其人歟敬服
同考試官署郎中劉　批　邊務大略類能指陳
求其計慮精密區畫確當可措諸實用者獨得
===
此篇非素抱經濟者不能宜錄以式
同考試官郎中南　批　戰守之略經生多不
能諳是篇獨詳酌機宜悉有成畫蓋留心經濟
之學者宜錄以式
考試官左諭德汪　批　禦戎之策無過戰守二端是
篇能較計利害而措之區畫一一可行貞儒士
也錄之
執事憤胡虜驁悍慨然爲戰守之詢將需
punctuated:
下啓來學之傳者出於其間乎？愚生諷誦陳編，徒有志焉而未逮也。姑述此爲明問復。

第四問
陳王道

同考試官教授陳批：指陳戰守機宜，歷歷有證，雖生長邊陲者不能道其詳如是。識時務者，非其人歟？敬服。

同考試官署郎中劉批：邊務大略，類能指陳；求其計慮精密、區畫確當、可措諸實用者，獨得此篇。非素抱經濟者不能，宜錄以式。

同考試官郎中南批：戰守之略，經生多不能諳。是篇獨詳酌機宜，悉有成畫，蓋留心經濟之學者，宜錄以式。

考試官左諭德汪批：禦戎之策，無過戰守二端。是篇能較計利害，而措之區畫，一一可行。貞儒士也，錄之。

執事憤胡虜驁悍，慨然爲戰守之詢，將需
translation_en:
…and emerge among them to transmit the learning to future students? I, your humble student, recite the old writings; I have the aspiration, but have yet to attain it. For now, I offer these observations in reply to your illuminating question.

Fourth Question
Chen Wangdao

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: His account of the practical considerations governing attack and defense is clear and supported by evidence throughout. Even someone raised on the frontier could not describe the details so fully. Is he not a man who understands the pressing affairs of the day? I respectfully admire him.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Acting Bureau Director: Most candidates can set out the broad outlines of frontier affairs. But in seeking precise deliberation and sound planning that could be put into actual practice, I found this essay alone. Such work is beyond anyone who has not long nurtured an aptitude for statecraft. It should be included as a model.

Comment by Associate Examiner Nan, Bureau Director: Students of the classics are often unfamiliar with strategies for attack and defense. This essay alone carefully weighs the practical circumstances and offers fully developed plans throughout. Its author evidently devotes himself to the study of statecraft. It should be included as a model.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher: Strategies for resisting the northern enemies come down to two courses: attack and defense. This essay weighs their advantages and disadvantages and embodies its conclusions in plans, each of which is practicable. He is an upright Confucian scholar. Include it.

You, sir, indignant at the northern barbarians’ arrogance and ferocity, have earnestly posed a question about attack and defense, intending to seek…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
才於諸生也愚生鄙陋無以復明問妄圖
其機要誠在靜而防之動而懾之爾夫自
古建立都邑率在北土蓋不止我
朝而我
朝近胡爲甚且如漢襲秦舊都關中匈奴入
寇烽火輒至甘泉唐襲隋舊亦都關中吐
蕃入寇輒至渭橋宋襲周舊都汴西無靈
夏北無燕雲其去元昊爲遠達契丹界直
浹旬耳景德之役亦輒至澶淵三治朝帽
===
帽蓋廣矣而定都若此者何制胡便也我
朝定鼎燕京東北去遼陽尚可數日去漁陽
百里爾西北去雲中尚可數日去上谷亦
僅倍漁陽爾近敵甚則常時封殖者尤勤
常時勤則一旦規畫措置也尤亟是故去
虜之近制虜之便莫有如
今日者也昔漢文帝朝晁錯有實塞分戍臨
陣合刃諸說而文帝取焉唐德宗朝陸贄
有險以固邦國兵以服兇獷諸說而德宗
punctuated:
才於諸生也。愚生鄙陋，無以復明問，妄圖其機要，誠在靜而防之，動而懾之爾。夫自古建立都邑，率在北土，蓋不止我朝，而我朝近胡爲甚。且如漢襲秦舊，都關中，匈奴入寇，烽火輒至甘泉；唐襲隋舊，亦都關中，吐蕃入寇，輒至渭橋；宋襲周舊，都汴，西無靈夏，北無燕雲，其去元昊爲遠，達契丹界直浹旬耳，景德之役，亦輒至澶淵。三治朝帽帽蓋廣矣，而定都若此者何？制胡便也。我朝定鼎燕京，東北去遼陽尚可數日，去漁陽百里爾；西北去雲中尚可數日，去上谷亦僅倍漁陽爾。近敵甚，則常時封殖者尤勤；常時勤，則一旦規畫措置也尤亟。是故去虜之近，制虜之便，莫有如今日者也。
昔漢文帝朝，晁錯有實塞分戍、臨陣合刃諸說，而文帝取焉；唐德宗朝，陸贄有險以固邦國、兵以服兇獷諸說，而德宗
translation_en:
…talent among the students. I, an ignorant and uncultivated student, have nothing with which to answer your discerning question. Yet I venture to consider the essentials: they truly lie in guarding against the enemy when they are inactive and overawing them when they move. From antiquity, capitals have generally been established in the northern lands. This is by no means confined to our dynasty, but our dynasty is especially close to the northern peoples. The Han, for example, followed the precedent of Qin and made its capital in Guanzhong; when the Xiongnu invaded, the beacon alarms would reach Ganquan. The Tang followed the precedent of Sui and likewise made its capital in Guanzhong; when the Tubo invaded, they would reach the Wei Bridge. The Song followed the precedent of Zhou and made its capital at Bian. It lacked Lingzhou and Xiazhou to the west and Yanzhou and Yunzhou to the north. Although comparatively distant from Yuanhao’s territory, it was only ten days’ journey from the Khitan frontier. During the campaign of the Jingde era, the enemy likewise reached Chanyuan. The territories of these three well-governed dynasties were presumably extensive [?]; why, then, did they locate their capitals in this way? Because it facilitated control of the northern peoples. Our dynasty established its capital at Yanjing. To the northeast, Liaoyang is still several days’ journey away, but Yuyang is only a hundred li away. To the northwest, Yunzhong is still several days’ journey away, but Shanggu is only twice as far away as Yuyang. The closer the enemy, the more diligently one ordinarily cultivates and strengthens one’s resources; with such habitual diligence, plans and dispositions can be made all the more swiftly when an emergency arises. Thus, for proximity to the enemy and ease of controlling them, no age has equaled our own.
Formerly, during the reign of Emperor Wen of Han, Chao Cuo offered proposals for populating the frontier, distributing garrisons, confronting the enemy in battle, and engaging in close combat, and Emperor Wen adopted them. During the reign of Emperor Dezong of Tang, Lu Zhi offered proposals for using natural defenses to secure the realm and military forces to subdue the fierce and unruly, and Emperor Dezong…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
取焉宋仁宗朝范仲淹有守兵聚散多寡
戰兵主客勞逸諸說而仁宗亦取焉今其
言載在三史中班班也而豈非經時石畫
哉然而漢卒患匈奴唐卒患吐蕃宋卒患
契丹西夏何也所行與所談悖也今之論
議毋亦類是乎夫分境畫疆秉持阨塞可
謂確矣然外有棄野所傷寔多是移其禍
而以鄰壑當之也於此不得以忘戰也驅
兵策馬衝擊郊原可謂雄矣然內無良材
===
所損非細是積其弱而以異日當之也於
此不得以忘守也守乃可戰而守之弊未
去守可得乎戰乃可守而戰之弊未去戰
可得乎然則竟如之何愚嘗悉其守之弊
而思以易之有五議焉元帝時單于願保
塞罷亭障候應不可以耳目有賴也今燧
墩時被虜毀而亦時加修葺矣如令不行
何令凡候卒丐閒者罪守吏放役者罪虜
入不知知而不傳者罪而末之然也可恃
punctuated:
取焉。宋仁宗朝，范仲淹有守兵聚散多寡、戰兵主客勞逸諸說，而仁宗亦取焉。今其言載在三史中，班班也，而豈非經時石畫哉？然而漢卒患匈奴，唐卒患吐蕃，宋卒患契丹、西夏，何也？所行與所談悖也。今之論議，毋亦類是乎？夫分境畫疆，秉持阨塞，可謂確矣；然外有棄野，所傷寔多，是移其禍而以鄰壑當之也。於此不得以忘戰也。驅兵策馬，衝擊郊原，可謂雄矣；然內無良材，所損非細，是積其弱而以異日當之也。於此不得以忘守也。守乃可戰，而守之弊未去，守可得乎？戰乃可守，而戰之弊未去，戰可得乎？然則竟如之何？愚嘗悉其守之弊，而思以易之，有五議焉。
元帝時，單于願保塞、罷亭障，候應不可以耳目有賴也。今燧墩時被虜毀，而亦時加修葺矣，如令不行何？令凡候卒丐閒者罪，守吏放役者罪，虜入不知、知而不傳者罪，而末之然也，可恃
translation_en:
…adopted them. In the reign of Emperor Renzong of the Song, Fan Zhongyan advanced proposals concerning the concentration and dispersal of defensive troops and their numbers, and concerning whether combat troops were local or brought in from elsewhere, fatigued or rested; Renzong likewise adopted them. Their words are now clearly recorded in the histories of the three dynasties. Were these not rock-solid plans for managing the affairs of their times? Yet the Han ultimately suffered from the Xiongnu, the Tang from the Tubo, and the Song from the Khitan and Western Xia. Why? Their actions contradicted their words. Might present-day deliberations be much the same?
Dividing territories, demarcating boundaries, and holding strategic passes may indeed be called sound measures. Yet when the countryside beyond is abandoned, the harm is very great. This merely shifts the calamity elsewhere, treating neighboring territory as a drainage ditch for it. Here, we must not forget the need to fight. Driving troops and spurring horses to charge across the open country may indeed be called bold. Yet without capable men within, the losses are no small matter. This allows weakness to accumulate, leaving a future day to bear the consequences. Here, we must not forget the need to defend. Only with defense can one fight; but if the defects in defense remain uncorrected, can defense be achieved? Only with fighting can one defend; but if the defects in fighting remain uncorrected, can fighting succeed? What, then, is ultimately to be done? I have sought to understand fully the defects in defense and considered how to change them. I have five proposals.
In the time of Emperor Yuan, the chanyu offered to protect the frontier and asked that its watch posts and fortified outposts be abolished. Hou Ying [?] judged this unacceptable, since these were needed as eyes and ears. Today, beacon towers are repeatedly destroyed by the enemy and repeatedly repaired. But what can be done if orders are not enforced? The orders prescribe punishment for lookout soldiers who beg for time off, for officers in charge who release men from duty, and for those who fail to detect an enemy incursion or detect it but fail to report it. Yet this is not carried out [?]. Can they be relied upon…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
爲耳目歟故嚴亭障者一議也武帝時主
父偃請城朔方從之乃其地可守以屏蔽
有資也今民堡被虜毀幾盡而戍城尚錯
峙矣如法不振何法凡陷一寨者刑陷一
堡者刑陷一戍城者重刑而末之然也可
恃爲屏蔽歟故愼城墉者一議也光武時
罷邊郡車騎材官與民休息隨有夷虜伍
其民補置之民不以爲厲也今里社中豈
無智勇頗格虜者乎而不以自試慮上之
===
人羈縛之耳其著爲令俾團結自衛寛其
他徭或名某甲或名某保無敵相守望有
敵相救助能奪虜所驅者予之得虜首者
官之能守一區者顯擢之有不輕生喜赴
敵者鮮矣故置保伍者一議也趙李牧守
北邊多用間諜知匈奴入急入收保邊固
無亡失也今覘邏之卒豈無智勇能入賊
壘者乎而不以自効緣上之人未嘗優厚
之耳其定爲式務令以夜爲日察得其情
punctuated: 爲耳目歟？故嚴亭障者，一議也。武帝時，主父偃請城朔方，從之，乃其地可守，以屏蔽有資也。今民堡被虜毀幾盡，而戍城尚錯峙矣，如法不振何？法凡陷一寨者刑，陷一堡者刑，陷一戍城者重刑，而末之然也，可恃爲屏蔽歟？故愼城墉者，一議也。光武時，罷邊郡車騎材官，與民休息，隨有夷虜，伍其民補置之，民不以爲厲也。今里社中，豈無智勇頗格虜者乎？而不以自試，慮上之人羈縛之耳。其著爲令，俾團結自衛，寛其他徭，或名某甲，或名某保。無敵相守望，有敵相救助。能奪虜所驅者予之，得虜首者官之，能守一區者顯擢之，有不輕生喜赴敵者鮮矣。故置保伍者，一議也。趙李牧守北邊，多用間諜，知匈奴入，急入收保，邊固無亡失也。今覘邏之卒，豈無智勇能入賊壘者乎？而不以自効，緣上之人未嘗優厚之耳。其定爲式，務令以夜爲日，察得其情
translation_en:
…as eyes and ears? Thus, tightening the administration of watchposts and frontier barriers is one proposal.

In Emperor Wu’s time, Zhufu Yan requested that Shuofang be fortified, and his request was granted: the terrain could be defended and thus afforded a protective screen. Today, civilian forts have almost all been destroyed by the raiders, while garrison towns still stand scattered about. But what can be done if the law is not enforced? The law prescribes punishment for those responsible for the fall of a stockade, punishment for the fall of a fort, and severe punishment for the fall of a garrison town. Yet these provisions are not put into effect [?]. Can these places be relied upon as a protective screen? Thus, attending carefully to fortifications is one proposal.

In Emperor Guangwu’s time, the chariot troops, cavalry, and trained infantry of the frontier commanderies were disbanded to give the people respite. Subsequently, wherever there were foreign tribesmen, local inhabitants were organized into units to replenish these forces [?], and the people did not regard this as an affliction. Surely there are men in today’s village communities whose intelligence and courage enable them to resist the raiders? They do not put themselves to the test simply because they fear that those above them will constrain them. Let an ordinance be promulgated allowing them to organize for self-defense and reducing their other labor services. Their units might be designated such-and-such a jia or such-and-such a bao. When there is no enemy, let them keep watch for one another; when an enemy appears, let them assist one another. Those who recover what the raiders are driving away should be given it; those who take raiders’ heads should receive official appointments; and those who can defend an area should be conspicuously promoted. Few would then fail to disregard their own lives and eagerly confront the enemy. Thus, establishing mutual-defense units is one proposal.

When Li Mu of Zhao defended the northern frontier, he made extensive use of spies. Upon learning that the Xiongnu were invading, he urgently gathered people into fortified refuges [?], so that the frontier remained secure and suffered no losses. Surely among today’s scouts and patrol soldiers there are men with the intelligence and courage to enter enemy strongholds? They do not offer their services simply because those above them have never treated them generously. Let fixed regulations be established, requiring them to make night into day and ascertain the enemy’s circumstances…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而法不爲禁其在行日倍常日衣廩之虜
入無喪失旌酬之有功亦準級而爵之不
幸而埸虜取其家贍養之有不毅然請行
的知虜動靜者鮮矣故任間諜者一議也
建武中烏桓郝旦等朝貢留居塞上令爲
偵候識者以爲自詒之慼也今處屬夷非
其遺意乎而不敢遽圖懼速釁耳其與爲
約能歲致虜不寇者賞能誘致虜使敗者
賞委曲以縻之俾不我叛從容以引之俾
===
不彼從久之亦且有濟矣故解黨與者一
議也是五議者其所爲守而靜以防之之
道乎愚又甞悉其戰之弊而思以易之亦
有五議焉趙奢爲韓敵秦軍中候進言斬
之乃許歷進言不斬更兩用其說解閼與
圍討慮不可徇亦不可專也今軍中有以
非計進斷而誅之者乎有以善計進斷而
予之者乎徇人者北自專者北無與言功
矣故審計慮者一議也田單守卽墨致燕
punctuated:
而法不爲禁。其在行日，倍常日衣廩之；虜入無喪失，旌酬之；有功，亦準級而爵之；不幸而埸虜，取其家贍養之。有不毅然請行、的知虜動靜者鮮矣。故任間諜者，一議也。
建武中，烏桓郝旦等朝貢，留居塞上，令爲偵候，識者以爲自詒之慼也。今處屬夷，非其遺意乎？而不敢遽圖，懼速釁耳。其與爲約：能歲致虜不寇者賞，能誘致虜使敗者賞。委曲以縻之，俾不我叛；從容以引之，俾不彼從。久之，亦且有濟矣。故解黨與者，一議也。
是五議者，其所爲守而靜以防之之道乎？愚又甞悉其戰之弊，而思以易之，亦有五議焉。
趙奢爲韓敵秦，軍中候進言，斬之；乃許歷進言不斬，更兩用其說，解閼與圍。討慮不可徇，亦不可專也。今軍中有以非計進，斷而誅之者乎？有以善計進，斷而予之者乎？徇人者北，自專者北，無與言功矣。故審計慮者，一議也。
田單守卽墨，致燕
translation_en:
…and the law should not prohibit it. For each day they are on assignment, provide them with twice their usual clothing allowance and grain ration. If an enemy incursion causes no losses, commend and reward them; if they render meritorious service, likewise confer rank according to the prescribed grades. If, unfortunately, they fall to the enemy [?], take their families into support. Few would then fail to volunteer resolutely and ascertain the enemy’s movements precisely. Thus, employing spies is one proposal.
During the Jianwu reign, Hao Dan and others of the Wuhuan came to present tribute. They were retained on the frontier and ordered to serve as scouts. Discerning men considered this an invitation to trouble. Does our present arrangement for the subject tribes not follow that precedent? Yet we dare not hastily devise changes, merely for fear of precipitating conflict. We should make an agreement with them: reward those who can keep the enemy from raiding throughout the year, and reward those who can lure the enemy into defeat. Accommodate them in every way to retain their allegiance, so that they do not rebel against us; patiently draw them toward us, so that they do not follow the enemy. In time, this too should produce results. Thus, breaking up the enemy’s alliances is one proposal.
Are these five proposals not the means of defending against them through steadfast, quiet resistance? I have also examined the defects in our conduct of battle and considered how to remedy them. Here too I have five proposals.
When Zhao She opposed Qin on behalf of Han, a military commandant offered advice, and he executed him. Yet when Xu Li offered advice, he did not execute him; instead, he adopted his counsel on two occasions and relieved the siege of Eyu. In deliberating strategy [?], one must neither blindly follow others nor decide entirely alone. In the army today, when someone advances an unsound plan, is there anyone who decisively executes him? When someone advances a good plan, is there anyone who decisively rewards him? Those who blindly follow others are defeated; those who act solely on their own judgment are defeated. With such men there can be no talk of achievement. Thus, carefully assessing plans is one proposal.
When Tian Dan defended Jimo, he induced the men of Yan …

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
人劓齊軍掘齊軍先墓齊軍皆奮泣出戰
遂敗燕師心志不可攜亦不可懈也今有
能激其衆使皆奮泣乎使皆願戰而不能
止乎心攜者北心懈者北無與言功矣故
齊心志者一議也孫權之於周泰也以其
身被多矢卽撤所張蓋賜之泰感而自効
成三分漢鼎之功今能爲權乎有勞不知
反朘削之有功不錄反掩取之其誰德我
而忘生爲也故鼓精强者一議也李光弼
===
之於郝廷玉懷恩也以其少自退却卽下
令取其首矣二人奮而死戰成再造唐室
之烈今能爲光弼乎或奸旗鼓不敢卽刑
或避鋒鏑不敢卽刑其誰憚我而忘死爲
也故懲怯懦者一議也漢伐右渠兩將軍
不協朝鮮幾危而唐之賀蘭不以兵進則
睢陽陷矣今能知同仇之義乎地壤邇甚
聞若罔聞營壁邇甚見若罔見非所以戮
力公家也而可無以示誡歟故明捄援者
punctuated: 人劓齊軍，掘齊軍先墓，齊軍皆奮泣出戰，遂敗燕師。心志不可攜，亦不可懈也。今有能激其衆，使皆奮泣乎？使皆願戰而不能止乎？心攜者北，心懈者北，無與言功矣。故齊心志者，一議也。孫權之於周泰也，以其身被多矢，卽撤所張蓋賜之。泰感而自効，成三分漢鼎之功。今能爲權乎？有勞不知，反朘削之；有功不錄，反掩取之。其誰德我而忘生爲也？故鼓精强者，一議也。李光弼之於郝廷玉、懷恩也，以其少自退却，卽下令取其首矣。二人奮而死戰，成再造唐室之烈。今能爲光弼乎？或奸旗鼓，不敢卽刑；或避鋒鏑，不敢卽刑。其誰憚我而忘死爲也？故懲怯懦者，一議也。漢伐右渠，兩將軍不協，朝鮮幾危；而唐之賀蘭不以兵進，則睢陽陷矣。今能知同仇之義乎？地壤邇甚，聞若罔聞；營壁邇甚，見若罔見。非所以戮力公家也，而可無以示誡歟？故明捄援者
translation_en:
…men to cut off the noses of Qi soldiers and dig up their ancestors’ graves. The Qi soldiers all went out to fight, weeping with indignation, and thereupon defeated the Yan army. The soldiers’ resolve must neither be divided nor grow slack. Is there anyone now who can rouse his troops so that they all weep with indignation, so that all wish to fight and cannot be restrained? Those whose resolve is divided are defeated; those whose resolve grows slack are defeated. There can be no talk of achievement with them. Thus, unifying the soldiers’ resolve is one proposal.

As for Sun Quan’s treatment of Zhou Tai, because Tai’s body had been struck by many arrows, Quan immediately took down the canopy erected over himself and bestowed it upon him. Moved by this, Tai devoted himself to service and helped accomplish the division of the Han realm into three. Can anyone today act as Quan did? When men have rendered service, it goes unrecognized; instead, they are exploited. When they have achieved merit, it goes unrecorded; instead, their achievements are concealed and appropriated. Who, then, would feel gratitude toward us and act without regard for his own life? Thus, encouraging vigor and strength is one proposal.

As for Li Guangbi’s treatment of Hao Tingyu and Huaien, because they had fallen back slightly, he immediately ordered their heads taken. The two men rallied and fought to the death, accomplishing the glorious feat of restoring the Tang ruling house. Can anyone today act as Guangbi did? Some disobey the signals of flags and drums, yet we dare not punish them immediately; others evade blades and arrows, yet we dare not punish them immediately. Who, then, would stand in awe of us and act without fear of death? Thus, punishing cowardice is one proposal.

When the Han attacked Youqu, its two generals failed to cooperate, and the campaign in Chaoxian nearly came to disaster [?]. Under the Tang, Helan failed to advance with his troops, and Suiyang consequently fell. Do men today understand the duty of confronting a common enemy?
