Their territories lie very close, yet they hear as though they heard nothing; their fortified camps lie very close, yet they see as though they saw nothing. This is no way to unite their efforts in service to the state. Can we fail to issue a warning? Thus, making clear the duty to provide relief and reinforcement is…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
一議也是五議者其所爲戰而動以衞之
之道乎夫守有要也比見守者據堂奧棄
門户失要甚矣借重地而自飾擁重兵而
自全他所不恤也而何以爲守乎戰有機
也比見戰者縱虜入縱虜歸失機甚矣掩
實衂而避誅張僞捷而徼寵他所不恤也
而何以爲戰乎是故守失其要非守矣而
得要者又必以戰爲守焉戰失其機非戰
矣而得機者又必以守爲戰焉何謂以戰
===
爲守蓋因戰而勝敵常懼也懼則視我之
瑕且以爲堅而况於堅乎視我之虚且以
爲實而况於實乎至是則我便於制敵敵
不便於制我彼安能久持境上必待吾衰
而入之耶是戰也益以固吾不可奪之勢
者也何謂以守爲戰蓋因守而固敵常疑
也疑則進不能前慮吾前之而銳氣消退
不能後慮吾後之而惰氣長至是則我利
於襲敵敵不利於襲我彼安能久居塞内
punctuated:
一議也。是五議者，其所爲戰而動以衞之之道乎？夫守有要也，比見守者據堂奧，棄門户，失要甚矣！借重地而自飾，擁重兵而自全，他所不恤也，而何以爲守乎？戰有機也，比見戰者縱虜入，縱虜歸，失機甚矣！掩實衂而避誅，張僞捷而徼寵，他所不恤也，而何以爲戰乎？是故守失其要，非守矣；而得要者，又必以戰爲守焉。戰失其機，非戰矣；而得機者，又必以守爲戰焉。
何謂以戰爲守？蓋因戰而勝，敵常懼也。懼則視我之瑕，且以爲堅，而况於堅乎？視我之虚，且以爲實，而况於實乎？至是則我便於制敵，敵不便於制我。彼安能久持境上，必待吾衰而入之耶？是戰也，益以固吾不可奪之勢者也。
何謂以守爲戰？蓋因守而固，敵常疑也。疑則進不能前，慮吾前之而銳氣消；退不能後，慮吾後之而惰氣長。至是則我利於襲敵，敵不利於襲我。彼安能久居塞内
translation_en:
…is one proposal. Are these five proposals the way to conduct warfare and take action to defend the realm? Defense has its essentials. Recently, those charged with defense have held the inner chambers while abandoning the gates: they have gravely neglected those essentials! They use their strategically important positions to embellish their own standing and keep large forces at hand to protect themselves, caring for nothing else. How can this count as defense? Battle has its opportune moments. Recently, those charged with fighting have let the enemy enter and let the enemy withdraw: they have gravely missed those opportunities! They conceal actual defeats to escape execution and proclaim fictitious victories to seek favor, caring for nothing else. How can this count as fighting? Thus, defense that misses its essentials is no defense; yet those who grasp its essentials must also use fighting as a means of defense. Fighting that misses its opportunities is no fighting; yet those who seize its opportunities must also use defense as a means of fighting.
What does it mean to use fighting as a means of defense? When fighting brings victory, the enemy remains fearful. In fear, they regard even our weak points as strong—how much more our actual strengths! They regard even our emptiness as fullness—how much more our actual fullness! At this point, we are well placed to control the enemy, while the enemy is poorly placed to control us. How could they hold out long along the frontier, determined to wait until we weaken before entering? Such fighting further secures our unassailable position.
What does it mean to use defense as a means of fighting? When defense makes our position secure, the enemy remains uncertain. In uncertainty, they cannot advance: fearing that we will confront them, their fighting spirit ebbs. Nor can they retreat: fearing that we will pursue them, their listlessness grows. At this point, we have the advantage in striking the enemy, while the enemy is at a disadvantage in striking us. How could they remain long within the frontier…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
必何吾隙而乘之耶是守也益以伸吾不
可加之威者也守矣而戰不專於守戰矣
而守不專於戰能闔能闢能卷能舒變化
轉移應用不滯其斯爲疆場之臣乎大抵
疆場之臣防虜在智慑虜在勇靖虜在忠
頃者
簡任諸臣固謂素具乎此也乃未見卓樹奇
績當
主上心毋亦有待耶
===
主上思建萬世長策輒假其人便宜之權無事
而聽其封殖不從中制也有事而聽其規
畫不從中制也一有
請疏即夜分必下樞筦臣以行不從中制也
而績尚有待耶愚知疆場之臣無一時自
寧於心矣夫全寧徙忠叢叢於遼左漁陽矣
今處遼左漁陽也得不以全寧爲鑒乎開
平興和遷忠叢於上谷矣今處上谷也得
不以開平興和爲鑒乎東勝移忠叢於雲
punctuated:
必何吾隙而乘之耶？是守也，益以伸吾不可加之威者也。守矣而戰，不專於守；戰矣而守，不專於戰。能闔能闢，能卷能舒，變化轉移，應用不滯，其斯爲疆場之臣乎？大抵疆場之臣，防虜在智，慑虜在勇，靖虜在忠。頃者簡任諸臣，固謂素具乎此也，乃未見卓樹奇績當主上心，毋亦有待耶？

主上思建萬世長策，輒假其人便宜之權。無事而聽其封殖，不從中制也；有事而聽其規畫，不從中制也；一有請疏，即夜分，必下樞筦臣以行，不從中制也。而績尚有待耶？愚知疆場之臣無一時自寧於心矣。夫全寧徙忠叢叢於遼左、漁陽矣，今處遼左、漁陽也，得不以全寧爲鑒乎？開平、興和遷忠叢於上谷矣，今處上谷也，得不以開平、興和爲鑒乎？東勝移忠叢於雲
translation_en:
…must they seek out [?] a gap in our defenses and exploit it? Such defense serves further to extend our might, which none can overcome. While defending, we fight, without devoting ourselves exclusively to defense; while fighting, we defend, without devoting ourselves exclusively to battle. Able to close and open, to contract and expand, adapting and shifting, responding to circumstances without impediment—are these not the qualities of officials serving on the frontier? In general, frontier officials rely on wisdom to guard against the enemy, courage to overawe them, and loyalty to pacify them. When the officials were recently selected and appointed, it was surely thought that they had long possessed these qualities. Yet we have seen no outstanding achievements to satisfy His Majesty. Can it be that these must still await their time?

His Majesty wishes to establish a lasting strategy for ten thousand generations, and accordingly grants these men authority to act as circumstances require. In quiet times, he allows them to cultivate and strengthen their resources, without interference from the court. When trouble arises, he allows them to devise their plans, without interference from the court. Whenever a memorial requesting action arrives, even in the middle of the night, he invariably refers it to the officials directing military affairs for implementation, without interference from the court. Must achievements nevertheless still await their time? I know that frontier officials cannot for a single moment feel at ease in their hearts. Quanning was relocated to Liaozuo and Yuyang [?; the wording 徙忠叢叢 is garbled]. Can those now stationed in Liaozuo and Yuyang fail to take Quanning as a warning? Kaiping and Xinghe were relocated to Shanggu [?; 遷忠叢 is garbled]. Can those now stationed in Shanggu fail to take Kaiping and Xinghe as a warning? Dongsheng was relocated [?; 移忠叢 is garbled] to Yun…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
中矣今處雲中也得不以東勝爲鑒乎愚
故知疆場之臣無一時自寧於心也夫心
不自寧卽大智大勇大忠胥由之出而萬
世長策從此建矣愚生未履疆場闇於大
計竊欲比晁陸范諸人故不覺論議至此
執事取之或可裨幕中一畫云
第五問
葉初春
同考試官主事吳　批〔指陳往迹鑿鑿有見且文詞高古議論精覈非但可以經生目之也〕
===
考試官左諭德汪　批〔區畫有條而敷答詳盡子其能握長勝之筭者歟〕
〔尤宜首錄〕
善用兵者以全取勝故順天時也因地利
也盡人謀也三者具而制勝之略盡焉矣
天時者何配時日於孤虛察精祲於玄象
而趨避之機存焉地利者何覈虛實向背
之形辨勞逸險易之勢而控制之方寓焉
punctuated:
中矣。今處雲中也，得不以東勝爲鑒乎？愚故知疆場之臣無一時自寧於心也。夫心不自寧，卽大智、大勇、大忠胥由之出，而萬世長策從此建矣。愚生未履疆場，闇於大計，竊欲比晁、陸、范諸人，故不覺論議至此。執事取之，或可裨幕中一畫云。

第五問
葉初春
同考試官主事吳批〔指陳往迹，鑿鑿有見，且文詞高古，議論精覈，非但可以經生目之也。〕
考試官左諭德汪批〔區畫有條，而敷答詳盡，子其能握長勝之筭者歟？〕〔尤宜首錄。〕

善用兵者，以全取勝，故順天時也，因地利也，盡人謀也。三者具，而制勝之略盡焉矣。天時者何？配時日於孤虛，察精祲於玄象，而趨避之機存焉。地利者何？覈虛實向背之形，辨勞逸險易之勢，而控制之方寓焉。
translation_en:
…in Yunzhong. Can those now stationed in Yunzhong fail to take Dongsheng as a warning? Thus I know that officials on the frontier cannot for a moment feel at ease. From this unease arise great wisdom, great courage, and great loyalty alike; upon it enduring plans for ten thousand generations are established. I, an unworthy scholar, have never set foot on the frontier and am ignorant of grand strategy. Yet privately aspiring to emulate such men as Chao, Lu, and Fan, I have unwittingly carried my discussion this far. If you, sir, find it acceptable, it may perhaps contribute a single plan to the deliberations of your headquarters.

Fifth Question
Ye Chuchun
Associate Examiner Wu, Secretary, comments: 〔His references to past events are precise and show insight. Moreover, his language is elevated and antique, and his arguments exact and thoroughly examined. He cannot be regarded merely as a student of the Classics.〕
Examiner Wang, Left Mentor, comments: 〔His plans are orderly, and his exposition detailed and comprehensive. Might you be one who commands the calculations that ensure lasting victory?〕〔Especially deserving of being selected first.〕

Those skilled in warfare achieve victory with everything intact. Accordingly, they follow Heaven’s timing, exploit the advantages of terrain, and make the fullest use of human planning. When these three are present, the means of securing victory are complete. What is Heaven’s timing? It means correlating hours and days with the “solitary” and “empty” positions in divination, and observing auspicious and baleful influences in celestial configurations: therein lies the key to knowing what to pursue and what to avoid. What are the advantages of terrain? They mean examining configurations of weakness and strength, favorable and unfavorable orientations, and distinguishing circumstances of exhaustion and rest, difficult and easy ground: therein lie the methods of strategic control.

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
人謀者何明審法令揣摩彼已訓練士卒
繕齊器械而折衝禦侮之術備焉故上觀
天道下察地理中酌物情三者賢豪之士
明智之將所不廢也雖然其輕重有等先
後有倫則又不可得而昧者故兵法曰先
修人事次盡地利後觀天時則萬舉而萬
全身安而國盛也其不然乎請因明問而
復之夫兵凶器也戰逆道也呼吸異宜勝
負分焉瞬息異用存亡決焉兵可易言乎
===
自夫兵家者流以生克為勝負以陰陽為
變化而天時之說準焉矣計遠近險阨以
待敵為鈎連曲折以盡數而地利之說準
焉矣講武治兵以作六師明法飭備以除
戎器而人謀之說準焉矣不特此也以星
宿孤虛列為天陣以山川向背布為地陣
以編伍彌縫著為人陣而取象效法無不
具焉矣三者其可一闕乎今夫兵之少勝
多敗者不能知此三者也賭勝賭敗者知
punctuated:
人謀者何？明審法令，揣摩彼已，訓練士卒，繕齊器械，而折衝禦侮之術備焉。故上觀天道，下察地理，中酌物情，三者賢豪之士、明智之將所不廢也。雖然，其輕重有等，先後有倫，則又不可得而昧者。故兵法曰：「先修人事，次盡地利，後觀天時，則萬舉而萬全，身安而國盛也。」其不然乎？請因明問而復之。夫兵，凶器也；戰，逆道也。呼吸異宜，勝負分焉；瞬息異用，存亡決焉。兵可易言乎？
自夫兵家者流，以生克為勝負，以陰陽為變化，而天時之說準焉矣；計遠近險阨以待敵，為鈎連曲折以盡數，而地利之說準焉矣；講武治兵以作六師，明法飭備以除戎器，而人謀之說準焉矣。不特此也，以星宿孤虛列為天陣，以山川向背布為地陣，以編伍彌縫著為人陣，而取象效法無不具焉矣。三者其可一闕乎？今夫兵之少勝多敗者，不能知此三者也；賭勝賭敗者，知
translation_en:
What is human planning? It consists in making laws and commands clear and examining them carefully, assessing the enemy and oneself [?], training officers and soldiers, and repairing and putting weapons and equipment in order. Thus the arts of repelling assaults and resisting aggression are fully provided for. Accordingly, one observes the Way of Heaven above, examines the configurations of the land below, and weighs the circumstances of things in between. These three are matters that worthy and outstanding men and discerning, intelligent generals never neglect. Nevertheless, they differ in importance and have a proper order of precedence; this, too, must not be overlooked. Thus the military treatise says: “First put human affairs in order; next make full use of the advantages of terrain; afterward observe Heaven’s timing. Then every undertaking will be entirely secure, one’s person will be safe, and the state will flourish.” Is this not so? Allow me to respond in accordance with your discerning question. Weapons are instruments of ill omen; warfare runs counter to the proper Way. A difference in what is appropriate within a single breath separates victory from defeat; a difference in action within an instant decides survival or destruction. Can military affairs be discussed lightly?
Ever since the military specialists took the cycles of generation and conquest as determining victory and defeat, and yin and yang as governing transformations, the doctrine of Heaven’s timing has had its established principles. They calculated distances and assessed dangerous passes to await the enemy, and devised interlocking and winding dispositions to exhaust the possibilities; thus the doctrine of the advantages of terrain has had its established principles. They practiced martial skills and put their troops in order to rouse the Six Armies, clarified regulations and set preparations in order to refurbish military equipment; thus the doctrine of human planning has had its established principles. Nor is this all. They used the stellar lodges and the “solitary” and “vacant” positions of military divination to arrange heavenly formations; used the orientations of mountains and rivers to deploy earthly formations; and used the organization of ranks and the closing of gaps to establish human formations. Thus nothing was lacking in their adoption of images and emulation of models. Can any one of these three be dispensed with? Now, those who win few battles and lose many fail to understand these three; those who gamble on victory or defeat know …

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之而不能全也全此三者故無不勝矣昔
漢任宏論次兵書別爲四種其所謂陰陽
者卽綜天時以盡變也形勢者審地形以
盡利也權謀技巧者修人事以盡謀也宏
之言非所謂決機握筭善言兵者歟然此
非宏之言也孫武子葢嘗言之矣其見於
始計之篇曰天地孰得則有以通乎上下
矣其曰兵衆孰强則有以該乎物情矣武
之著論非所謂察微通變者耶亦非武之
===
言也太公望葢言之詳矣其曰星曆風氣
非天時之謂耶遠近險易非地利之謂乎
行事成敗非人謀之謂耶此非識權達化
明於三才之道妙於機宜之術者何以與
此試以往事徵之而知其說矣何則天有
顯象吉凶著焉故歲星南見非晉之分野
所屬乎而謝玄淝水之捷有以適逢其會
矣月行掩昴非旄頭之國所當乎而崔浩
北伐之請有以豫識其幾矣薛仁貴之擊
punctuated: 之而不能全也。全此三者，故無不勝矣。昔漢任宏論次兵書，別爲四種。其所謂陰陽者，卽綜天時以盡變也；形勢者，審地形以盡利也；權謀技巧者，修人事以盡謀也。宏之言，非所謂決機握筭、善言兵者歟？然此非宏之言也，孫武子葢嘗言之矣。其見於《始計》之篇曰：「天地孰得？」則有以通乎上下矣。其曰：「兵衆孰强？」則有以該乎物情矣。武之著論，非所謂察微通變者耶？亦非武之言也，太公望葢言之詳矣。其曰星曆風氣，非天時之謂耶？遠近險易，非地利之謂乎？行事成敗，非人謀之謂耶？此非識權達化、明於三才之道、妙於機宜之術者，何以與此？試以往事徵之，而知其說矣。何則？天有顯象，吉凶著焉。故歲星南見，非晉之分野所屬乎？而謝玄淝水之捷，有以適逢其會矣。月行掩昴，非旄頭之國所當乎？而崔浩北伐之請，有以豫識其幾矣。薛仁貴之擊
translation_en: …them, yet cannot fully encompass them. Fully encompassing these three factors therefore ensures victory in every case. Formerly, Ren Hong of the Han classified and arranged military writings into four categories. What he called “yin and yang” comprehensively treats Heaven’s timing to account for every change; “dispositions and configurations” examines the terrain to exploit every advantage; and “strategic planning” and “technical skills” cultivate human affairs to exhaust the possibilities of planning. Do not Hong’s words exemplify what is meant by judging the critical moment, holding the winning calculations, and speaking expertly of warfare? Yet these ideas did not originate with Hong: Master Sun Wu had already spoken of them. In his chapter “Initial Assessments,” he says, “Which side enjoys the advantages of Heaven and Earth?” This provides a means of comprehending what is above and below. When he says, “Which side’s troops are stronger?” this provides a means of encompassing the actual circumstances of things. Does not Wu’s written discussion exemplify what is meant by discerning subtleties and comprehending change? Nor did these ideas originate with Wu: Taigong Wang had already discussed them in detail. When he speaks of the stars, calendrical calculations, winds, and atmospheric influences, does he not mean Heaven’s timing? Do distance and proximity, difficult and easy terrain, not refer to the advantages of the land? Do success and failure in conducting affairs not refer to human planning? How could anyone attain such understanding without recognizing expedient measures and comprehending transformation, understanding the Way of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—and mastering the arts of responding appropriately to circumstances? Test this against past events, and the validity of the argument becomes clear. Why is this? Heaven displays visible signs in which good and ill fortune are manifest. Thus, when Jupiter appeared in the south, was this not within the celestial region corresponding to Jin? Xie Xuan’s victory at the Fei River duly coincided with that moment. When the moon passed over and occulted the lunar lodge Mao, did this not bear upon the country associated with the Hairy Head stars? Cui Hao’s request for a northern expedition thus showed his advance recognition of the incipient opportunity. When Xue Rengui attacked…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
吐蕃也謂歲在庚午西行者敗非逆之而
凶者乎李晟之平朱泚也謂熒惑退舍用
兵者昌非順之而吉者乎夫象緯見於上
而事幾應於下不可誣也雖然有宋武之
紀律則時日之背不計也有孝恭之忠勇
則杯酒之變不卻也蓋禁疑去祥轉禍爲
福此又識微知著者能之耳安可以一端
盡哉地有險易强弱分焉彼趙奢納許歷
之計先據北山而秦軍破卒著救韓之功
===
矣馬援奪水草之利絕山依谷而諸酋遁
卒樹定羌之績矣賊兵乘勝勢何熾也光
弼移軍河陽北阻澤潞使驕賊睥睨而不
敢窺者非所謂批亢擣虛形格勢禁則自
爲解者耶虜騎侵軼力難支矣潘美襲取
固軍奪其要害使黠胡逡巡而不敢近者
非所謂主客勞逸倏忽變易能制其命者
耶夫險易既分安危懸絕惡可不審也雖
然有淮陰奇詭之謀自能蹂轢彊陣而陷
punctuated:
吐蕃也，謂歲在庚午，西行者敗，非逆之而凶者乎？李晟之平朱泚也，謂熒惑退舍，用兵者昌，非順之而吉者乎？夫象緯見於上，而事幾應於下，不可誣也。雖然，有宋武之紀律，則時日之背不計也；有孝恭之忠勇，則杯酒之變不卻也。蓋禁疑去祥，轉禍爲福，此又識微知著者能之耳，安可以一端盡哉？

地有險易，强弱分焉。彼趙奢納許歷之計，先據北山而秦軍破，卒著救韓之功矣。馬援奪水草之利，絕山依谷而諸酋遁，卒樹定羌之績矣。賊兵乘勝，勢何熾也！光弼移軍河陽，北阻澤潞，使驕賊睥睨而不敢窺者，非所謂批亢擣虛，形格勢禁，則自爲解者耶？虜騎侵軼，力難支矣！潘美襲取固軍，奪其要害，使黠胡逡巡而不敢近者，非所謂主客勞逸，倏忽變易，能制其命者耶？夫險易既分，安危懸絕，惡可不審也？雖然，有淮陰奇詭之謀，自能蹂轢彊陣而陷
translation_en:
…when attacking Tubo, it was said that the year was gengwu and that those who marched west would be defeated. Was this not a case of defying the celestial signs and meeting disaster? When Li Sheng suppressed Zhu Ci, it was said that Mars was retreating from its celestial lodge and that those who took up arms would prosper. Was this not a case of following the signs and meeting good fortune? Celestial configurations appear above, and the critical turns of events respond below: this cannot be denied. Nevertheless, with the military discipline of Emperor Wu of Song, one need not reckon with unfavorable times and days; with Xiaogong’s loyalty and courage, one need not recoil at an uncanny change in a cup of wine. For suppressing doubts and setting aside omens, thereby turning calamity into good fortune, is something that only those who discern the subtle and recognize what will become manifest can accomplish. How could any single principle encompass it all?

Terrain has its difficult and easy features, which determine relative strength and weakness. Zhao She accepted Xu Li’s plan, occupied the northern hill first, and defeated the Qin army, ultimately winning distinction for rescuing Han. Ma Yuan seized the advantages of water and pasture, crossed the mountains and kept to the valleys, putting the various chieftains to flight and ultimately establishing his achievement in pacifying the Qiang. How formidable was the momentum of the rebel troops as they rode their victories! Guangbi moved his army to Heyang and blocked access to Zezhou and Luzhou in the north, so that the arrogant rebels could glare at him but dared not attempt an incursion. Was this not what is meant by striking the enemy’s vital point and attacking his undefended places, so that, constrained in his dispositions and checked in his momentum, he withdraws of his own accord? When enemy cavalry invaded, their force was hard to withstand! Pan Mei took Gujun [?] by surprise and seized its strategic positions, making the cunning northern foes hesitate and dare not approach. Was this not what is meant by swiftly reversing the respective positions of defender and invader, of weary and rested troops, and thus gaining control over the enemy’s fate? Once the advantages and disadvantages of terrain are distinguished, safety and danger stand far apart. How could one fail to examine them carefully? Nevertheless, with the extraordinary and ingenious plans of the Marquis of Huaiyin, one can trample through strong battle formations and plunge …

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之亡地可也有韓世忠必勝之策自能遏
禦奔衝而塞之歸路可也盖隨宜設變因
地制形此所論於方略之外者耳安可執
一求哉至於盡人謀修軍政摧敵制勝攻
取守固此古今論兵者必先以得人爲之
本故秦楚之技擊不足以當桓文之節制
桓文之節制不足以當湯武之仁義言之
較然不待辨也昔孔明負王佐之才昭烈
舉國而聽之任將擇材練兵選士故能恢
===
復漢室定鼎三分掎角羣雄樹勳當代焉
周瑜具豪邁之識孫權悉討而從之請兵
拒敵力排羣議故能擊走强魏易如拉朽
開闢荆土勢若轉圜焉子儀平安史之亂
却吐蕃之侵再造王室厥勳茂矣而稽其
功實非以賞罰明而威信著耶李愬靖蔡
州之難擒元濟之奸安民保衆厥功偉矣
而綜其行事非以計慮周而誠信孚耶故
將苟知兵則整齊和附士卒樂用何堅之
punctuated: 之亡地可也。有韓世忠必勝之策，自能遏禦奔衝而塞之歸路可也。盖隨宜設變，因地制形，此所論於方略之外者耳，安可執一求哉？至於盡人謀，修軍政，摧敵制勝，攻取守固，此古今論兵者必先以得人爲之本。故秦楚之技擊不足以當桓文之節制，桓文之節制不足以當湯武之仁義，言之較然，不待辨也。昔孔明負王佐之才，昭烈舉國而聽之，任將擇材，練兵選士，故能恢復漢室，定鼎三分，掎角羣雄，樹勳當代焉。周瑜具豪邁之識，孫權悉討而從之，請兵拒敵，力排羣議，故能擊走强魏，易如拉朽；開闢荆土，勢若轉圜焉。子儀平安史之亂，却吐蕃之侵，再造王室，厥勳茂矣。而稽其功實，非以賞罰明而威信著耶？李愬靖蔡州之難，擒元濟之奸，安民保衆，厥功偉矣。而綜其行事，非以計慮周而誠信孚耶？故將苟知兵，則整齊和附，士卒樂用，何堅之
translation_en:
…them into deadly ground, and this is acceptable. With Han Shizhong’s strategy for certain victory, one can check a headlong charge and block the enemy’s route of retreat, and this too is acceptable. Adapting one’s measures to circumstances and shaping one’s dispositions according to the terrain belong to what must be discussed beyond prescribed strategies. How could one insist on a single approach?

As for making the fullest use of human planning, putting military administration in order, crushing the enemy and securing victory, taking positions by assault and holding them firmly: those who discuss warfare, ancient and modern alike, must first make finding the right men their foundation. Thus the fighting skills of Qin and Chu could not match the disciplined command of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin; nor could their disciplined command match the benevolence and righteousness of Tang and Wu. This is manifestly clear and needs no debate.

Formerly, Kongming possessed the talent to assist a true king, and Emperor Zhaolie entrusted the entire state to his direction. He appointed commanders and chose capable men, trained troops and selected fighting men. Thus he was able to restore the Han imperial house, establish its throne in a realm divided into three, confront the rival warlords through coordinated operations, and win distinction in his age. Zhou Yu possessed bold and far-reaching discernment. Sun Quan fully consulted him [?] and followed his advice. Zhou requested troops to resist the enemy and vigorously opposed the assembled dissenting opinions. Thus he routed mighty Wei as easily as snapping rotten wood, and opened up the territory of Jing with the ease of rolling a ball.

Ziyi quelled the rebellion of An and Shi, repelled the Tibetan invasion, and restored the imperial house: his achievements were outstanding. Yet, if we examine the substance of his accomplishments, was this not because his rewards and punishments were clear, and his authority and trustworthiness manifest? Li Su pacified the troubles in Caizhou, captured the treacherous Yuanji, and brought peace to the people and protection to the populace: his achievements were great. Yet, if we consider his actions as a whole, was this not because his planning was thorough and his sincerity inspired trust? Thus, if a commander understands warfare, his troops will be orderly, united, and loyal, and his soldiers willing to serve. What strong position …

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
不可瑕何釁之不可批哉若馬謖之守正
而無救於街亭之敗房琯之談兵而卒致
陳濤之潰失律僨師罪莫甚焉惡在其能
修人事耶於戲帝王之師以全取勝故三
者廢一不可也後世兵家者流縱橫闔闢
出奇效詭雖變化不窮而卒莫能舍此三
者故良將愼擇而善應之以爲全師保勝
之道世儒不權輕重猥云德化乃執拘攣
之說而忘善事之圖明於此而闇於彼得
===
其一而遺其二者又惡足以與於三軍之
權也哉雖然三者重矣而人和要焉故曰
任時不如任法任法不如任人彼舍人而
談天者則撤藩胥寇其不爲墨翟之守者
幾希據險而廢謀者則憑陵自恃其不爲
旅焚之圖者幾希是以握機決勝之士諰
諰焉務盡人謀以合天心修德政以固形
勢其慮之也周守之也密而動之也愼布
恩威明賞罰以至公而服其心謹號令責
punctuated:
不可瑕，何釁之不可批哉？若馬謖之守正，而無救於街亭之敗；房琯之談兵，而卒致陳濤之潰，失律僨師，罪莫甚焉，惡在其能修人事耶？於戲！帝王之師，以全取勝，故三者廢一不可也。後世兵家者流，縱橫闔闢，出奇效詭，雖變化不窮，而卒莫能舍此三者。故良將愼擇而善應之，以爲全師保勝之道。世儒不權輕重，猥云德化，乃執拘攣之說，而忘善事之圖，明於此而闇於彼，得其一而遺其二者，又惡足以與於三軍之權也哉？
雖然，三者重矣，而人和要焉。故曰：「任時不如任法，任法不如任人。」彼舍人而談天者，則撤藩胥寇，其不爲墨翟之守者幾希；據險而廢謀者，則憑陵自恃，其不爲旅焚之圖者幾希。是以握機決勝之士，諰諰焉務盡人謀，以合天心，修德政以固形勢。其慮之也周，守之也密，而動之也愼。布恩威，明賞罰，以至公而服其心；謹號令，責
translation_en:
…cannot be breached, and what opening cannot be exploited? Consider Ma Su, whose adherence to orthodox methods could not avert defeat at Jieting, or Fang Guan, whose talk of warfare ultimately brought about the rout at Chentao. For violating military discipline and ruining an army, no guilt could be greater. Where was their ability to attend properly to human affairs? Alas! The armies of emperors and kings seek victory while preserving their forces intact; thus none of these three factors can be dispensed with. Military strategists of later ages maneuvered freely, opening and closing, deploying surprises and practicing deception. Though their variations were inexhaustible, ultimately they could not abandon these three factors. Thus good generals choose carefully and respond skillfully, making this the way to preserve their armies and ensure victory. The scholars of our age fail to weigh relative importance and glibly speak of transformation through virtue. Clinging to restrictive doctrines, they forget to plan for the proper conduct of affairs. Understanding this but remaining blind to that, grasping one factor while neglecting the other two—how could they be fit to participate in directing the armies?
Nevertheless, though all three factors are important, harmony among people is essential. Thus it is said: “Relying on timing is inferior to relying on methods; relying on methods is inferior to relying on people.” Those who disregard people and speak only of Heaven are removing their fences and awaiting invaders; scarcely can they avoid becoming an instance of Mo Di’s defense [?]. Those who occupy defensible terrain but abandon planning rely arrogantly on their commanding position; scarcely can they avoid the plight of the traveler whose lodging burns. Therefore, men who seize opportunities and determine victory anxiously strive to exhaust the possibilities of human planning in order to accord with Heaven’s mind, and cultivate virtuous government to strengthen their strategic position. Their deliberations are comprehensive, their defenses meticulous, and their movements cautious. They display favor and majesty, make rewards and punishments clear, and win people’s allegiance through perfect impartiality; they exercise care in issuing commands and demand…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
功實以嚴明而濟其用審主客計虛實以
全力而制其敝而又倡之勇敢以作其氣
齊之禮義以示其方節之坐作進退以習
其法熟之金鼓旗物以便其趨而使兵識
將意將識士情庶幾以攻則取以守則固
雖使之蹈水火赴鼎鑊無不可者豈不足
爲王室屏翰公侯腹心矣乎故國之强弱
不在於兵而在於將昔荀卿氏曰上不隆
禮則兵弱下不愛民則兵弱已諾不信則
===
兵弱賞罰不漸則兵弱此非言積弱之有
由乎隨武子曰夫兵觀釁而動視竭而進
德刑政事典禮不易不可敵也此非言致
强之有本乎蓋紀綱旣振威令自中强之
道也法弛而媮卒驕而惰弱之道也夫由
荀卿之言而反其所以弱由武子之言而
求其所以强則人謀旣盡而握機決勝之
道在我外此而支干遁甲之占谿山關隘
之守抑其次矣謹對
punctuated:
功實，以嚴明而濟其用；審主客，計虛實，以全力而制其敝。而又倡之勇敢，以作其氣；齊之禮義，以示其方；節之坐作進退，以習其法；熟之金鼓旗物，以便其趨。而使兵識將意，將識士情，庶幾以攻則取，以守則固。雖使之蹈水火、赴鼎鑊，無不可者，豈不足爲王室屏翰、公侯腹心矣乎？故國之强弱，不在於兵，而在於將。昔荀卿氏曰：「上不隆禮則兵弱，下不愛民則兵弱，已諾不信則兵弱，賞罰不漸則兵弱。」此非言積弱之有由乎？
隨武子曰：「夫兵，觀釁而動，視竭而進。德刑政事典禮不易，不可敵也。」此非言致强之有本乎？蓋紀綱旣振，威令自中，强之道也；法弛而媮，卒驕而惰，弱之道也。夫由荀卿之言而反其所以弱，由武子之言而求其所以强，則人謀旣盡，而握機決勝之道在我。外此，而支干遁甲之占、谿山關隘之守，抑其次矣。謹對。
translation_en:
…actual achievements, making their service effective through strictness and clarity; assess the positions of host and invading forces, weigh weaknesses and strengths, and employ one's full strength to exploit the enemy's vulnerabilities. Moreover, inspire them with courage to rouse their spirits; order them through ritual propriety and righteousness to show them the proper course; regulate their sitting, rising, advancing, and retreating to train them in military methods; and familiarize them with gongs, drums, flags, and standards so that they can readily respond. Let the soldiers understand their commanders' intentions and the commanders understand their men's feelings. Then one may hope that their attacks will succeed and their defenses hold firm. Even if ordered to tread through water and fire or face the boiling cauldrons of execution, they would shrink from nothing. Would they not suffice as bulwarks of the royal house and trusted servants of dukes and marquises? Thus a state's strength or weakness lies not in its soldiers but in its commanders. Xun Qing once said: “If those above do not exalt ritual propriety, the army will be weak; if they do not cherish the people below, the army will be weak; if promises already made are not kept, the army will be weak; if rewards and punishments are not properly graduated [?], the army will be weak.” Does this not explain that accumulated weakness has its causes?
Sui Wuzi said: “In warfare, move when you perceive an opening, and advance when you see exhaustion. When virtue, punishments, governmental affairs, and established rites remain intact, the enemy cannot be opposed.” Does this not explain that attaining strength has its foundations? Once discipline and order are invigorated, authoritative commands will naturally be fitting [?]: this is the way to strength. When laws grow lax and are treated carelessly, and soldiers become arrogant and indolent, this is the way to weakness. If, following Xun Qing's words, we reverse the causes of weakness, and, following Wuzi's words, seek the sources of strength, then human planning will have been fully exercised, and the means of seizing opportunities and securing victory will lie in our own hands. Beyond this, divination by the earthly branches and heavenly stems and by the dunjia arts, and defense through streams, mountains, passes, and defiles, are of secondary importance. I respectfully submit this reply.

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄後序
嘉靖甲子秋當
京省鄉試士先是憲臣以重選
舉爲請首先慎簡試官及以
在京部寺等官分任試事事
下禮部禮部酌議以
上
===
上允之屆期乃
命左諭德臣鏜主試事臣國珍等猥
以職事充同考之任臣惟選
舉之典重矣躬逢
新命濫與校閱不亦榮乎顧茲重
典臣盼焉以淺陋當之又惴
惴焉唯辱
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄後序

嘉靖甲子秋，當京省鄉試士。先是，憲臣以重選舉爲請，首先慎簡試官，及以在京部寺等官分任試事。事下禮部，禮部酌議以上，上允之。屆期，乃命左諭德臣鏜主試事，臣國珍等猥以職事充同考之任。臣惟選舉之典重矣，躬逢新命，濫與校閱，不亦榮乎？顧茲重典，臣盼焉，以淺陋當之，又惴惴焉，唯辱
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the jiazi year of Jiajing (1564), it was time to examine candidates in the capitals and provinces in the Provincial Examination. Before this, the censorial officials had petitioned that due weight be given to the selection of men for office: first, examination officials should be carefully chosen, and officials from the ministries, courts, and other offices in the capital should share responsibility for examination duties. The matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites, which deliberated and submitted its recommendations to the throne. His Majesty approved them.

When the appointed time arrived, His Majesty commanded your servant Tang 鏜, Left Admonisher, to preside over the examination. Your servant Guozhen 國珍 and others were undeservedly assigned, by virtue of our official duties, to serve as Associate Examiners. I reflected that the institution of selecting men for office is a weighty one. Personally to receive this new appointment and, unworthily, to participate in evaluating the papers—was this not an honor? Yet, contemplating this weighty institution, I looked upon it [?], undertaking the responsibility with my shallow learning and limited understanding, and trembled with apprehension, fearing only that I might disgrace…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
任使是懼夫榮且懼必將竭愚
忠以效報稱則所以懋茲其
職者固非倍萬於常時不已
也既竣事成錄以
獻臣復當承乏序諸末簡謹拜
手稽首颺言曰臣唯我
明取士之法取諸周若鄉試則
===
周大比賓興之遺也或乃謂
古以德藝而賓興賢能今徒
以其文宜若有未盡者不知
時代雖殊降才不異顧所尚
何如耳尚德藝則士以德藝
見尚文辭則士以文辭見故
今時所取士有文辭而無德
punctuated: 任使是懼。夫榮且懼，必將竭愚忠以效報稱，則所以懋茲其職者，固非倍萬於常時不已也。既竣事，成錄以獻，臣復當承乏，序諸末簡，謹拜手稽首，颺言曰：臣唯我明取士之法，取諸周。若鄉試，則周大比賓興之遺也。或乃謂古以德藝而賓興賢能，今徒以其文，宜若有未盡者。不知時代雖殊，降才不異，顧所尚何如耳。尚德藝，則士以德藝見；尚文辭，則士以文辭見。故今時所取士，有文辭而無德
translation_en: …the commission entrusted to me is what I fear failing. Feeling both honored and apprehensive, I must exhaust my humble loyalty to render service commensurate with this trust. In diligently fulfilling this office, I cannot rest without exerting myself ten thousand times more than ordinarily. Once the work was completed and the record compiled for presentation to the throne, I was again called upon, for want of someone more capable, to write an afterword on its final leaves. Reverently bowing with my hands joined and my forehead to the ground, I proclaim: I submit that our Ming dynasty’s method of selecting scholars derives from the Zhou. The Provincial Examination preserves the legacy of the Zhou’s triennial assessment, when the worthy and able were honored as guests and recommended for office. Some contend that in antiquity the worthy and able were thus honored and recommended on the basis of virtue and accomplishments, whereas today selection depends solely on their writing, so that something seems to be lacking. They do not understand that although the ages differ, Heaven’s bestowal of talent is unchanged; it depends only on what is esteemed. When virtue and accomplishments are esteemed, scholars distinguish themselves through virtue and accomplishments; when literary expression is esteemed, scholars distinguish themselves through literary expression. Thus, among the scholars selected today, there are those who possess literary skill but lack virtue…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
藝者有之求其德藝兼修以
翊贊
國家彪炳之化則夫有外文辭
而得之者矧
天地元精
帝王神化其涵育啟流固靡所壅
閼若
===
畿甸之士得之尤先且厚故文
王思皇之楨取諸王國而萬
邦以孚其機固有然者耳乃
皇祖根本之地晉以洪武甲子頒
應天我
今科舉條格遵行三閱甲子
矣我
punctuated:
藝者有之。求其德藝兼修，以翊贊國家彪炳之化，則夫有外文辭而得之者？矧天地元精、帝王神化，其涵育啟流，固靡所壅閼。若畿甸之士，得之尤先且厚。故文王思皇之楨，取諸王國，而萬邦以孚，其機固有然者耳。
乃皇祖根本之地，晉以洪武甲子頒應天我今科舉條格，遵行三閱甲子矣。我
translation_en:
…There are indeed those who possess literary skill but lack virtue and cultivated accomplishments. Yet if we seek men who cultivate both virtue and accomplishments, to assist in the state's brilliant transforming influence, can they be found apart from literary expression? [?] Moreover, the primal essence of Heaven and Earth and the wondrous transforming influence of emperors nurture and enlighten without obstruction. Scholars of the metropolitan region receive these benefits especially early and abundantly. Thus King Wen's splendid pillars of support were drawn from the royal domain, and the myriad states consequently placed their trust in him: there was assuredly a reason why this was so.
Now, this is the ancestral emperor's foundational territory. In the jiazi year of Hongwu [1384], the regulations for the civil-service examinations were promulgated for Yingtian [?]; their observance has continued through three sixty-year cycles. [The wording linking the territory, promulgation, and Yingtian is garbled.] I…

title: 嘉靖四十三年應天府鄉試錄
text:
負於
明時庶幾以對揚
聖天子之
寵命
南京吏部文選清吏司郎中
蔡〔國珍〕謹序
punctuated:
負於明時，庶幾以對揚聖天子之寵命。

南京吏部文選清吏司郎中蔡〔國珍〕謹序。
translation_en:
…fail this enlightened age, hoping thereby to requite and extol the gracious command of the sagely Son of Heaven.

Preface respectfully written by Cai Guozhen 蔡國珍, Director of the Bureau of Appointments in the Ministry of Personnel at Nanjing.
